          "text": "Integrations will consume more time than you expect"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is a classic problem."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The architecture might say:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "`connect CRM`"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But then you need:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "OAuth, scopes, refreshing credentials, webhooks, pagination, schema mapping, rate limits, failures, deleted records, permissions and provider-specific semantics."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Then repeat for:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "HubSpot, Google Analytics, Search Console, Slack, Drive, Notion, ad platforms, CMS, social platforms, call transcripts, etc."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is why I would **not support 20 integrations initially**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Three good integrations are considerably more valuable than fifteen unreliable ones."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "I would also remove the “computer” from the critical path initially"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "You don't actually need a persistent virtual computer for every client to make V1 useful."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Start with:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**Postgres + object storage + agent runtime + external APIs.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Add sandbox/computer execution when an agent genuinely needs:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "file transformations, browser work, code execution, scraping/research tooling or heavyweight artifact creation."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Current platforms already make on-demand sandbox execution practical; Cloudflare, for example, separates durable agent state from Sandbox files/processes and recommends durable workflows for long-running work. citeturn606842search13turn606842search35"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That lets the computer become an **execution tool**, rather than another infrastructure problem you have to solve immediately."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "What a solo founder can realistically build"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "If you're reasonably capable technically and are using coding agents aggressively, I would think about the project in three stages."
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 3,
          "text": "First convincing prototype: ~4–8 weeks"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "You could have:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "one company, basic Brand Core, website/PDF ingestion, several canonical entities, Research/Strategy/Story agents, working feed, comments/reactions, basic avatar state animations, and manually configured client knowledge."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That could look extremely impressive."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "It will **not** yet be robust."
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 3,
          "text": "First genuinely paid deployment: ~3–5 months"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "You'd need to add:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "proper tenant separation, onboarding, provenance, knowledge editing, context compilation, permissions, agent tracing, failure handling, a few real integrations, human approvals, usage/cost tracking and enough polish that you aren't fixing things constantly."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "At this stage I think you can legitimately sell the product."
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 3,
          "text": "Repeatable managed platform: ~6–12 months"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The goal here is:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "client #10 takes dramatically less effort than client #1."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "You need reusable onboarding, standardized schema, integration adapters, agent configuration, evaluation, versioning, admin tooling and monitoring."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is where it stops being a bespoke AI project."
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 3,
          "text": "Entire mature vision: ~18–36 months solo"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Meaning:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "rich living brand model, customer/market intelligence, many integrations, highly reliable multi-agent workflows, execution, learning, attribution, beautiful avatar system, sophisticated feed, mobile experience, granular permissions, auditability, strong evaluations and high autonomy."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That is a **real software company**, not a side project."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "A small excellent team could compress that substantially, but I would still think in terms of many months rather than weeks."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Those timelines are estimates, not guarantees; they depend heavily on your engineering experience and how aggressively you constrain scope."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "The biggest mistake would be trying to build the vision horizontally"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "You could easily spend a year building:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "“the ultimate Marketing OS”"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "without having a customer."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That would be a mistake."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The architecture should be broad."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**The first deployed product should be narrow.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For example, your first version might really only do:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**Brand Core**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "→ **continuous market/customer research**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "→ **positioning/narrative recommendations**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "→ **feed interaction**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "→ **campaign briefing**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That is already useful."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "And importantly, it demonstrates the unique thing:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**multiple intelligent actors drawing from one persistent representation of the brand.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "You don't need autonomous ad buying to prove the thesis."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "What I would build myself vs buy"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is perhaps the most consequential architecture decision."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I would **own**:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**canonical company/brand model**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**knowledge API**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**context compiler**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**feed/event semantics**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**feedback/decision model**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**agent personas/roles**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**UX and avatar language**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**client configuration model**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Those are your product."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I would **not build from scratch**:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "LLM infrastructure, generic agent loops, vector database primitives, sandbox runtime, authentication, file storage, model hosting, workflow checkpointing or animation rendering."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Current products already provide most of those lower layers. citeturn606842search22turn606842search3turn606842search19"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Where I think the project genuinely contains technical novelty"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Not in multi-agent orchestration."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Not in avatars."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Not in RAG."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The interesting technical/product problem is:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**How do you create and continuously maintain a structured, temporally aware, source-grounded representation of a brand/company that heterogeneous agents can reliably reason over?**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "And then:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**How do human interactions and real-world marketing results safely modify that representation over time?**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "If you solve those two problems well, almost everything else becomes modular."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Models can change."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Agents can change."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Video providers can change."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "CRMs can change."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The Brand Core remains."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Final assessment"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I would **not be scared away by the engineering difficulty**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Nothing in the vision requires a scientific breakthrough. The underlying agent infrastructure is mature enough that tool use, structured outputs, handoffs, persistence, durable workflows and sandboxed execution can be assembled from existing components. citeturn606842search0turn606842search23turn606842search27"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But I would be very careful about believing:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "“I can build the whole thing in three months because AI can code.”"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "You can probably build **20–30% of the vision in three months**, and that 20–30% could already be commercially valuable."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The full vision is closer to an **8–9/10 software-product challenge**, mostly because you're combining a knowledge system, agent platform, marketing application, integration platform, learning system and unusually polished interaction design."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The good news is that you **don't need the full vision for the business to work**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I would aim for the smallest system that proves this proposition:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**Give us your fragmented company knowledge. We turn it into a living Brand Core. Specialized agents continuously work from that same understanding, bring important insights and recommendations into a feed, and learn from your decisions.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "If *that* produces enough value that a company pays several thousand euros per month, then every additional layer we've discussed becomes an expansion rather than a prerequisite."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That is how I would approach building the entire vision as a solopreneur. memcite"
        }
      ],
      "artifact_refs": []

      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "In simple terms:\n\nYou are building **one central “brain” for a brand**, then letting different AI agents use that brain to do different jobs.\n\nThe hard part is not making the agents. The hard part is making the brain accurate, organized, and reliable.\n\nThe system needs to do four things:\n\n- collect everything about the company: brand, customers, products, competitors, past campaigns, research\n- organize it into a shared structure so every agent understands it the same way\n- let specialized agents use that shared knowledge to research, strategize, create, and recommend actions\n- let the user react, comment, approve, or correct things so the system improves over time\n\nThe feed UI and the little animated agents are relatively easy compared with the knowledge system behind them.\n\nThe biggest technical challenges are:\n\n- deciding what the system should believe when documents contradict each other\n- giving each agent only the right context for its task\n- safely learning from user feedback\n- connecting reliably to tools like HubSpot, analytics, Slack, CMSs, etc.\n- making the system dependable enough that clients trust it\n\nYou do **not** need to build the entire vision at once.\n\nA strong first version could simply be:\n\n**Brand Core → Research Agent → Strategy Agent → Storytelling Agent → Feed → human feedback**\n\nSo a client gives you their company material, you build their Brand Core, and the agents continuously post useful things into the feed:\n\n> “Competitor X changed positioning.”\n\n> “Customers are mentioning this problem more often.”\n\n> “I think this is a positioning opportunity.”\n\n> “Here are three narratives based on that.”\n\nThen the client likes, comments, corrects, or approves.\n\nThat alone could already be valuable.\n\nThe full vision is difficult, but **a useful paid first version is very achievable**. The smart approach is to build the core brain first, then add more agents and integrations over time. memcite",

    {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "Yes — **but only for a specific layer of our architecture**.\n\nAfter reading the repository architecture, session model, subagent system, MCP bridge, SDK, tool pipeline, approval system, persistence model, and context assembly, my conclusion is:\n\n> **DeepSeek Harness is unusually well aligned with the agent-runtime part of our system.**\n>\n> **It is not the Brand Core / “box,” and I would not let it become the architecture of the whole product.**\n\nI also **would not make the business production-dependent on it yet**, because DeepSeek explicitly labels it a developer preview and warns that compatibility-breaking changes will happen. fileciteturn3file0L2-L2\n\n### Where it fits\n\nOur architecture can be separated like this:\n\n| Our layer | DeepSeek Harness fit | Recommendation |\n|---|---:|---|\n| Brand/Core world model | 2/10 | **Build ourselves** |\n| Ontology + provenance | 1/10 | **Build ourselves** |\n| Knowledge retrieval/context compiler | 5/10 | Our system feeding Harness |\n| Individual agent runtime | **9/10** | Harness is very interesting |\n| Agent personas + scoped capabilities | **9/10** | Harness |\n| Multi-agent delegation | **9/10** | Harness can do this |\n| Tool execution | **9/10** | Harness |\n| MCP connections | **9/10** | Harness |\n| Human approval | **8/10** | Useful, but needs adaptation |\n| Agent session persistence | **9/10** | Harness |\n| Audit/replay | **10/10** | Harness is excellent here |\n| Feed/product semantics | 4/10 | **Build ourselves** |\n| Avatar state system | 4/10 | Build on Harness events |\n| Multi-tenant client management | 3/10 | **Build ourselves** |\n| Marketing logic | 1/10 | **Build ourselves** |\n\nSo I would place it here:\n\n```text\n                 OUR PRODUCT\n\n              BRAND CORE / \"BOX\"\n                     │\n          ontology + knowledge\n                     │\n              Context Compiler\n                     │\n                     ▼\n        ┌────────────────────────┐\n        │   DEEPSEEK HARNESS     │\n        │                        │\n        │ agent runtime          │\n        │ sessions               │\n        │ tools                  │\n        │ MCP                    │\n        │ subagents              │\n        │ approvals              │\n        │ persistence            │\n        └───────────┬────────────┘\n                    │\n          APIs / MCP / Computer\n                    │\n                    ▼\n               REAL WORLD\n\n       ↑ events / findings / actions ↑\n\n               OUR FEED UI\n```\n\nThat separation is important.\n\n## Why Harness is unusually relevant to us\n\nThe strongest architectural idea in the repo is:\n\n> **everything is a plugin.**\n\nModels, tools, sessions, the agent loop, sandbox, persistence and other capabilities are replaceable components mounted into a shared Cordis context. fileciteturn4file0L2-L2\n\nThat's highly compatible with our concept.\n\nWe want the Researcher to have:\n\n`web + research databases + Brand Core read`\n\nwhile the Strategist gets:\n\n`Brand Core + customer intelligence + positioning tools`\n\nand perhaps the Creative Agent gets:\n\n`Brand Core + asset system + Higgsfield MCP`.\n\nHarness already has **agent-scoped registrations and tool restrictions**. Subagents can have separate personas, tool filters and depth limits. fileciteturn6file0L2-L2\n\nThat's almost exactly the low-level machinery we'd otherwise have to build.\n\n---\n\n## The session/event architecture is particularly valuable\n\nThis may be the most useful part for our feed idea.\n\nHarness treats an agent session as an **append-only typed event log**. The LLM conversation is derived from that event history rather than being the primary source of truth. fileciteturn9file0L2-L2\n\nEvents include things such as:\n\n`turn/start`\n\n`step/start`\n\n`user/message`\n\n`assistant/message`\n\n`tool/call`\n\n`tool/result`\n\netc.\n\nAnd the event vocabulary is extensible by plugins. fileciteturn9file0L2-L2\n\nThis aligns beautifully with the feed.\n\nSuppose Researcher runs:\n\n```text\nResearcher starts\n       ↓\nweb search\n       ↓\nreads 15 sources\n       ↓\nfinds competitor change\n       ↓\ncreates hypothesis\n       ↓\nposts insight\n```\n\nHarness can give us the **execution events**.\n\nOur product translates those into **domain events**:\n\n```text\nResearchStarted\nSourcesAnalyzed\nCompetitorChangeDetected\nInsightCreated\nRecommendationCreated\n```\n\nAnd then our frontend displays:\n\n**🔵 Researcher**\n\n> I found something interesting.\n\ninstead of exposing raw agent logs.\n\nThat's a strong architecture.\n\n---\n\n# It also fits the avatar system\n\nHarness agents expose lifecycle events and statuses, although the built-in public status is basically only `idle` or `running`. fileciteturn18file0L2-L2\n\nSo Harness won't magically give us:\n\n> Researcher is scanning.\n\n> Strategist is synthesizing.\n\n> Storyteller is weaving.\n\nWe would add those semantics ourselves.\n\nBut Harness gives us plenty of signals:\n\n```text\nagent running\ntool called\ntool completed\nmodel request\nsubagent started\napproval requested\nturn completed\n```\n\nThen our presentation layer maps them into avatar states:\n\n```text\nweb.search\n→ Researcher = SCANNING\n\nknowledge.get_related()\n→ Researcher = CONNECTING\n\nmodel reasoning\n→ Researcher = THINKING\n\ninsight.create()\n→ Researcher = PRESENTING\n```\n\nThat is probably a **better architecture than having the LLM control animation directly**.\n\nThe animation remains deterministic and meaningful.\n\n---\n\n# MCP support is very useful for us\n\nHarness already has a proper MCP-client plugin.\n\nAn MCP server's tools become normal agent tools, namespaced by server. It supports stdio and Streamable HTTP, reconnect logic, dynamic tool discovery, timeout handling and tool-list updates. fileciteturn8file0L2-L2\n\nThat means something such as:\n\n```text\nHiggsfield MCP\nSemrush MCP\nHubSpot MCP\nBrowser MCP\ncustom Brand Core MCP\n```\n\ncan potentially enter the same tool system.\n\nThat saves us from writing a lot of generic integration plumbing.\n\n---\n\n# The tool architecture is also excellent for a managed system\n\nHarness doesn't merely expose `tool()`.\n\nIts tool pipeline supports:\n\n- typed inputs\n- typed outputs\n- execution policies\n- cancellation\n- parallel/exclusive execution\n- scoped restrictions\n- pre/post execution interception\n- UI presentation metadata\n\nfileciteturn10file0L2-L2\n\nThat matters because our system eventually needs:\n\n> Growth Agent can **read** Meta Ads.\n\nbut:\n\n> Growth Agent cannot **change a €20k budget without approval**.\n\nThe distinction between capabilities and permissions needs to be structural rather than prompt-based.\n\nHarness is already designed around that idea.\n\n---\n\n# Human approvals are also built in\n\nHarness has an explicit approval system.\n\nActions can ask:\n\n> may this particular action proceed?\n\nThe outcome is recorded, auditable, and fail-closed. fileciteturn21file0L2-L2\n\nThat fits our feed very naturally.\n\nFor example:\n\n**🟢 Growth Agent**\n\n> I recommend increasing spend on Campaign B from €500/day to €650/day.\n\n**Approve** · **Reject** · **Discuss**\n\nOur UI could become the approval answerer.\n\nThat's exactly the kind of agent infrastructure we'd otherwise have to design ourselves.\n\n---\n\n# Multi-agent support is significantly more sophisticated than we need initially\n\nThis repo isn't doing simplistic:\n\n> Agent A sends string to Agent B.\n\nIt has persistent child sessions, continuation, parent/child authorization, interruption, tool restrictions, personas, durable lineage and multiple subagent providers—including in-process agents and adapters for things such as Codex and Claude Code. fileciteturn6file0L2-L2\n\nTechnically, that's impressive.\n\nBut I would **not use all of it**.\n\nWe've already reached a good architectural conclusion for our product:\n\n> Agents should not just freely chat with each other.\n\nThe Marketing Director / orchestration logic should decide what work happens.\n\nSo I would use Harness subagents primarily as an **execution primitive**, not let its delegation model dictate our business logic.\n\n---\n\n# What Harness absolutely does NOT solve\n\nThis is the most important part.\n\nHarness doesn't give us:\n\n> **the box.**\n\nOur hardest and most important system remains:\n\n```text\nBrand\n│\n├── Identity\n├── Products\n├── Audiences\n│   ├── motivations\n│   ├── pains\n│   ├── objections\n│   └── language\n├── Positioning\n├── Narratives\n├── Competitors\n├── Claims\n│   └── evidence\n├── Campaigns\n├── Decisions\n└── Performance\n```\n\nwith:\n\n**relationships + provenance + confidence + temporal state + approval status.**\n\nHarness's session system is **agent history**.\n\nOur Brand Core is **company reality**.\n\nThose should remain separate.\n\nThat's crucial.\n\n---\n\n# I would integrate them through a Brand Core plugin\n\nConceptually:\n\n```text\nDeepSeek Harness\n       │\n       ▼\nBrandCorePlugin\n       │\n       ├── knowledge.get_entity()\n       ├── knowledge.search()\n       ├── knowledge.get_related()\n       ├── knowledge.get_evidence()\n       ├── knowledge.get_history()\n       ├── knowledge.propose_update()\n       └── knowledge.record_decision()\n       │\n       ▼\nOUR BRAND CORE DATABASE\n```\n\nThen Harness doesn't own the brand.\n\nIt knows how to **access the brand**.\n\nThat's exactly where I want the boundary.\n\n---\n\n# The Context Compiler could also integrate nicely\n\nHarness's system-prompt subsystem supports scoped, dynamic context contributions evaluated when requests are assembled. fileciteturn19file0L2-L2\n\nThat means our Context Compiler could say:\n\n> Researcher is investigating competitor positioning.\n\nand dynamically provide:\n\n```text\nCurrent positioning\nRelevant competitors\nPrimary ICP\nRecent market observations\nApproved brand assumptions\n```\n\nwhile the Storyteller receives a completely different context package.\n\nSo Harness could serve as the **consumer of our Context Compiler**.\n\nAgain:\n\n> Harness runs intelligence.\n\n> We decide what intelligence knows.\n\n---\n\n# There's a significant problem today: maturity\n\nThis is where I would be cautious.\n\nThe repo was only publicly created on **August 13, 2026**, two days before this conversation, according to GitHub metadata. fileciteturn1file0L2-L2\n\nAnd the README explicitly states:\n\n> developer preview\n\nand warns that there will be **compatibility-breaking changes**. fileciteturn3file0L2-L2\n\nFor experimenting?\n\nFine.\n\nFor:\n\n> “Five German clients pay me €5k/month and their marketing infrastructure depends on this”?\n\nI wouldn't trust that dependency yet.\n\nNot because the architecture looks poor—it actually looks unusually thoughtful.\n\nBecause its API surface is explicitly unstable.\n\n---\n\n# There is another weakness for our custom frontend\n\nHarness has a TypeScript SDK capable of driving a runtime through JSON-RPC, subscribing to events and maintaining sessions. That's promising for connecting our custom feed frontend/backend to Harness. fileciteturn15file0L2-L2\n\nHowever, the SDK currently documents some important limitations:\n\n- no mid-turn cancellation;\n- no per-prompt result/cancellation primitive;\n- client→server notifications are not implemented;\n- server→client requests are not implemented;\n- it explicitly notes that those missing channels are relevant to future approval flows.\n\nfileciteturn15file0L2-L2\n\nThat matters for us.\n\nOur UI is highly interactive:\n\n> agent proposes action → feed asks approval → user comments → agent adjusts → work continues.\n\nSo we'd likely need either:\n\n**a custom Harness plugin/server bridge**\n\nor improvements upstream before the SDK perfectly fits our interface.\n\nThat is solvable, but it's not zero work.\n\n---\n\n# Another concern: Cordis\n\nHarness isn't a tiny library.\n\nYou have to learn Cordis's model:\n\n> contexts → services → plugins → typed events → waterfalls → reversible effects.\n\nfileciteturn22file0L2-L2\n\nArchitecturally, I like it.\n\nAs a solo founder, however, it introduces **another conceptual framework you have to own**.\n\nThat's a real cost.\n\nWith something simple like:\n\n`Vercel AI SDK + Postgres + custom orchestration`\n\nyou understand virtually every piece yourself.\n\nWith Harness, you're buying substantial power but also adopting DeepSeek's application architecture.\n\nSo it only makes sense if we actually use enough of that power.\n\nFor our full vision, I think we probably would.\n\nFor a three-agent MVP, maybe not.\n\n---\n\n# My current recommendation\n\nI would **not make DeepSeek Harness the foundation of V1 yet**.\n\nBut I would absolutely investigate it as the likely **Agent Runtime layer**.\n\nSpecifically, I'd design our own architecture like:\n\n```text\ninterface AgentRuntime {\n    createAgent()\n    run()\n    interrupt()\n    send()\n    subscribe()\n    registerTools()\n    resume()\n}\n```\n\nThen:\n\n```text\nDeepSeekHarnessRuntime implements AgentRuntime\n```\n\nOur product never depends directly on DSH everywhere.\n\nThat gives us:\n\n```text\n                    OUR SYSTEM\n\n Brand Core ─────────────────────── permanent\n Context Compiler ───────────────── permanent\n Feed/Event Model ───────────────── permanent\n Marketing Domain Logic ─────────── permanent\n Client Configuration ───────────── permanent\n\n                AgentRuntime\n                     │\n                     ▼\n            DeepSeek Harness\n                replaceable\n```\n\nThat is the architecture I'd choose.\n\n---\n\n## And I would run one very specific experiment\n\nBefore deciding, build only:\n\n**Researcher Agent**\n\nusing Harness.\n\nConnect:\n\n`Brand Core mock → Researcher → web/MCP → insight → event → feed post`\n\nand test these capabilities:\n\n| Test | Why it matters |\n|---|---|\n| Inject Brand Core context | proves Context Compiler integration |\n| Give Researcher restricted tools | proves role isolation |\n| Use MCP | proves external tool strategy |\n| Persist/resume agent | proves background continuity |\n| Stream events to our feed | proves UI architecture |\n| Map execution → avatar states | proves interaction concept |\n| Human approval from our UI | exposes the biggest integration gap |\n| Restart runtime and resume | proves durability |\n| Run two isolated client instances | tests managed-service architecture |\n\nIf Harness performs well there, **I would seriously consider adopting it**.\n\nIf approval/custom-UI integration or Cordis becomes painful, we can abandon it without touching the Brand Core.\n\n---\n\n# Bottom line\n\nDeepSeek Harness could remove a **large amount of generic agent-runtime engineering** from the project.\n\nIt already solves difficult problems we would otherwise eventually encounter:\n\n**agent lifecycle**\n\n**session durability**\n\n**replay**\n\n**tool execution**\n\n**permissions**\n\n**approvals**\n\n**MCP**\n\n**model adapters**\n\n**subagents**\n\n**cancellation**\n\n**scoped capabilities**\n\n**plugin lifecycle**\n\nThose are substantial.\n\nBut it does **not solve the hardest product-specific problem**:\n\n> **building and maintaining the structured shared world representation of the brand, and deciding how real-world evidence and human feedback change that representation.**\n\nThat remains ours.\n\nSo my revised architecture would be:\n\n> **Brand Core = our moat.**\n>\n> **Feed/avatars = our product experience.**\n>\n> **Marketing intelligence logic = our domain IP.**\n>\n> **DeepSeek Harness = potentially the engine room underneath the agents.**\n\nI think that is a genuinely strong fit.\n\n**Today I would rate Harness ~8/10 architecturally for our agent-runtime needs, but only ~5/10 as a production dependency because it is explicitly brand-new developer-preview software.**\n\nIf it stabilizes, it could save us from building a surprisingly large amount of infrastructure that has little to do with what actually differentiates our product. memcite",
      "blocks": [

          "text": "Yes — **but only for a specific layer of our architecture**."

          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "After reading the repository architecture, session model, subagent system, MCP bridge, SDK, tool pipeline, approval system, persistence model, and context assembly, my conclusion is:"

          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I also **would not make the business production-dependent on it yet**, because DeepSeek explicitly labels it a developer preview and warns that compatibility-breaking changes will happen. fileciteturn3file0L2-L2"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",

          "text": "Where it fits"

          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So I would place it here:"

        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "                 OUR PRODUCT\n\n              BRAND CORE / \"BOX\"\n                     │\n          ontology + knowledge\n                     │\n              Context Compiler\n                     │\n                     ▼\n        ┌────────────────────────┐\n        │   DEEPSEEK HARNESS     │\n        │                        │\n        │ agent runtime          │\n        │ sessions               │\n        │ tools                  │\n        │ MCP                    │\n        │ subagents              │\n        │ approvals              │\n        │ persistence            │\n        └───────────┬────────────┘\n                    │\n          APIs / MCP / Computer\n                    │\n                    ▼\n               REAL WORLD\n\n       ↑ events / findings / actions ↑\n\n               OUR FEED UI"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",

          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Conceptually:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "DeepSeek Harness\n       │\n       ▼\nBrandCorePlugin\n       │\n       ├── knowledge.get_entity()\n       ├── knowledge.search()\n       ├── knowledge.get_related()\n       ├── knowledge.get_evidence()\n       ├── knowledge.get_history()\n       ├── knowledge.propose_update()\n       └── knowledge.record_decision()\n       │\n       ▼\nOUR BRAND CORE DATABASE"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Then Harness doesn't own the brand."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "It knows how to **access the brand**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's exactly where I want the boundary."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "The Context Compiler could also integrate nicely"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Harness's system-prompt subsystem supports scoped, dynamic context contributions evaluated when requests are assembled. fileciteturn19file0L2-L2"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That means our Context Compiler could say:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "Researcher is investigating competitor positioning."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "and dynamically provide:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Current positioning\nRelevant competitors\nPrimary ICP\nRecent market observations\nApproved brand assumptions"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "while the Storyteller receives a completely different context package."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So Harness could serve as the **consumer of our Context Compiler**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Again:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "Harness runs intelligence."
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "We decide what intelligence knows."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "There's a significant problem today: maturity"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is where I would be cautious."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The repo was only publicly created on **August 13, 2026**, two days before this conversation, according to GitHub metadata. fileciteturn1file0L2-L2"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "And the README explicitly states:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "developer preview"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "and warns that there will be **compatibility-breaking changes**. fileciteturn3file0L2-L2"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For experimenting?"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Fine."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "“Five German clients pay me €5k/month and their marketing infrastructure depends on this”?"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I wouldn't trust that dependency yet."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Not because the architecture looks poor—it actually looks unusually thoughtful."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Because its API surface is explicitly unstable."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "There is another weakness for our custom frontend"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Harness has a TypeScript SDK capable of driving a runtime through JSON-RPC, subscribing to events and maintaining sessions. That's promising for connecting our custom feed frontend/backend to Harness. fileciteturn15file0L2-L2"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "However, the SDK currently documents some important limitations:"
        },
        {
          "type": "list",
          "ordered": false,
          "items": [
            "no mid-turn cancellation;",
            "no per-prompt result/cancellation primitive;",
            "client→server notifications are not implemented;",
            "server→client requests are not implemented;",
            "it explicitly notes that those missing channels are relevant to future approval flows."
          ]
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "fileciteturn15file0L2-L2"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That matters for us."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Our UI is highly interactive:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "agent proposes action → feed asks approval → user comments → agent adjusts → work continues."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So we'd likely need either:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**a custom Harness plugin/server bridge**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "or improvements upstream before the SDK perfectly fits our interface."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That is solvable, but it's not zero work."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Another concern: Cordis"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Harness isn't a tiny library."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "You have to learn Cordis's model:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "contexts → services → plugins → typed events → waterfalls → reversible effects."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "fileciteturn22file0L2-L2"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Architecturally, I like it."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "As a solo founder, however, it introduces **another conceptual framework you have to own**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's a real cost."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "With something simple like:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "`Vercel AI SDK + Postgres + custom orchestration`"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "you understand virtually every piece yourself."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "With Harness, you're buying substantial power but also adopting DeepSeek's application architecture."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So it only makes sense if we actually use enough of that power."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For our full vision, I think we probably would."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For a three-agent MVP, maybe not."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "My current recommendation"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I would **not make DeepSeek Harness the foundation of V1 yet**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But I would absolutely investigate it as the likely **Agent Runtime layer**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Specifically, I'd design our own architecture like:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "interface AgentRuntime {\n    createAgent()\n    run()\n    interrupt()\n    send()\n    subscribe()\n    registerTools()\n    resume()\n}"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Then:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "DeepSeekHarnessRuntime implements AgentRuntime"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Our product never depends directly on DSH everywhere."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That gives us:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "                    OUR SYSTEM\n\n Brand Core ─────────────────────── permanent\n Context Compiler ───────────────── permanent\n Feed/Event Model ───────────────── permanent\n Marketing Domain Logic ─────────── permanent\n Client Configuration ───────────── permanent\n\n                AgentRuntime\n                     │\n                     ▼\n            DeepSeek Harness\n                replaceable"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That is the architecture I'd choose."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 2,
          "text": "And I would run one very specific experiment"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Before deciding, build only:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**Researcher Agent**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "using Harness."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Connect:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "`Brand Core mock → Researcher → web/MCP → insight → event → feed post`"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "and test these capabilities:"
        },
        {
          "type": "table",
          "header": [
            "Test",
            "Why it matters"
          ],
          "rows": [
            [
              "Inject Brand Core context",
              "proves Context Compiler integration"
            ],
            [
              "Give Researcher restricted tools",
              "proves role isolation"
            ],
            [
              "Use MCP",
              "proves external tool strategy"
            ],
            [
              "Persist/resume agent",
              "proves background continuity"
            ],
            [
              "Stream events to our feed",
              "proves UI architecture"
            ],
            [
              "Map execution → avatar states",
              "proves interaction concept"
            ],
            [
              "Human approval from our UI",
              "exposes the biggest integration gap"
            ],
            [
              "Restart runtime and resume",
              "proves durability"
            ],
            [
              "Run two isolated client instances",
              "tests managed-service architecture"
            ]
          ]
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "If Harness performs well there, **I would seriously consider adopting it**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "If approval/custom-UI integration or Cordis becomes painful, we can abandon it without touching the Brand Core."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Bottom line"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "DeepSeek Harness could remove a **large amount of generic agent-runtime engineering** from the project."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "It already solves difficult problems we would otherwise eventually encounter:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**agent lifecycle**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**session durability**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**replay**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**tool execution**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**permissions**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**approvals**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**MCP**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**model adapters**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**subagents**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**cancellation**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**scoped capabilities**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**plugin lifecycle**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Those are substantial."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But it does **not solve the hardest product-specific problem**:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**building and maintaining the structured shared world representation of the brand, and deciding how real-world evidence and human feedback change that representation.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That remains ours."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So my revised architecture would be:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**Brand Core = our moat.**\n\n**Feed/avatars = our product experience.**\n\n**Marketing intelligence logic = our domain IP.**\n\n**DeepSeek Harness = potentially the engine room underneath the agents.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I think that is a genuinely strong fit."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**Today I would rate Harness ~8/10 architecturally for our agent-runtime needs, but only ~5/10 as a production dependency because it is explicitly brand-new developer-preview software.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "If it stabilizes, it could save us from building a surprisingly large amount of infrastructure that has little to do with what actually differentiates our product. memcite"
        }
      ],
      "artifact_refs": []
    },

      "content": "but would it helps us implement content compilation between our box and the agents?",

      "content": "Without DeepSeek Harness, you would need to assemble or build most of the **agent runtime layer** yourself. track status.\n- **Session/state management:** persist conversations, tool calls, intermediate steps, resumability, crash recovery.\n- **Prompt/context assembly:** take the output of our Context Compiler and reliably inject it into the right agent/request.\n- **Tool registry:** define tools, schemas, permissions, timeouts, errors, parallel execution.\n- **Agent-specific tool access:** Researcher can use web tools, Growth can use analytics, Storyteller gets different capabilities.\n- **MCP integration:** connections, namespacing, reconnects, tool discovery, failures.\n- **Multi-agent delegation:** parent/child agents, task passing, continuation, cancellation, depth limits.\n- **Approval system:** pause a dangerous action, ask the user, record the answer, resume safely.\n- **Event stream:** emit reliable events for `agent_started`, `tool_called`, `result`, `approval_needed`, etc.—which our feed and avatar animations would consume.\n- **Persistence/replay:** reconstruct exactly what an agent saw and did later for debugging and audits.\n- **Model abstraction:** switching DeepSeek/OpenAI/Anthropic/etc. without rewriting agents.\n- **Failure handling:** retries, timeouts, interrupted runs, tool failures, partial executions.\n- **Observability:** traces, token usage, costs, agent runs, tool activity.\n\nHarness already has sophisticated versions of many of these concepts: its sessions are event-sourced and persistent, its tool pipeline supports scoped policies and typed inputs/outputs, it has agent-scoped prompt/context assembly, MCP, subagents, and explicit approval primitives. fileciteturn4file0L2-L2 fileciteturn10file0L2-L2 fileciteturn21file0L2-L2\n\n### What we still build regardless\n\nHarness does **not** remove the most loop\nSessions\nTools\nMCP\nSubagents\nApprovals\nPersistence\nEvents\nModel adapters\n```\n\nWithout Harness, I'd probably use something like **OpenAI Agents SDK / Vercel AI SDK + a workflow engine + Postgres**, rather than writing absolutely everything from zero.\n\nSo the real comparison is not:\n\n> **Harness vs building everything ourselves**\n\nIt's:\n\n> **Harness vs assembling 4–6 smaller libraries and writing the glue ourselves.**\n\nFor V1, that glue is manageable.\n\nFor the mature system we've described, it becomes a **substantial engineering subsystem** of its own.\n\nThat's why Harness is interesting: it could let you spend much more of your time on the **Brand Core, Context Compiler, marketing intelligence and UX**, which are the parts that actually differentiate the product. memcite",

      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "Yes — **but not all of it**.\n\nIf you used LangGraph, you would avoid building a lot of the runtime machinery from scratch. LangGraph already gives you durable execution, checkpointed state, resumable threads, human-in-the-loop interrupts, subgraphs, streaming, and fault recovery. It is explicitly designed as a low-level orchestration runtime for long-running stateful agents. citeturn926954search0turn692059search2\n\nSo with LangGraph, you would **not** need to reinvent things like:\n\n- workflow state and checkpoints\n- pause/resume for approvals\n- durable multi-step execution\n- subagent/subgraph state\n- basic memory/thread persistence\n- recovery after failures\n- graph routing between deterministic and agentic steps\n\nFor example, LangGraph's `interrupt()` can pause a workflow, persist its current state, wait indefinitely for a human response, and then resume from the saved checkpoint. citeturn692059search1\n\nBut you would still have to build more surrounding infrastructure than with something like DeepSeek Harness.\n\nThe difference is roughly:\n\n> **LangGraph = orchestration engine**\n>\n> **DeepSeek Harness = fuller agent runtime/harness**\n\nLangChain itself describes LangGraph as intentionally low-level and focused on orchestration; model/tool abstractions generally come from LangChain or your own code. citeturn926954search0\n\nFor our system, the comparison would look like this:\n\n| Requirement | LangGraph | DeepSeek Harness |\n|---|---:|---:|\n| Durable workflows | ✅ | ✅ |\n| Pause/resume | ✅ | ✅ |\n| Human approval | ✅ primitives | ✅ dedicated approval layer |\n| Multi-agent/subagents | ✅ via graphs/subgraphs | ✅ dedicated subagent system |\n| Session persistence | ✅ checkpoints | ✅ event-sourced sessions |\n| Tool calling | Usually LangChain/custom | ✅ native tool registry |\n| Agent-specific tool permissions | You design | ✅ built-in scoping/filtering |\n| MCP | Via `langchain-mcp-adapters` | ✅ native plugin |\n| Model abstraction | Usually LangChain | ✅ adapter layer |\n| Agent personas | You implement | ✅ scoped persona system |\n| Agent event stream | LangGraph streaming/state | ✅ richer runtime events |\n| Tool execution policy | Mostly yours | ✅ dedicated pipeline |\n| Plugin lifecycle | Mostly yours | ✅ Cordis |\n| Custom workflows | **Excellent** | Good |\n| Low-level control | **Excellent** | Good |\n\nLangChain now has an official MCP adapter, so MCP itself wouldn't be hard to add alongside LangGraph. citeturn926954search2\n\n### The important part for our Brand Core\n\nRegardless of whether we choose LangGraph or Harness, **we still have to build this ourselves**:\n\n```text\nBrand Core\n    ↓\nknowledge retrieval\n    ↓\nContext Compiler\n    ↓\nrelevant ContextPackage\n    ↓\nagent\n```\n\nNeither framework knows that a Storytelling Agent should receive:\n\n> positioning + customer language + proof + brand beliefs + narrative history\n\nwhile a Research Agent should receive:\n\n> market context + competitors + hypotheses + customer signals.\n\nThat logic is ours.\n\nWith LangGraph, we'd probably implement a node like:\n\n```text\nTask\n ↓\ncompile_context\n ↓\nStrategist Agent\n ↓\nvalidate\n ↓\nhuman approval?\n ↓\nwrite result\n```\n\nLangGraph is very good for expressing exactly this kind of workflow because graphs consist of explicit **state, nodes and edges**. citeturn926954search7\n\nSo for us, LangGraph might look like:\n\n```text\n            OUR BRAND CORE\n                   │\n                   ▼\n           Context Compiler\n                   │\n                   ▼\n        ┌────────────────────┐\n        │     LANGGRAPH      │\n        │                    │\n        │ Researcher         │\n        │ Strategist         │\n        │ Storyteller        │\n        │ validators         │\n        │ approval nodes     │\n        │ workflow routing   │\n        └─────────┬──────────┘\n                  │\n                  ▼\n               Tools\n```\n\nWhereas Harness is closer to:\n\n```text\n            OUR BRAND CORE\n                   │\n                   ▼\n           Context Compiler\n                   │\n                   ▼\n        ┌────────────────────┐\n        │      HARNESS       │\n        │ agent sessions     │\n        │ tool registry      │\n        │ permissions        │\n        │ subagents          │\n        │ approvals          │\n        │ MCP                │\n        │ event logs         │\n        │ model adapters     │\n        └────────────────────┘\n```\n\n### Which is better for our system?\n\nI think there is an important distinction.\n\nIf we want **very explicit marketing workflows**, such as:\n\n> research → synthesize → formulate hypothesis → strategist review → founder approval → campaign brief\n\nthen **LangGraph is extremely attractive**.\n\nWe can see the whole workflow as a deterministic graph and control every transition.\n\nIf instead we want something closer to:\n\n> persistent autonomous agent inhabitants that have sessions, tools, identities, permissions, conversations and can keep working over time\n\nthen **Harness is closer to our conceptual product**.\n\nAnd our vision increasingly looks like the second one.\n\nThe little guys aren't merely nodes in workflows.\n\nThey are supposed to feel like **persistent actors inside the brand's world**.\n\nResearcher exists continuously.\n\nStrategist exists continuously.\n\nFounder can chat with Strategist.\n\nResearcher can work in the background.\n\nTheir activity appears in the feed.\n\nTheir state drives avatar animations.\n\nThat maps quite naturally to Harness's persistent-agent/session architecture.\n\n### There is also a possible hybrid\n\nThis is actually what I would keep in mind:\n\n> **Harness for agents.**\n>\n> **LangGraph—or a simpler workflow engine—for important deterministic workflows.**\n\nFor example:\n\n```text\nResearch Agent\n     │\n     ▼\nfinds opportunity\n     │\n     ▼\n   LangGraph workflow\n     │\n     ├─ validate evidence\n     ├─ ask Strategist\n     ├─ Brand Guardian check\n     ├─ human approval\n     └─ create campaign\n```\n\nYou do **not** necessarily want every business process to be an autonomous agent conversation.\n\nSome things should be deterministic pipelines.\n\nSo in our architecture I increasingly see three distinct things:\n\n```text\n1. BRAND CORE\n   what the company knows\n\n2. AGENT RUNTIME\n   who thinks / works\n\n3. WORKFLOW ENGINE\n   how important processes execute\n```\n\nDeepSeek Harness could potentially handle **#2**.\n\nLangGraph is excellent for **#3**, while also being capable of implementing #2 if we want to build more of the surrounding agent infrastructure ourselves.\n\nSo yes: **LangGraph would already save you a lot of work.**\n\nBut compared with Harness, you would likely still write more of the **persistent-agent product layer** yourself.\n\nAnd critically, neither eliminates the hardest proprietary part:\n\n> **Brand Core + Context Compiler + marketing semantics.**\n\nThat's where I would continue to concentrate most of our engineering effort. memcite",
