presence\n```\n\nLangGraph owns something more like:\n\n```text\n             STRATEGY PROCESS\n\n                    ↓\n\n          understand objective\n                    ↓\n          identify key tension\n                    ↓\n          generate hypotheses\n                    ↓\n         ┌──────────┴──────────┐\n         ↓                     ↓\n customer evidence       competitive evidence\n         ↓                     ↓\n         └──────────┬──────────┘\n                    ↓\n             score options\n                    ↓\n            critic challenge\n                    ↓\n            strong enough?\n             ↙          ↘\n           no            yes\n           ↓              ↓\n      investigate        decide\n           ↓              ↓\n           └──── revise ──┘\n                    ↓\n             recommendation\n```\n\nLangGraph gives you direct control over that structure. citeturn680676search2\n\nThat's much deeper than:\n\n> \"You are an expert strategist.\"\n\nIt means **being a Strategist actually corresponds to a different computational process.**\n\nThat is valuable for our concept.\n\n---\n\n# And every little guy could genuinely think differently\n\nResearcher:\n\n```text\nquestion\n→ break into research questions\n→ search\n→ source-quality analysis\n→ extract evidence\n→ identify contradictions\n→ investigate missing evidence\n→ synthesize\n→ confidence check\n```\n\nStrategist:\n\n```text\nproblem\n→ tensions\n→ hypotheses\n→ evidence\n→ alternatives\n→ critic\n→ tradeoffs\n→ recommendation\n```\n\nStoryteller:\n\n```text\nbrand truth\n→ audience tension\n→ narrative territories\n→ divergence\n→ originality evaluation\n→ brand-fit evaluation\n→ convergence\n→ story\n```\n\nBrand Guardian:\n\n```text\nproposed output\n→ identify claims\n→ compare Brand Core\n→ identify contradictions\n→ evaluate evidence\n→ evaluate tone\n→ risk score\n→ allow / revise / escalate\n```\n\nGrowth:\n\n```text\nsignal\n→ anomaly?\n→ identify likely causes\n→ generate hypotheses\n→ query evidence\n→ rank opportunities\n→ expected impact\n→ recommended experiment\n```\n\nNow the characters aren't different because they have different prompts.\n\nThey're different because they have **different decision architectures**.\n\nLangGraph is particularly strong for exactly this because state, nodes and routing are first-class concepts rather than hidden inside a generic agent loop. citeturn611701search4\n\n---\n\n# Technically, there are four ways to combine the frameworks\n\nI evaluated them like this:\n\n| Architecture | Feasibility | Complexity | My view |\n|---|---:|---:|---|\n| Harness → LangGraph cognitive tool | **9/10** | Medium | **Best** |\n| Custom Harness loop implemented with LangGraph | 7/10 | Very high | Later |\n| LangGraph → Harness agents through SDK | 7/10 | High | Avoid |\n| Two independent services | 9/10 | Medium-high | Possible later |\n\nThe first one is the interesting option.\n\n---\n\n# Option 1 — Harness calls LangGraph\n\nYou build a Harness plugin approximately conceptually like:\n\n```text\nstrategy_reasoning()\nresearch_reasoning()\nstory_reasoning()\ngrowth_reasoning()\n```\n\nUnderneath:\n\n```text\nstrategy_reasoning()\n        ↓\ncompiled LangGraph\n        ↓\nstructured recommendation\n```\n\nHarness custom tools are just async TypeScript execution functions with typed arguments and outputs, cancellation, policy interception and access to the current agent. fileciteturn23file0\n\nAnd LangGraph has a JavaScript/TypeScript implementation, so this can all happen **inside the same Node process** rather than requiring Python or a separate microservice. LangGraph graphs expose normal `invoke()` and `stream()` interfaces. citeturn680676search2\n\nConceptually:\n\n```ts\nHarness plugin\n      │\n      └─ StrategyGraph.invoke({\n             task,\n             contextPackage\n         })\n```\n\nVery normal integration.\n\nNo HTTP service is inherently necessary.\n\n---\n\n# But there's an important trap: double persistence\n\nBoth frameworks know how to persist state.\n\nHarness has its append-only session/event system.\n\nLangGraph has checkpointed thread state saved after graph execution steps. citeturn549031search4\n\nIf we naïvely enable everything:\n\n```text\nHarness session\n     ↓\nLangGraph thread\n     ↓\nHarness tool calls\n     ↓\nLangGraph checkpoints\n     ↓\nHarness events\n     ↓\nLangGraph interrupts\n     ↓\nHarness approvals\n```\n\nwe've created **two sources of truth**.\n\nThat's bad.\n\nWhich one resumes the workflow?\n\nWhich one owns cancellation?\n\nWhich one represents the user approval?\n\nWhich one says the task completed?\n\nWhich history drives the feed?\n\nThis is the biggest architectural problem with combining them.\n\n---\n\n# So I would impose a hard ownership rule\n\n### Harness owns the agent lifecycle.\n\nLangGraph owns **only the reasoning procedure**.\n\nMeaning:\n\n```text\nHARNESS OWNS\n\nidentity\npersistent conversation\nagent existence\ntool permissions\nMCP\nexternal actions\nhuman approvals\nruntime/session history\n```\n\nwhile:\n\n```text\nLANGGRAPH OWNS\n\ninternal reasoning state\nbranches\nloops\ncritics\nhypothesis evaluation\ndecision algorithms\ntemporary working state\n```\n\nThat boundary makes the combination clean.\n\n---\n\n# I would initially disable LangGraph persistence\n\nFor most agent reasoning runs:\n\n```text\ntask\n    ↓\nLangGraph\n    ↓\nresult\n```\n\nI'd treat LangGraph like a sophisticated deterministic function.\n\nSomething like:\n\n```text\nStrategyGraph(\n    task,\n    contextPackage\n)\n→ StrategyDecision\n```\n\nNo persistent LangGraph thread.\n\nNo LangGraph memory.\n\nNo LangGraph human approval.\n\nNo separate long-term LangGraph state.\n\nHarness owns persistence outside it.\n\nThis removes a huge amount of complexity.\n\nLangGraph explicitly supports graphs without checkpointing when durable execution isn't needed. citeturn549031search0\n\n---\n\n# What about long-running reasoning?\n\nLater, perhaps the Research Agent does:\n\n```text\nresearch market\n→ 35 searches\n→ compare sources\n→ wait for more data\n→ continue tomorrow\n```\n\nNow LangGraph durability becomes genuinely useful.\n\nIts checkpointer saves graph state between execution steps and supports recovery from prior successful checkpoints. citeturn549031search4\n\nAt that point I might allow:\n\n```text\nHarness session ID\n        │\n        └── reasoning run ID\n                │\n                └── LangGraph thread ID\n```\n\nBut explicitly.\n\nFor example:\n\n```text\nagent_session:\nstrategist_482\n\nreasoning_run:\nstrategy_992\n\nlanggraph_thread:\nstrategy_992\n```\n\nHarness remains the parent truth.\n\nLangGraph owns the detailed state of that particular reasoning run.\n\n---\n\n# Human approval should NOT exist in both\n\nLangGraph has an excellent interrupt mechanism: execution can pause, checkpoint itself, surface a request and resume later with human input. citeturn680676search1\n\nHarness also has a dedicated human-approval system that records requests and decisions. fileciteturn21file0\n\nUsing both would be a mistake.\n\nFor our product I'd choose:\n\n> **Harness = human-facing approvals.**\n\nLangGraph can internally decide:\n\n```text\nconfidence < threshold\n→ requires_human_review = true\n```\n\nBut it returns that state to Harness.\n\nThen Harness creates:\n\n**🟡 Strategist**\n\n> I'm uncertain about this positioning decision.\n\n> I found two plausible directions.\n\n**Discuss** · **Choose A** · **Choose B**\n\nThe feed/user interaction remains governed by our agent runtime.\n\nMuch cleaner.\n\n---\n\n# Same thing with external tools\n\nThis is another place where we need discipline.\n\nBoth ecosystems can expose tools.\n\nBut we should not have:\n\n```text\nHarness HubSpot tool\n\nAND\n\nLangGraph HubSpot tool\n```\n\nThat's dangerous.\n\nPermissions could disagree.\n\nCredentials could disagree.\n\nLogging could disagree.\n\nApprovals could disagree.\n\nInstead:\n\n> **Harness owns real-world tools.**\n\nHarness already has a guarded tool pipeline with typed schemas, agent-specific restrictions, execution interception and MCP bridging. fileciteturn10file0\n\nLangGraph should access those through an adapter.\n\nConceptually:\n\n```text\nLangGraph node\n    ↓\nsearchCompetitors()\n    ↓\nHarness Tool Adapter\n    ↓\nctx.tools\n    ↓\nweb search / MCP\n```\n\nThen:\n\n**one credential system**\n\n**one permission system**\n\n**one audit system**\n\n**one tool implementation**\n\n---\n\n# That bridge is some engineering\n\nThis is where \"possible\" differs from \"free.\"\n\nWe would need a small adapter roughly like:\n\n```text\nHarnessTool\n      ↓\nLangGraph-compatible callable\n```\n\nor:\n\n```text\nLangGraph node\n      ↓\nHarness ctx.tools.execute()\n```\n\nHarness's tool runtime already exposes structured execution inputs and supports nested/composite dispatch patterns, so the architecture is capable of this. fileciteturn10file0\n\nI would estimate a basic adapter as a relatively small engineering job.\n\nMaking it production-grade with:\n\ncancellation, permissions, tracing, error translation, streaming and structured result typing\n\nis more work.\n\nBut still far less work than rebuilding an agent runtime.\n\n---\n\n# The avatar idea actually benefits from LangGraph\n\nThis was a somewhat unexpected conclusion from the research.\n\nLangGraph has rich execution streaming.\n\nIt can emit:\n\n**state changes**\n\n**node changes**\n\n**model messages**\n\n**tool activity**\n\n**subgraph activity**\n\n**custom application events**\n\nand its newer event-streaming layer exposes named execution namespaces and custom projections. citeturn611701search2\n\nThat maps extremely well to:\n\n```text\nResearcher\n\nSEARCHING\n↓\nEVALUATING\n↓\nCONNECTING\n↓\nQUESTIONING\n↓\nSYNTHESIZING\n↓\nPRESENTING\n```\n\nThose don't need to be fake UI animations.\n\nThey can correspond to **actual graph states**.\n\nFor example:\n\n```text\nLangGraph node:\nsource_quality_analysis\n\n        ↓\n\nfrontend event:\nresearcher.evaluating_sources\n\n        ↓\n\navatar:\nblue creature inspects floating documents\n```\n\nThen:\n\n```text\nLangGraph node:\nevidence_synthesis\n\n        ↓\n\navatar:\nfragments move together into one shape\n```\n\nThis is exactly the kind of thing that could make our interaction design unusually coherent.\n\nLangGraph's own frontend documentation even discusses mapping named graph nodes to visible execution states and UI cards. citeturn680676search7\n\nFor us we'd map them to the little guys instead.\n\n---\n\n# Option 2 — replace Harness's agent loop with LangGraph\n\nThis is technically even more elegant.\n\nHarness explicitly says its `Agent` interface has **zero dependency on its concrete loop**, so the loop is swappable, and custom agents can implement the interface themselves. fileciteturn25file0\n\nConceptually:\n\n```text\nHarness Agent API\n       │\n       ▼\nOur LangGraphAgentLoop\n       │\n       ▼\nLangGraph\n```\n\nThen there wouldn't be:\n\n> Harness outer LLM → calls LangGraph tool → LangGraph LLM → back to Harness LLM.\n\nLangGraph would simply **be the agent's reasoning engine**.\n\nThat's conceptually beautiful.\n\nBut I would **not build this yet**.\n\nWhy?\n\nHarness has strong invariants around:\n\nsessions, model-visible history, event logging, tool calls, turn boundaries, persistence and replay.\n\nIts architecture says the session log is the source from which model history is reconstructed. fileciteturn4file0\n\nIf LangGraph suddenly becomes the driver, we'd have to correctly translate:\n\n```text\nLangGraph model call\n→ Harness step event\n\nLangGraph tool call\n→ Harness tool/call\n\nLangGraph result\n→ Harness tool/result\n\nLangGraph state\n→ Harness events\n\nLangGraph completion\n→ Harness turn/end\n```\n\nThat's significant infrastructure.\n\nAnd Harness is currently explicitly a **developer preview with compatibility-breaking changes expected**. fileciteturn3file0\n\nBuilding deep internals against it today would create unnecessary risk.\n\nMaybe later.\n\nNot V1.\n\n---\n\n# Option 3 — LangGraph outside, Harness inside\n\nSomething like:\n\n```text\nLangGraph\n    │\n    ├── Research node → Harness Researcher\n    │\n    ├── Strategy node → Harness Strategist\n    │\n    └── Story node → Harness Storyteller\n```\n\nThis is also possible because Harness exposes a TypeScript SDK that can launch and drive a Harness runtime through JSON-RPC. fileciteturn15file0\n\nBut I don't like it for our system.\n\nThe current SDK documentation explicitly lists limitations including no mid-turn cancellation, no prompt-specific result primitive, and incomplete client↔server messaging relevant to things such as approval flows. fileciteturn15file0\n\nYou also end up with:\n\n```text\nLangGraph thread\n      ↓\nHarness session\n      ↓\nHarness agent\n      ↓\nHarness subagents\n```\n\ntoo many lifecycle abstractions.\n\nIt's feasible.\n\nIt's not elegant.\n\n---\n\n# The Context Compiler stays clean in the hybrid\n\nThis is especially important.\n\nOur proprietary Context Compiler remains above both systems.\n\n```text\nTask:\n\"Should we reposition enterprise messaging?\"\n\n              ↓\n\nContext Compiler\n\n              ↓\n\n{\n  positioning,\n  enterpriseICP,\n  objections,\n  customerLanguage,\n  competitorPositions,\n  proof,\n  previousDecisions,\n  relevantPerformance\n}\n\n              ↓\n\nStrategist's LangGraph\n```\n\nHarness should not determine those facts.\n\nLangGraph should not retrieve the whole box indiscriminately.\n\n**Our compiler decides the context.**\n\nThat preserves one of the core pieces of IP we've identified.\n\n---\n\n# There is a subtle efficiency issue: nested LLM calls\n\nImagine Harness's Strategist itself is an LLM agent.\n\nIt thinks:\n\n> I should invoke `strategic_analysis`.\n\nThen LangGraph runs:\n\n```text\nLLM\n→ evidence check\n→ LLM\n→ critic\n→ LLM\n→ recommendation\n```\n\nThen the Harness agent receives the result and calls another LLM to explain it.\n\nWe've now potentially created:\n\n```text\nHarness LLM\n     ↓\nLangGraph LLM\n     ↓\nLangGraph LLM\n     ↓\nLangGraph LLM\n     ↓\nHarness LLM\n```\n\nThat costs latency and tokens.\n\nThis is why I would eventually structure agents slightly differently.\n\nThe Harness shell should be **thin**.\n\nFor serious tasks:\n\n```text\nUSER\n ↓\nHarness agent/router\n ↓\nStrategyGraph\n ↓\nstructured StrategyDecision\n ↓\npresentation layer\n```\n\nDon't make the outer model rethink the entire answer.\n\nThe final graph output should already be structured enough for presentation.\n\n---\n\n# An even better conceptual model\n\nAfter researching this, I would distinguish three levels:\n\n```text\nPERSONALITY\n\"What kind of agent am I?\"\n\nHarness persona / agent definition\n\nCOGNITION\n\"How do I approach problems?\"\n\nLangGraph\n\nKNOWLEDGE\n\"What do I know about this company?\"\n\nBrand Core + Context Compiler\n```\n\nThat is a very strong architecture.\n\nFor example:\n\n```text\n                     STRATEGIST\n\nPersonality    calm / challenging / analytical\n                     │\n                 HARNESS\n                     │\n                     ▼\nCognition     tension → hypotheses → critique\n                     │\n                 LANGGRAPH\n                     │\n                     ▼\nKnowledge     brand / customers / market / history\n                     │\n                BRAND CORE\n```\n\nThose layers are meaningfully different.\n\n---\n\n# Is it efficient for a solopreneur?\n\nThis is where my answer becomes more cautious.\n\n### Technically:\n**Yes.**\n\n### Architecturally:\n**Yes, if responsibilities are separated.**\n\n### From day one:\n**Probably not.**\n\nBecause there is substantial overlap.\n\nBoth can handle:\n\npersistence, state, streaming, agents/subagents and human interaction concepts. citeturn549031search0turn549031search2turn611701search2\n\nEvery overlap is another place where you need to decide:\n\n> who's in charge?\n\nFor a solo founder, that cognitive overhead is real.\n\n---\n\n# What I would actually do\n\nI would build **one experiment**, not redesign everything around both frameworks.\n\nImplement:\n\n```text\nSTRATEGIST\n```\n\nusing:\n\n```text\nBrand Core mock\n      ↓\nContext Compiler\n      ↓\nHarness Strategist\n      ↓\nLangGraph strategy process\n      ↓\nHarness tool access\n      ↓\nstructured recommendation\n      ↓\nFeed post\n      ↓\navatar state animation\n```\n\nAnd specifically test:\n\n1. Does the LangGraph reasoning structure produce materially better strategy than a strong prompt?\n\n2. Can Harness → LangGraph context transfer remain simple?\n\n3. Can LangGraph use Harness-managed tools without ugly plumbing?\n\n4. Can LangGraph node events cleanly drive avatar states?\n\n5. Can we maintain **one** approval system?\n\n6. Can we maintain **one** external tool/credential system?\n\n7. Is latency acceptable?\n\nIf the answer is yes, the combination is worth pursuing.\n\n---\n\n# My resulting recommendation\n\nI'd currently rank our choices:\n\n| Architecture | Fit for full vision |\n|---|---:|\n| LangGraph alone | **8.5/10** |\n| Harness alone | **8.5/10** |\n| Naively combine both | **5/10** |\n| **Harness shell + selective LangGraph cognition** | **9.5/10 conceptually** |\n| Custom LangGraph-powered Harness loop today | 6/10 |\n| Custom LangGraph-powered Harness loop later | **9/10** |\n\nThe highest-potential architecture is therefore **not**:\n\n> Harness + LangGraph everywhere.\n\nIt's:\n\n> **Use Harness for what makes an agent an enduring actor.**\n>\n> **Use LangGraph only where a specialized cognitive process genuinely benefits from an explicit graph.**\n\nThe Researcher might have a fairly elaborate graph.\n\nStrategist could have another.\n\nBrand Guardian could have a very deterministic one.\n\nA simple conversational Orchestrator might not need LangGraph at all.\n\nThat is much more efficient than forcing everything into graphs.\n\nAnd because LangGraph also has a Functional API specifically designed to add its runtime features to otherwise normal procedural code, we don't even need to turn every thought process into a giant node diagram. citeturn611701search9\n\n### One major caveat\n\nI would put DeepSeek Harness behind our own abstraction today:\n\n```text\nAgentRuntime\n├── create()\n├── send()\n├── cancel()\n├── subscribe()\n├── executeTool()\n└── dispose()\n```\n\nbecause Harness itself says it's still a developer preview and expects breaking compatibility changes. fileciteturn3file0\n\nSo the final stack I currently like best is:\n\n```text\n             OUR PRODUCT\n─────────────────────────────────\n\n             Brand Core\n                 │\n          Context Compiler\n                 │\n       Agent Definitions\n                 │\n     Cognitive Graph Library\n          [LangGraph]\n                 │\n          AgentRuntime\n                 │\n     [DeepSeek Harness adapter]\n                 │\n        Tools / MCP / APIs\n                 │\n             Feed UI\n                 │\n       Avatar Motion System\n```\n\n**Brand Core, Context Compiler, cognitive graphs, domain semantics and UI remain ours.**\n\nHarness becomes replaceable infrastructure.\n\nLangGraph becomes replaceable cognitive infrastructure.\n\nThat protects us from being trapped by either framework while still letting us exploit both.\n\nAfter doing the deeper research, **I think the hybrid is more technically credible than I initially expected — but only with this strict separation of responsibilities.** memcite",
      "blocks": [
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Yes. I dug into both architectures, and **combining them is technically possible and can be architecturally elegant**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But there is an important condition:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**Do not use LangGraph and DeepSeek Harness as two competing agent runtimes.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "If both try to own agents, persistence, approvals, tools, memory, streaming, and orchestration, the result will be unnecessarily complicated."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The combination becomes attractive when each gets **one clearly defined job**."
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 2,
          "text": "The architecture I would use"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For our system:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "                      BRAND CORE\n                    \"the box\"\n                        │\n                        ▼\n                 CONTEXT COMPILER\n                        │\n              ContextPackage<Task>\n                        │\n                        ▼\n          ┌─────────────────────────┐\n          │    DEEPSEEK HARNESS     │\n          │                         │\n          │ persistent agent        │\n          │ identity                │\n          │ session                 │\n          │ permissions             │\n          │ MCP / tools             │\n          │ approvals               │\n          │ runtime events          │\n          └────────────┬────────────┘\n                       │\n             agent needs to think\n                       │\n                       ▼\n          ┌─────────────────────────┐\n          │       LANGGRAPH         │\n          │                         │\n          │ agent-specific          │\n          │ cognitive process       │\n          │                         │\n          │ hypothesize             │\n          │ investigate             │\n          │ compare                 │\n          │ critique                │\n          │ revise                  │\n          │ decide                  │\n          └────────────┬────────────┘\n                       │\n                  structured result\n                       │\n                       ▼\n               DEEPSEEK HARNESS\n                       │\n                 action / post\n                       │\n                       ▼\n                   OUR FEED"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is feasible because Harness is deliberately plugin-based and agent-scoped; custom tools and services can be registered inside an agent's context, and DeepSeek explicitly designed the `Agent` interface so that the concrete loop is replaceable. fileciteturn25file0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "LangGraph, meanwhile, is specifically designed for custom execution structures with explicit sequential steps, branches, loops, parallel work and combinations of deterministic and LLM logic. citeturn611701search0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That separation fits remarkably well."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "The key insight: LangGraph becomes the brain pattern, not the agent"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Take our Strategist."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Harness owns:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Strategist\n├── identity\n├── conversation\n├── Brand Core access\n├── tools\n├── permissions\n├── model configuration\n├── persistent session\n└── feed presence"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "LangGraph owns something more like:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "             STRATEGY PROCESS\n\n                    ↓\n\n          understand objective\n                    ↓\n          identify key tension\n                    ↓\n          generate hypotheses\n                    ↓\n         ┌──────────┴──────────┐\n         ↓                     ↓\n customer evidence       competitive evidence\n         ↓                     ↓\n         └──────────┬──────────┘\n                    ↓\n             score options\n                    ↓\n            critic challenge\n                    ↓\n            strong enough?\n             ↙          ↘\n           no            yes\n           ↓              ↓\n      investigate        decide\n           ↓              ↓\n           └──── revise ──┘\n                    ↓\n             recommendation"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "LangGraph gives you direct control over that structure. citeturn680676search2"

          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,

        },

          "type": "code",

          "text": "question\n→ break into research questions\n→ search\n→ source-quality analysis\n→ extract evidence\n→ identify contradictions\n→ investigate missing evidence\n→ synthesize\n→ confidence check"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Strategist:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "problem\n→ tensions\n→ hypotheses\n→ evidence\n→ alternatives\n→ critic\n→ tradeoffs\n→ recommendation"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Storyteller:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "brand truth\n→ audience tension\n→ narrative territories\n→ divergence\n→ originality evaluation\n→ brand-fit evaluation\n→ convergence\n→ story"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Brand Guardian:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "proposed output\n→ identify claims\n→ compare Brand Core\n→ identify contradictions\n→ evaluate evidence\n→ evaluate tone\n→ risk score\n→ allow / revise / escalate"
        },

          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Growth:"
        },

          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "signal\n→ anomaly?\n→ identify likely causes\n→ generate hypotheses\n→ query evidence\n→ rank opportunities\n→ expected impact\n→ recommended experiment"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Now the characters aren't different because they have different prompts."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "They're different because they have **different decision architectures**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "LangGraph is particularly strong for exactly this because state, nodes and routing are first-class concepts rather than hidden inside a generic agent loop. citeturn611701search4"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Technically, there are four ways to combine the frameworks"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I evaluated them like this:"
        },
        {
          "type": "table",
          "header": [
            "Architecture",
            "Feasibility",
            "Complexity",
            "My view"
          ],
          "rows": [
            [
              "Harness → LangGraph cognitive tool",
              "**9/10**",
              "Medium",
              "**Best**"
            ],
            [
              "Custom Harness loop implemented with LangGraph",
              "7/10",
              "Very high",
              "Later"
            ],
            [
              "LangGraph → Harness agents through SDK",
              "7/10",
              "High",
              "Avoid"
            ],
            [
              "Two independent services",
              "9/10",
              "Medium-high",
              "Possible later"
            ]
          ]
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The first one is the interesting option."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Option 1 — Harness calls LangGraph"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "You build a Harness plugin approximately conceptually like:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "strategy_reasoning()\nresearch_reasoning()\nstory_reasoning()\ngrowth_reasoning()"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Underneath:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "strategy_reasoning()\n        ↓\ncompiled LangGraph\n        ↓\nstructured recommendation"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Harness custom tools are just async TypeScript execution functions with typed arguments and outputs, cancellation, policy interception and access to the current agent. fileciteturn23file0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "And LangGraph has a JavaScript/TypeScript implementation, so this can all happen **inside the same Node process** rather than requiring Python or a separate microservice. LangGraph graphs expose normal `invoke()` and `stream()` interfaces. citeturn680676search2"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Conceptually:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "ts",
          "text": "Harness plugin\n      │\n      └─ StrategyGraph.invoke({\n             task,\n             contextPackage\n         })"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Very normal integration."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "No HTTP service is inherently necessary."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "But there's an important trap: double persistence"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Both frameworks know how to persist state."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Harness has its append-only session/event system."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "LangGraph has checkpointed thread state saved after graph execution steps. citeturn549031search4"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "If we naïvely enable everything:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Harness session\n     ↓\nLangGraph thread\n     ↓\nHarness tool calls\n     ↓\nLangGraph checkpoints\n     ↓\nHarness events\n     ↓\nLangGraph interrupts\n     ↓\nHarness approvals"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "we've created **two sources of truth**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's bad."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Which one resumes the workflow?"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Which one owns cancellation?"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Which one represents the user approval?"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Which one says the task completed?"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Which history drives the feed?"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is the biggest architectural problem with combining them."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "So I would impose a hard ownership rule"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 3,
          "text": "Harness owns the agent lifecycle."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "LangGraph owns **only the reasoning procedure**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Meaning:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "HARNESS OWNS\n\nidentity\npersistent conversation\nagent existence\ntool permissions\nMCP\nexternal actions\nhuman approvals\nruntime/session history"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "while:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "LANGGRAPH OWNS\n\ninternal reasoning state\nbranches\nloops\ncritics\nhypothesis evaluation\ndecision algorithms\ntemporary working state"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That boundary makes the combination clean."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "I would initially disable LangGraph persistence"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For most agent reasoning runs:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "task\n    ↓\nLangGraph\n    ↓\nresult"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I'd treat LangGraph like a sophisticated deterministic function."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Something like:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "StrategyGraph(\n    task,\n    contextPackage\n)\n→ StrategyDecision"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "No persistent LangGraph thread."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "No LangGraph memory."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "No LangGraph human approval."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "No separate long-term LangGraph state."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Harness owns persistence outside it."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This removes a huge amount of complexity."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "LangGraph explicitly supports graphs without checkpointing when durable execution isn't needed. citeturn549031search0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "What about long-running reasoning?"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Later, perhaps the Research Agent does:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "research market\n→ 35 searches\n→ compare sources\n→ wait for more data\n→ continue tomorrow"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Now LangGraph durability becomes genuinely useful."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Its checkpointer saves graph state between execution steps and supports recovery from prior successful checkpoints. citeturn549031search4"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "At that point I might allow:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Harness session ID\n        │\n        └── reasoning run ID\n                │\n                └── LangGraph thread ID"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But explicitly."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For example:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "agent_session:\nstrategist_482\n\nreasoning_run:\nstrategy_992\n\nlanggraph_thread:\nstrategy_992"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Harness remains the parent truth."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "LangGraph owns the detailed state of that particular reasoning run."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Human approval should NOT exist in both"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "LangGraph has an excellent interrupt mechanism: execution can pause, checkpoint itself, surface a request and resume later with human input. citeturn680676search1"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Harness also has a dedicated human-approval system that records requests and decisions. fileciteturn21file0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Using both would be a mistake."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For our product I'd choose:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**Harness = human-facing approvals.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "LangGraph can internally decide:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "confidence < threshold\n→ requires_human_review = true"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But it returns that state to Harness."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Then Harness creates:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**🟡 Strategist**"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "I'm uncertain about this positioning decision."
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "I found two plausible directions."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**Discuss** · **Choose A** · **Choose B**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The feed/user interaction remains governed by our agent runtime."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Much cleaner."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Same thing with external tools"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is another place where we need discipline."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Both ecosystems can expose tools."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But we should not have:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Harness HubSpot tool\n\nAND\n\nLangGraph HubSpot tool"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's dangerous."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Permissions could disagree."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Credentials could disagree."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Logging could disagree."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Approvals could disagree."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Instead:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**Harness owns real-world tools.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Harness already has a guarded tool pipeline with typed schemas, agent-specific restrictions, execution interception and MCP bridging. fileciteturn10file0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "LangGraph should access those through an adapter."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Conceptually:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "LangGraph node\n    ↓\nsearchCompetitors()\n    ↓\nHarness Tool Adapter\n    ↓\nctx.tools\n    ↓\nweb search / MCP"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Then:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**one credential system**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**one permission system**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**one audit system**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**one tool implementation**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "That bridge is some engineering"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is where \"possible\" differs from \"free.\""
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "We would need a small adapter roughly like:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "HarnessTool\n      ↓\nLangGraph-compatible callable"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "or:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "LangGraph node\n      ↓\nHarness ctx.tools.execute()"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Harness's tool runtime already exposes structured execution inputs and supports nested/composite dispatch patterns, so the architecture is capable of this. fileciteturn10file0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I would estimate a basic adapter as a relatively small engineering job."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Making it production-grade with:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "cancellation, permissions, tracing, error translation, streaming and structured result typing"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "is more work."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But still far less work than rebuilding an agent runtime."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "The avatar idea actually benefits from LangGraph"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This was a somewhat unexpected conclusion from the research."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "LangGraph has rich execution streaming."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "It can emit:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**state changes**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**node changes**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**model messages**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**tool activity**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**subgraph activity**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**custom application events**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "and its newer event-streaming layer exposes named execution namespaces and custom projections. citeturn611701search2"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That maps extremely well to:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Researcher\n\nSEARCHING\n↓\nEVALUATING\n↓\nCONNECTING\n↓\nQUESTIONING\n↓\nSYNTHESIZING\n↓\nPRESENTING"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Those don't need to be fake UI animations."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "They can correspond to **actual graph states**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For example:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "LangGraph node:\nsource_quality_analysis\n\n        ↓\n\nfrontend event:\nresearcher.evaluating_sources\n\n        ↓\n\navatar:\nblue creature inspects floating documents"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Then:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "LangGraph node:\nevidence_synthesis\n\n        ↓\n\navatar:\nfragments move together into one shape"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is exactly the kind of thing that could make our interaction design unusually coherent."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "LangGraph's own frontend documentation even discusses mapping named graph nodes to visible execution states and UI cards. citeturn680676search7"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For us we'd map them to the little guys instead."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Option 2 — replace Harness's agent loop with LangGraph"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is technically even more elegant."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Harness explicitly says its `Agent` interface has **zero dependency on its concrete loop**, so the loop is swappable, and custom agents can implement the interface themselves. fileciteturn25file0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Conceptually:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Harness Agent API\n       │\n       ▼\nOur LangGraphAgentLoop\n       │\n       ▼\nLangGraph"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Then there wouldn't be:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "Harness outer LLM → calls LangGraph tool → LangGraph LLM → back to Harness LLM."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "LangGraph would simply **be the agent's reasoning engine**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's conceptually beautiful."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But I would **not build this yet**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Why?"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Harness has strong invariants around:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "sessions, model-visible history, event logging, tool calls, turn boundaries, persistence and replay."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Its architecture says the session log is the source from which model history is reconstructed. fileciteturn4file0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "If LangGraph suddenly becomes the driver, we'd have to correctly translate:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "LangGraph model call\n→ Harness step event\n\nLangGraph tool call\n→ Harness tool/call\n\nLangGraph result\n→ Harness tool/result\n\nLangGraph state\n→ Harness events\n\nLangGraph completion\n→ Harness turn/end"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's significant infrastructure."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "And Harness is currently explicitly a **developer preview with compatibility-breaking changes expected**. fileciteturn3file0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Building deep internals against it today would create unnecessary risk."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Maybe later."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Not V1."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Option 3 — LangGraph outside, Harness inside"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Something like:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "LangGraph\n    │\n    ├── Research node → Harness Researcher\n    │\n    ├── Strategy node → Harness Strategist\n    │\n    └── Story node → Harness Storyteller"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is also possible because Harness exposes a TypeScript SDK that can launch and drive a Harness runtime through JSON-RPC. fileciteturn15file0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But I don't like it for our system."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The current SDK documentation explicitly lists limitations including no mid-turn cancellation, no prompt-specific result primitive, and incomplete client↔server messaging relevant to things such as approval flows. fileciteturn15file0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "You also end up with:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "LangGraph thread\n      ↓\nHarness session\n      ↓\nHarness agent\n      ↓\nHarness subagents"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "too many lifecycle abstractions."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "It's feasible."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "It's not elegant."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "The Context Compiler stays clean in the hybrid"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is especially important."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Our proprietary Context Compiler remains above both systems."
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Task:\n\"Should we reposition enterprise messaging?\"\n\n              ↓\n\nContext Compiler\n\n              ↓\n\n{\n  positioning,\n  enterpriseICP,\n  objections,\n  customerLanguage,\n  competitorPositions,\n  proof,\n  previousDecisions,\n  relevantPerformance\n}\n\n              ↓\n\nStrategist's LangGraph"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Harness should not determine those facts."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "LangGraph should not retrieve the whole box indiscriminately."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**Our compiler decides the context.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That preserves one of the core pieces of IP we've identified."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "There is a subtle efficiency issue: nested LLM calls"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Imagine Harness's Strategist itself is an LLM agent."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "It thinks:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "I should invoke `strategic_analysis`."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Then LangGraph runs:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "LLM\n→ evidence check\n→ LLM\n→ critic\n→ LLM\n→ recommendation"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Then the Harness agent receives the result and calls another LLM to explain it."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "We've now potentially created:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",

       BRAND BOX API\n                 thin interface we own\n                         │\n                         ▼\n                ┌──────────────────┐\n                │      COGNEE      │\n                  │\n                           ▼\n                     Feed + avatars\n```\n\nThe important part is that we would **not** treat Cognee, Graphiti, Harness and LangGraph as four **Harness = persistent agent runtime**\n> **Our code = marketing intelligence**\n\nThat separation could work very well.\n\n---\n\n# Why Cognee is unusually close to our “box”\n\nRemember what our box was supposed to do:\n\n```text\nraw company information\n        ↓\nentities + relationships\n        ↓\nevidence + provenance\n        ↓\nstructured brand world\n        ↓\nsemantic + relational objects all coexist?”\n\nThat's already infrastructure.\n\n---\n\n# We can define our Brand World directly\n\nThis was the biggest thing I wanted to verify.\n\nCognee lets you define **custom Pydantic actually define:\n\n```text\nCompany\nProduct\nAudience\nProblem\nMotivation\nObjection\nBenefit\nFeature\nClaim\nProof\nCompetitor\nPositioning\nNarrative\nMessage\nCampaign\nCreative\nExperiment\nDecision\n```\n\nas actual typed objects.\n\nAnd:\n\n```text\nProduct ─solves──────→ Problem\n\nAudience ─experiences→ Problem\n\nClaim ─supported_by──→ Proof\n\nPositioning ─targets──→ Audience\n\nPositioning ─differs_from→ Competitor\n\nNarrative ─expresses──→ Positioning\n```\n\nas actual relationships.\n\nThat means **we do not have to build a graph abstraction or entity framework ourselves**.\n\nWe mostly define the marketing semantics.\n\nThat's exactly the kind of work we *should* own.\n\n---\n\n# Even our truth states can be modeled rather than engineered from scratch\n\nWe could create
