confidence\n├── valid_from\n├── valid_to\n├── source_ids\n├── approved_by\n├── approved_at\n└── supersedes\n```\n\nCognee's DataPoints already carry metadata, provenance-oriented context and explicit versioning support; custom fields are ours to define. Version increments are manual via `update_version()`, so I would probably represent important brand decisions as immutable revisions rather than silently mutating an existing object. citeturn138102search8turn281576search1\n\nThis is much less engineering than implementing our own knowledge database.\n\n---\n\n# I would separate “evidence” from “truth”\n\nThis remains important.\n\nI would not allow:\n\n> PDF says X → therefore Brand Core says X.\n\nInstead:\n\n```text\nRAW EVIDENCE\n      │\n      ▼\nCognee extraction\n      │\n      ▼\nObservation / candidate fact\n      │\n      ▼\nour intelligence / human review\n      │\n      ▼\nCONFIRMED BRAND FACT\n```\n\nAnd Cognee can hold both.\n\nConceptually:\n\n```text\nclient_dataset\n\n├── canonical\n│   ├── approved positioning\n│   ├── products\n│   ├── ICP definitions\n│   ├── brand rules\n│   └── decisions\n│\n├── evidence\n│   ├── documents\n│   ├── calls\n│   ├── CRM observations\n│   └── customer quotes\n│\n├── hypotheses\n│\n├── market_signals\n│\n└── history\n```\n\nThis is where our intelligence starts.\n\n---\n\n# Ingestion is largely solved too\n\nThis surprised me.\n\nCognee can already normalize text, files, directories, URLs and Docling-supported formats; its loader system includes PDF, office formats, Unstructured and Docling pathways. It also deduplicates ingested content using hashes. citeturn363896search6turn363896search10\n\nFor SaaS systems, Cognee documents ingestion through `dlt` connectors for sources such as Slack, Notion and GitHub, as well as databases. citeturn363896search3\n\nSo instead of us implementing:\n\n```text\nPDF ingestion\nDOCX ingestion\nweb ingestion\nSlack ingestion\nNotion ingestion\ndatabase ingestion\nchunking\nnormalization\ndeduplication\n```\n\nwe largely get an existing pipeline.\n\nWe still need domain-specific adapters for systems such as HubSpot or particular analytics sources when no suitable connector exists, but those become **source adapters**, not our whole knowledge architecture.\n\n---\n\n# Cognee also already solves much of retrieval\n\nIt exposes multiple retrieval modes:\n\nsemantic chunks, lexical chunks, graph completion, triplet retrieval, graph summaries, natural-language graph queries and temporal retrieval. citeturn138102search1\n\nThat means our Context Compiler does not have to implement:\n\n> vector database search + lexical search + graph traversal + reranking\n\nfrom first principles.\n\nInstead, our compiler can decide:\n\n```text\nThis is a positioning task.\n\nRetrieve:\n\n1. confirmed positioning facts\n2. ICP-related graph neighborhood\n3. recent customer evidence\n4. competitor changes\n5. prior strategic decisions\n```\n\nand then call appropriate retrieval mechanisms underneath.\n\nSo the proprietary thing becomes:\n\n> **what should be retrieved?**\n\nrather than:\n\n> how do I build a graph/vector retrieval engine?\n\nThat's exactly where I want our work concentrated.\n\n---\n\n# And LangGraph already has a Cognee integration\n\nCognee publishes an official `cognee-integration-langgraph` package that exposes memory tools to LangGraph agents with user/session scoping. citeturn288036search1turn872928search1\n\nSo our cognitive graphs could access the box without us inventing a new LangGraph memory layer.\n\nFor example:\n\n```text\nStrategyGraph\n\nidentify tension\n      ↓\nbox.search(customer evidence)\n      ↓\nbox.search(current positioning)\n      ↓\ngenerate hypotheses\n      ↓\nbox.search(competitor evidence)\n      ↓\ncritic\n      ↓\nrecommend\n```\n\nWe may still wrap Cognee's tools in our own domain-specific interface, but that wrapper should be thin.\n\n---\n\n# And Harness can talk to it over MCP\n\nCognee now ships an MCP server supporting HTTP/SSE/stdio, while Harness's MCP client can discover MCP tools and register them into its own tool registry. citeturn872928search2turn506051search2 fileciteturn8file0\n\nSo potentially:\n\n```text\nHarness Researcher\n       │\n       │ MCP\n       ▼\n     Box API\n       │\n       ▼\n     Cognee\n```\n\nNo bespoke transport protocol.\n\nThat's one of the strongest compatibility signals I found.\n\n---\n\n# I would *not* expose raw Cognee directly to the agents\n\nCognee's current MCP interface is deliberately minimal: essentially `remember`, `recall`, and `forget`. citeturn506051search2\n\nFor our product we want semantics like:\n\n```text\nbox.get_entity()\n\nbox.get_related()\n\nbox.get_evidence()\n\nbox.get_current_truth()\n\nbox.get_history()\n\nbox.search_customer_language()\n\nbox.propose_fact()\n\nbox.confirm_fact()\n\nbox.record_decision()\n```\n\nSo I would build a tiny service:\n\n```text\n              OUR BOX API\n\n                   │\n        ┌──────────┴──────────┐\n        ▼                     ▼\n      Cognee               Graphiti\n    general memory        temporal facts\n```\n\nAnd expose **our Box API** over MCP.\n\nThat's an elegant adapter and gives us a stable interface even if we later replace Cognee.\n\n---\n\n# Graphiti becomes much more interesting as an optional subsystem\n\nGraphiti is built specifically around **temporal context graphs**.\n\nIts facts have validity windows, entities evolve, and derived facts retain provenance back to the raw episodes that created them. It supports incremental ingestion plus hybrid semantic/keyword/graph search. citeturn984161search3turn257819search1\n\nThat's extremely useful for things like:\n\n```text\nCompetitor X positioning\n\n2026-02\n\"Enterprise automation\"\n\n2026-06\n\"AI-native operations\"\n\n2026-08\n\"Autonomous workforce\"\n```\n\nor:\n\n```text\nICP preference\n         │\n         ├── old belief\n         ├── new evidence\n         └── current belief\n```\n\nAnd interestingly, Cognee already has a **Graphiti mode**. Its documentation describes a second temporal path where documents become timestamped Graphiti episodes, Graphiti tracks entities/facts over time, and those results can then be indexed into Cognee's vector layer. citeturn257819search0\n\nSo we don't necessarily have to invent the Cognee↔Graphiti integration ourselves.\n\n---\n\n# But I would not make Graphiti the canonical truth database\n\nThere are still edge cases. For example, Graphiti has an open issue concerning temporal versioning of mutable **node attributes**, even though fact/relationship edges have temporal validity semantics. citeturn257819search8\n\nThat reinforces a design I already prefer:\n\nDon't encode important changing brand beliefs as mutable properties like:\n\n```text\nBrand.positioning = \"X\"\n```\n\nInstead encode:\n\n```text\nBrand\n  │\n  └── HAS_POSITIONING\n          │\n          ▼\n      PositioningFact\n      status\n      evidence\n      valid_from\n      valid_to\n```\n\nThat's much more auditable anyway.\n\n---\n\n# Feedback is partly solved too\n\nCognee has a feedback mechanism where retrieval traces can be associated with user feedback and later `improve()` passes adjust the weight of graph elements involved in retrieval. citeturn872928search0turn872928search11\n\nThat aligns almost perfectly with our feed.\n\nFor example:\n\n```text\nStrategist posts insight\n        ↓\nFounder 👍\n        ↓\nretrieval evidence receives positive signal\n```\n\nBut again:\n\n**like = retrieval preference signal**\n\nnot:\n\n**like = canonical truth**\n\nExplicit approval would still be our operation.\n\nCognee has also introduced a \"truth subspace\" built from distilled accepted session learnings for retrieval/reranking, but I would treat that as retrieval infrastructure rather than a replacement for our explicit `CONFIRMED / INFERRED / REJECTED` governance model. citeturn484694search0\n\n---\n\n# Multi-client isolation is already there\n\nCognee has datasets as its primary permission boundary and supports users, tenants, roles, ACLs and dataset-scoped read/write/delete/share permissions. In supported configurations it can physically isolate graph/vector storage by dataset rather than merely relying on a prompt-level tenant ID. citeturn433413search0turn433413search3turn433413search7\n\nThat saves another substantial chunk of infrastructure.\n\nFor our system:\n\n```text\nAcme tenant\n   └── Acme Brand Box\n\nFlora tenant\n   └── Flora Brand Box\n\nClient C tenant\n   └── Client C Brand Box\n```\n\nAgents only get access to the box belonging to their client.\n\n---\n\n# So what would we actually need to build?\n\nAfter this research, I would divide it like this:\n\n| Component | Build? |\n|---|---:|\n| File parsing | No |\n| Chunking | No |\n| embeddings | No |\n| vector DB abstraction | No |\n| graph DB abstraction | No |\n| entity extraction plumbing | Mostly no |\n| relationship extraction plumbing | Mostly no |\n| provenance infrastructure | Mostly no |\n| document ingestion | Mostly no |\n| SaaS connector framework | Mostly no |\n| graph retrieval | No |\n| semantic retrieval | No |\n| lexical retrieval | No |\n| temporal retrieval | Mostly no |\n| user/dataset isolation | Mostly no |\n| MCP transport | No |\n| LangGraph memory integration | No |\n| feedback storage/ranking | Mostly no |\n| **brand ontology** | **Yes** |\n| **truth/governance semantics** | **Yes** |\n| **Context Compiler** | **Yes** |\n| **agent cognitive graphs** | **Yes** |\n| **marketing intelligence algorithms** | **Yes** |\n| **evaluation system** | **Yes** |\n| **feed/product experience** | **Yes** |\n\nThat's a much better workload.\n\n---\n\n# What our custom code could eventually look like\n\nThe box interface might genuinely stay this small:\n\n```text\nBox\n\nread:\n  get(entity)\n  related(entity, relation)\n  search(query, scope)\n  evidence(fact)\n  history(entity)\n\ncontext:\n  compile(agent, task)\n\nwrite:\n  observe(signal)\n  propose(fact)\n  confirm(fact)\n  reject(fact)\n  decide(decision)\n\nfeedback:\n  react(object, signal)\n```\n\nEverything underneath those calls could be infrastructure.\n\nEverything **above** them becomes our intelligence.\n\n---\n\n# Then the full system becomes extremely clean\n\n```text\nDATA SOURCES\n\nwebsite\nCRM\ncalls\ndocs\nSlack\nanalytics\nresearch\nmarket data\n        │\n        ▼\n────────────────────────────\n      COGNEE / GRAPHITI\n          THE BOX\n────────────────────────────\n        │\n        ▼\n    Box API\n        │\n        ▼\n Context Compiler\n        │\n        ▼\n────────────────────────────\n       LANGGRAPH\n   cognitive architectures\n────────────────────────────\n        │\n        ▼\n────────────────────────────\n   DEEPSEEK HARNESS\n persistent agent actors\n────────────────────────────\n        │\n        ▼\n MCP / APIs / computers\n        │\n        ▼\n      WORLD\n\n        ↑\n results / evidence\n        ↑\n\n      FEED UI\n```\n\nThat is very close to the architecture we've been gradually converging on.\n\n---\n\n## Where I would be cautious\n\nCognee is currently marked **Beta**, and the project is developing quickly. Its issue tracker also shows active work around MCP ingestion behavior, Neo4j details and other reliability edges. citeturn281576search4turn506051search0\n\nTherefore I would **not let our application import Cognee types everywhere**.\n\nEverything should go through:\n\n```text\ninterface Box {\n    ...\n}\n```\n\nThen:\n\n```text\nCogneeBox implements Box\n```\n\nIf in two years something better appears:\n\n```text\nNewBox implements Box\n```\n\nNothing above it changes.\n\nSame philosophy we've discussed for Harness.\n\n---\n\n# One important architectural simplification\n\nI would also **not use Cognee's session memory as our agent session**.\n\nWe already have Harness for that.\n\nSo:\n\n```text\nHarness\n= who the agent is\n= conversation\n= current work\n= runtime state\n```\n\nwhile:\n\n```text\nCognee\n= what the company knows\n= what happened historically\n= evidence\n= relationships\n= durable organizational knowledge\n```\n\nAnd:\n\n```text\nLangGraph\n= how the agent thinks\n```\n\nThat removes most framework overlap.\n\n---\n\n# My current preferred stack\n\nI would prototype:\n\n```text\nFrontend\nReact / Next\n        │\n        ▼\nProduct backend\n        │\n        ├── Feed/events\n        ├── Client config\n        └── Box API\n                │\n                ▼\n             Cognee\n         ┌──────┼──────┐\n         ▼      ▼      ▼\n     Postgres  Vector  Graph\n                       │\n                 [Graphiti later]\n\n        │\n        ▼\nContext Compiler\n        │\n        ▼\nLangGraph cognitive graphs\n        │\n        ▼\nDeepSeek Harness\n        │\n        ▼\nMCP / APIs / browser / computer\n```\n\nFor Cognee's backend, its own docs support Postgres for relational state, PGVector for vectors and graph backends including Neo4j; the exact production combination should be load-tested against its multi-tenant support before we commit. citeturn433413search10turn554309search11turn554309search12\n\nI would avoid building infrastructure underneath this unless a real limitation forces us to.\n\n---\n\n# The biggest conclusion from the research\n\nI would update my earlier estimate of the technical difficulty.\n\nOriginally, we were implicitly considering building:\n\n> knowledge architecture + ingestion + graph + retrieval + agents + reasoning + UX.\n\nThere is now credible open-source infrastructure for almost all of the first half.\n\nSo the project can increasingly become:\n\n> **Design the brand ontology.**\n>\n> **Design how truth changes.**\n>\n> **Design how context is selected.**\n>\n> **Encode expert marketing reasoning.**\n>\n> **Design how humans interact with that intelligence.**\n\nThose are exactly the interesting parts.\n\nMy engineering estimate—not a measured fact—is that a Cognee-centered approach could remove roughly **70–85% of the generic “box plumbing”** we were previously assuming we might have to implement.\n\nThe remaining work is still difficult, but importantly, it becomes **domain/intelligence difficulty rather than infrastructure difficulty**.\n\nAnd that is probably where this product can actually develop proprietary value. memcite",
      "blocks": [
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Yes. The deeper I looked, the more I think **we can avoid building most of the generic “box” infrastructure ourselves**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The strongest candidate I found is **Cognee**, with **Graphiti used selectively underneath/alongside it for temporal facts**. Cognee already covers ingestion, relational metadata/provenance, graph storage, vector search, custom typed knowledge models, ontology grounding, temporal retrieval, multi-user isolation, feedback-driven retrieval improvement, an MCP server, and an official LangGraph integration. citeturn554309search6turn872928search4turn433413search4turn288036search1"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That gets surprisingly close to the “box” we designed."
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 2,
          "text": "The stack I would now seriously prototype"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "                         OUR PRODUCT\n────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n                      BRAND BOX API\n                 thin interface we own\n                         │\n                         ▼\n                ┌──────────────────┐\n                │      COGNEE      │\n                │                  │\n                │ ingestion        │\n                │ provenance       │\n                │ graph            │\n                │ vectors          │\n                │ ontology         │\n                │ temporal search  │\n                │ permissions      │\n                │ feedback         │\n                │ retrieval        │\n                └────────┬─────────┘\n                         │\n              optional temporal layer\n                         ▼\n                    GRAPHITI\n              evolving facts/history\n\n────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n                     Context Compiler\n                           │\n                           ▼\n                       LANGGRAPH\n                 cognitive algorithms\n                           │\n                           ▼\n                 DEEPSEEK HARNESS\n             agents / tools / sessions / MCP\n                           │\n                           ▼\n                     Feed + avatars"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The important part is that we would **not** treat Cognee, Graphiti, Harness and LangGraph as four competing agent systems."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Each gets one job:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**Cognee = company knowledge infrastructure**\n**Graphiti = optional temporal/evolving-fact engine**\n**LangGraph = cognitive algorithms**\n**Harness = persistent agent runtime**\n**Our code = marketing intelligence**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That separation could work very well."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Why Cognee is unusually close to our “box”"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Remember what our box was supposed to do:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "raw company information\n        ↓\nentities + relationships\n        ↓\nevidence + provenance\n        ↓\nstructured brand world\n        ↓\nsemantic + relational retrieval\n        ↓\ncontext for agents"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Cognee already has a three-store architecture:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**relational store** for documents, chunks and provenance;\n**vector store** for semantic retrieval;\n**graph store** for entities and relationships. citeturn554309search7turn433413search11"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So we don't need to invent:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "“How should documents, embeddings, metadata and graph objects all coexist?”"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's already infrastructure."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "We can define our Brand World directly"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This was the biggest thing I wanted to verify."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Cognee lets you define **custom Pydantic `DataPoint` types** and insert them directly into the graph, including explicit relationships and fields that should be semantically indexed. citeturn872928search4turn281576search0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So we could actually define:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Company\nProduct\nAudience\nProblem\nMotivation\nObjection\nBenefit\nFeature\nClaim\nProof\nCompetitor\nPositioning\nNarrative\nMessage\nCampaign\nCreative\nExperiment\nDecision"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "as actual typed objects."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "And:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Product ─solves──────→ Problem\n\nAudience ─experiences→ Problem\n\nClaim ─supported_by──→ Proof\n\nPositioning ─targets──→ Audience\n\nPositioning ─differs_from→ Competitor\n\nNarrative ─expresses──→ Positioning"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "as actual relationships."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That means **we do not have to build a graph abstraction or entity framework ourselves**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "We mostly define the marketing semantics."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's exactly the kind of work we *should* own."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Even our truth states can be modeled rather than engineered from scratch"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "We could create something like:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "BrandFact\n├── subject\n├── predicate\n├── object\n├── status\n│    ├── inferred\n│    ├── proposed\n│    ├── confirmed\n│    ├── rejected\n│    └── superseded\n│\n├── confidence\n├── valid_from\n├── valid_to\n├── source_ids\n├── approved_by\n├── approved_at\n└── supersedes"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Cognee's DataPoints already carry metadata, provenance-oriented context and explicit versioning support; custom fields are ours to define. Version increments are manual via `update_version()`, so I would probably represent important brand decisions as immutable revisions rather than silently mutating an existing object. citeturn138102search8turn281576search1"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is much less engineering than implementing our own knowledge database."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "I would separate “evidence” from “truth”"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This remains important."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I would not allow:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "PDF says X → therefore Brand Core says X."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Instead:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "RAW EVIDENCE\n      │\n      ▼\nCognee extraction\n      │\n      ▼\nObservation / candidate fact\n      │\n      ▼\nour intelligence / human review\n      │\n      ▼\nCONFIRMED BRAND FACT"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "And Cognee can hold both."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Conceptually:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "client_dataset\n\n├── canonical\n│   ├── approved positioning\n│   ├── products\n│   ├── ICP definitions\n│   ├── brand rules\n│   └── decisions\n│\n├── evidence\n│   ├── documents\n│   ├── calls\n│   ├── CRM observations\n│   └── customer quotes\n│\n├── hypotheses\n│\n├── market_signals\n│\n└── history"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is where our intelligence starts."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Ingestion is largely solved too"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This surprised me."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Cognee can already normalize text, files, directories, URLs and Docling-supported formats; its loader system includes PDF, office formats, Unstructured and Docling pathways. It also deduplicates ingested content using hashes. citeturn363896search6turn363896search10"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For SaaS systems, Cognee documents ingestion through `dlt` connectors for sources such as Slack, Notion and GitHub, as well as databases. citeturn363896search3"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So instead of us implementing:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "PDF ingestion\nDOCX ingestion\nweb ingestion\nSlack ingestion\nNotion ingestion\ndatabase ingestion\nchunking\nnormalization\ndeduplication"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "we largely get an existing pipeline."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "We still need domain-specific adapters for systems such as HubSpot or particular analytics sources when no suitable connector exists, but those become **source adapters**, not our whole knowledge architecture."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Cognee also already solves much of retrieval"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "It exposes multiple retrieval modes:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "semantic chunks, lexical chunks, graph completion, triplet retrieval, graph summaries, natural-language graph queries and temporal retrieval. citeturn138102search1"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That means our Context Compiler does not have to implement:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "vector database search + lexical search + graph traversal + reranking"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "from first principles."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Instead, our compiler can decide:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "This is a positioning task.\n\nRetrieve:\n\n1. confirmed positioning facts\n2. ICP-related graph neighborhood\n3. recent customer evidence\n4. competitor changes\n5. prior strategic decisions"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "and then call appropriate retrieval mechanisms underneath."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So the proprietary thing becomes:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**what should be retrieved?**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "rather than:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "how do I build a graph/vector retrieval engine?"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's exactly where I want our work concentrated."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "And LangGraph already has a Cognee integration"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Cognee publishes an official `cognee-integration-langgraph` package that exposes memory tools to LangGraph agents with user/session scoping. citeturn288036search1turn872928search1"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So our cognitive graphs could access the box without us inventing a new LangGraph memory layer."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For example:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "StrategyGraph\n\nidentify tension\n      ↓\nbox.search(customer evidence)\n      ↓\nbox.search(current positioning)\n      ↓\ngenerate hypotheses\n      ↓\nbox.search(competitor evidence)\n      ↓\ncritic\n      ↓\nrecommend"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "We may still wrap Cognee's tools in our own domain-specific interface, but that wrapper should be thin."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "And Harness can talk to it over MCP"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Cognee now ships an MCP server supporting HTTP/SSE/stdio, while Harness's MCP client can discover MCP tools and register them into its own tool registry. citeturn872928search2turn506051search2 fileciteturn8file0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So potentially:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Harness Researcher\n       │\n       │ MCP\n       ▼\n     Box API\n       │\n       ▼\n     Cognee"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "No bespoke transport protocol."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's one of the strongest compatibility signals I found."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "I would *not* expose raw Cognee directly to the agents"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Cognee's current MCP interface is deliberately minimal: essentially `remember`, `recall`, and `forget`. citeturn506051search2"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For our product we want semantics like:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "box.get_entity()\n\nbox.get_related()\n\nbox.get_evidence()\n\nbox.get_current_truth()\n\nbox.get_history()\n\nbox.search_customer_language()\n\nbox.propose_fact()\n\nbox.confirm_fact()\n\nbox.record_decision()"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So I would build a tiny service:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "              OUR BOX API\n\n                   │\n        ┌──────────┴──────────┐\n        ▼                     ▼\n      Cognee               Graphiti\n    general memory        temporal facts"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "And expose **our Box API** over MCP."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's an elegant adapter and gives us a stable interface even if we later replace Cognee."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Graphiti becomes much more interesting as an optional subsystem"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Graphiti is built specifically around **temporal context graphs**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Its facts have validity windows, entities evolve, and derived facts retain provenance back to the raw episodes that created them. It supports incremental ingestion plus hybrid semantic/keyword/graph search. citeturn984161search3turn257819search1"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's extremely useful for things like:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Competitor X positioning\n\n2026-02\n\"Enterprise automation\"\n\n2026-06\n\"AI-native operations\"\n\n2026-08\n\"Autonomous workforce\""
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "or:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "ICP preference\n         │\n         ├── old belief\n         ├── new evidence\n         └── current belief"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "And interestingly, Cognee already has a **Graphiti mode**. Its documentation describes a second temporal path where documents become timestamped Graphiti episodes, Graphiti tracks entities/facts over time, and those results can then be indexed into Cognee's vector layer. citeturn257819search0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So we don't necessarily have to invent the Cognee↔Graphiti integration ourselves."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "But I would not make Graphiti the canonical truth database"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "There are still edge cases. For example, Graphiti has an open issue concerning temporal versioning of mutable **node attributes**, even though fact/relationship edges have temporal validity semantics. citeturn257819search8"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That reinforces a design I already prefer:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Don't encode important changing brand beliefs as mutable properties like:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Brand.positioning = \"X\""
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Instead encode:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Brand\n  │\n  └── HAS_POSITIONING\n          │\n          ▼\n      PositioningFact\n      status\n      evidence\n      valid_from\n      valid_to"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's much more auditable anyway."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Feedback is partly solved too"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Cognee has a feedback mechanism where retrieval traces can be associated with user feedback and later `improve()` passes adjust the weight of graph elements involved in retrieval. citeturn872928search0turn872928search11"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That aligns almost perfectly with our feed."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For example:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Strategist posts insight\n        ↓\nFounder 👍\n        ↓\nretrieval evidence receives positive signal"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But again:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**like = retrieval preference signal**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "not:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**like = canonical truth**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Explicit approval would still be our operation."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Cognee has also introduced a \"truth subspace\" built from distilled accepted session learnings for retrieval/reranking, but I would treat that as retrieval infrastructure rather than a replacement for our explicit `CONFIRMED / INFERRED / REJECTED` governance model. citeturn484694search0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Multi-client isolation is already there"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Cognee has datasets as its primary permission boundary and supports users, tenants, roles, ACLs and dataset-scoped read/write/delete/share permissions. In supported configurations it can physically isolate graph/vector storage by dataset rather than merely relying on a prompt-level tenant ID. citeturn433413search0turn433413search3turn433413search7"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That saves another substantial chunk of infrastructure."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For our system:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Acme tenant\n   └── Acme Brand Box\n\nFlora tenant\n   └── Flora Brand Box\n\nClient C tenant\n   └── Client C Brand Box"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Agents only get access to the box belonging to their client."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "So what would we actually need to build?"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "After this research, I would divide it like this:"
        },
        {
          "type": "table",
          "header": [
            "Component",
            "Build?"
          ],
          "rows": [
            [
              "File parsing",
              "No"
            ],
            [
              "Chunking",
              "No"
            ],
            [
              "embeddings",
              "No"
            ],
            [
              "vector DB abstraction",
              "No"
            ],
            [
              "graph DB abstraction",
              "No"
            ],
            [
              "entity extraction plumbing",
              "Mostly no"
            ],
            [
              "relationship extraction plumbing",
              "Mostly no"
            ],
            [
              "provenance infrastructure",
              "Mostly no"
            ],
            [
              "document ingestion",
              "Mostly no"
            ],
            [
              "SaaS connector framework",
              "Mostly no"
            ],
            [
              "graph retrieval",
              "No"
            ],
            [
              "semantic retrieval",
              "No"
            ],
            [
              "lexical retrieval",
              "No"
            ],
            [
              "temporal retrieval",
              "Mostly no"
            ],
            [
              "user/dataset isolation",
              "Mostly no"
            ],
            [
              "MCP transport",
              "No"
            ],
            [
              "LangGraph memory integration",
              "No"
            ],
            [
              "feedback storage/ranking",
              "Mostly no"
            ],
            [
              "**brand ontology**",
              "**Yes**"
            ],
            [
              "**truth/governance semantics**",
              "**Yes**"
            ],
            [
              "**Context Compiler**",
              "**Yes**"
            ],
            [
              "**agent cognitive graphs**",
              "**Yes**"
            ],
            [
              "**marketing intelligence algorithms**",
              "**Yes**"
            ],
            [
              "**evaluation system**",
              "**Yes**"
            ],
            [
              "**feed/product experience**",
              "**Yes**"
            ]
          ]
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's a much better workload."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "What our custom code could eventually look like"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The box interface might genuinely stay this small:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Box\n\nread:\n  get(entity)\n  related(entity, relation)\n  search(query, scope)\n  evidence(fact)\n  history(entity)\n\ncontext:\n  compile(agent, task)\n\nwrite:\n  observe(signal)\n  propose(fact)\n  confirm(fact)\n  reject(fact)\n  decide(decision)\n\nfeedback:\n  react(object, signal)"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Everything underneath those calls could be infrastructure."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Everything **above** them becomes our intelligence."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Then the full system becomes extremely clean"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "DATA SOURCES\n\nwebsite\nCRM\ncalls\ndocs\nSlack\nanalytics\nresearch\nmarket data\n        │\n        ▼\n────────────────────────────\n      COGNEE / GRAPHITI\n          THE BOX\n────────────────────────────\n        │\n        ▼\n    Box API\n        │\n        ▼\n Context Compiler\n        │\n        ▼\n────────────────────────────\n       LANGGRAPH\n   cognitive architectures\n────────────────────────────\n        │\n        ▼\n────────────────────────────\n   DEEPSEEK HARNESS\n persistent agent actors\n────────────────────────────\n        │\n        ▼\n MCP / APIs / computers\n        │\n        ▼\n      WORLD\n\n        ↑\n results / evidence\n        ↑\n\n      FEED UI"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That is very close to the architecture we've been gradually converging on."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 2,
          "text": "Where I would be cautious"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Cognee is currently marked **Beta**, and the project is developing quickly. Its issue tracker also shows active work around MCP ingestion behavior, Neo4j details and other reliability edges. citeturn281576search4turn506051search0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Therefore I would **not let our application import Cognee types everywhere**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Everything should go through:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "interface Box {\n    ...\n}"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Then:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "CogneeBox implements Box"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "If in two years something better appears:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "NewBox implements Box"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Nothing above it changes."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Same philosophy we've discussed for Harness."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "One important architectural simplification"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I would also **not use Cognee's session memory as our agent session**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "We already have Harness for that."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Harness\n= who the agent is\n= conversation\n= current work\n= runtime state"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "while:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Cognee\n= what the company knows\n= what happened historically\n= evidence\n= relationships\n= durable organizational knowledge"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "And:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "LangGraph\n= how the agent thinks"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That removes most framework overlap."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "My current preferred stack"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I would prototype:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Frontend\nReact / Next\n        │\n        ▼\nProduct backend\n        │\n        ├── Feed/events\n        ├── Client config\n        └── Box API\n                │\n                ▼\n             Cognee\n         ┌──────┼──────┐\n         ▼      ▼      ▼\n     Postgres  Vector  Graph\n                       │\n                 [Graphiti later]\n\n        │\n        ▼\nContext Compiler\n        │\n        ▼\nLangGraph cognitive graphs\n        │\n        ▼\nDeepSeek Harness\n        │\n        ▼\nMCP / APIs / browser / computer"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For Cognee's backend, its own docs support Postgres for relational state, PGVector for vectors and graph backends including Neo4j; the exact production combination should be load-tested against its multi-tenant support before we commit. citeturn433413search10turn554309search11turn554309search12"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I would avoid building infrastructure underneath this unless a real limitation forces us to."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "The biggest conclusion from the research"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I would update my earlier estimate of the technical difficulty."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Originally, we were implicitly considering building:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "knowledge architecture + ingestion + graph + retrieval + agents + reasoning + UX."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "There is now credible open-source infrastructure for almost all of the first half."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So the project can increasingly become:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**Design the brand ontology.**\n\n**Design how truth changes.**\n\n**Design how context is selected.**\n\n**Encode expert marketing reasoning.**\n\n**Design how humans interact with that intelligence.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Those are exactly the interesting parts."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "My engineering estimate—not a measured fact—is that a Cognee-centered approach could remove roughly **70–85% of the generic “box plumbing”** we were previously assuming we might have to implement."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The remaining work is still difficult, but importantly, it becomes **domain/intelligence difficulty rather than infrastructure difficulty**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "And that is probably where this product can actually develop proprietary value. memcite"
        }
      ],
      "artifact_refs": []

      "content": "is cognee open source, modular/customizable and free for me to use",
      "blocks": [
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "is cognee open source, modular/customizable and free for me to use"
        }
      ],
      "artifact_refs": []
    },
    {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "**Yes, broadly.** Cognee is unusually suitable for this precisely because it is open-source and designed to be extended.\n\n### 1. Open source: yes\n\nThe core urlCognee repositoryturn0search6 is public and licensed under **Apache License 2.0**. citeturn0search6\n\nThat license generally permits you to:\n\n- use it commercially;\n- self-host it;\n- modify the source;\n- build proprietary software on top of it;\n- distribute modified versions;\n- charge clients for your product/service.\n\nYou need to comply with Apache-2.0's notice/license requirements if you distribute covered code, but **you do not have to open-source your proprietary Brand OS code merely because it uses Cognee**.\n\nSo yes: using Cognee underneath a paid product is compatible with its core license.\n\n### 2. Free: the software is; operating it isn't\n\nYou can self-host the open-source version without paying Cognee a SaaS fee.\n\nBut your actual box still incurs infrastructure costs:\n\n**Cognee:** €0 license\n**Postgres:** hosting cost\n**Neo4j/other graph DB:** potentially hosting/license cost depending on choice\n**embeddings:** API/compute cost\n**LLMs used for extraction:** API/compute cost\n**object storage:** small hosting cost\n**server:** hosting cost\n\nCognee also supports local models through Ollama, so theoretically you could even eliminate much of the model API cost. citeturn0search2\n\nFor our business, I'd probably pay for good models rather than optimize this prematurely.\n\n### 3. Modular: very much so\n\nThis is one of its strongest characteristics.\n\nIts architecture is essentially:\n\n```text\nAPI\n ↓\npipelines\n ↓\ntasks\n ↓\ndomain modules\n ↓\ninfrastructure adapters\n ↓\ndatabases / LLMs / storage\n```\n\nIts pipelines consist of composable tasks, and database implementations sit behind interfaces. citeturn0search2\n\nYou can replace or extend:\n\n```text\nLLM provider\nembedding provider\ngraph database\nvector database\nrelational database\ndocument loaders\nretrievers\nsearch strategies\npipelines\npipeline tasks\ngraph models\nontologies\n```\n\nThere is even a separate community ecosystem explicitly containing custom **pipelines, tasks, retrievers and database adapters**. citeturn0search0\n\nThat's exactly what we want.\n\n### 4. Custom ontology: yes\n\nThis is particularly important for us.\n\nCognee lets us define custom Pydantic `DataPoint` models. citeturn0search1\n\nSo rather than accepting Cognee's generic idea of knowledge, we can define:\n\n```text\nAudience\nPositioning\nNarrative\nClaim\nEvidence\nCompetitor\nCustomerProblem\nMotivation\nObjection\nCampaign\nDecision\nBrandPrinciple\n```\n\nand their relationships.\n\nIt also supports ontology-grounded extraction using OWL ontologies. citeturn0search2\n\nSo **Cognee provides the machinery; we provide the marketing worldview.**\n\nThat's exactly the division I'd want.\n\n### 5. Custom pipelines: yes\n\nWe don't have to accept:\n\n```text\ndocument\n→ Cognee default extraction\n→ graph\n```\n\nWe can create:\n\n```text\ndocument\n ↓\nclassify source\n ↓\nextract marketing entities\n ↓\nextract claims\n ↓\nextract evidence\n ↓\ndetect contradictions\n ↓\nresolve against existing Brand Core\n ↓\nassign confidence\n ↓\ncreate candidate facts\n ↓\nstore\n```\n\nCognee explicitly supports custom sequential task pipelines through `run_custom_pipeline()`. citeturn0search1\n\nThat means our **knowledge intelligence algorithms themselves can live inside/alongside Cognee's infrastructure** without us rebuilding ingestion and storage.\n\n---\n\n## The important distinction\n\nI wouldn't fork Cognee and start modifying its internals heavily.\n\nI'd do:\n\n```text\n                OUR CODE\n\nBrandOntology\nTruthModel\nExtractionAlgorithms\nContextCompiler\nMarketingRetrievers\nDecisionLogic\n        │\n        ▼\n─────────────────────────\n       Box interface\n─────────────────────────\n        │\n        ▼\n       COGNEE\n─────────────────────────\ningestion\npipelines\ngraph abstraction\nvector abstraction\nrelational storage\npermissions\nretrieval infrastructure\nMCP\n─────────────────────────\n```\n\nThat way we're **extending Cognee rather than becoming maintainers of a Cognee fork**.\n\nAnd if Cognee disappears someday:\n\n```text\nCogneeBox\n     ↓\nreplace with\n     ↓\nCustomBox\n```\n\nwithout rewriting our intelligence layer.\n\n## One caution\n\nOpen source doesn't mean risk-free infrastructure.\n\nCognee is moving quickly and has a large active issue/PR surface; for example, there are still experimental areas such as its Postgres graph adapter. citeturn0search8turn0search10\n\nSo I would **pin versions, test upgrades, keep our Box abstraction, and use mature underlying storage backends**.\n\nBut from a licensing and architecture perspective, the answer is unusually favorable:\n\n> **Yes — we can commercially self-host Cognee, customize it extensively, define our own Brand ontology and pipelines, and keep our actual marketing intelligence proprietary.**\n\nThat makes it considerably more attractive for what we're building than a closed managed-memory API would be. memcite",

      "content": "Think of our system as building an **AI company brain**.\n\n### Cognee = builds and maintains the brain\n\nWe give Cognee messy company information:\n\n```text\nWebsite\nSales calls\nStrategy documents\nCRM\nCustomer research\nCampaigns\nCompetitor research\nSlack\nAnalytics\n        ↓\n      COGNEE\n        ↓\nStructured Brand World\n```\n\nCognee handles the boring infrastructure:\n\n**reading documents → extracting information → storing it → connecting related things → making everything searchable.**\n\nInstead of the system just having 5,000 documents, it can understand structures roughly like:\n\n```text\nCustomer\n   ↓ experiences\nProblem\n   ↓ addressed by\nProduct\n   ↓ supports\nPositioning\n\nCompetitor\n   ↓ competes with\nProduct\n\nClaim\n   ↓ supported by\nEvidence\n```\n\nWe define **what these concepts mean** and how our marketing ontology should look. Cognee provides much of the machinery to create, store and retrieve that structure.\n\nSo:\n\n> **Cognee turns messy company information into the structured “box.”**\n\n---\n\n### Graphiti = gives the box a sense of time\n\nGraphiti solves a more specific problem.\n\nCompanies change.\n\nFor example:\n\n```text\nJanuary:\nPrimary ICP = startups\n\nApril:\nCompany decides to move upmarket\n\nAugust:\nPrimary ICP = enterprise\n```\n\nA simple database might overwrite:\n\n`startups → enterprise`\n\nGraphiti is designed to represent evolving facts and their validity over time.\n\nSo the system can understand:\n\n```text\nUSED TO BE\nStartups\n\n      ↓ changed\n\nCURRENTLY\nEnterprise\n```\n\nThis becomes useful for:\n\n- positioning changes\n- competitor changes\n- customer behavior changes\n- strategy changes\n- market developments\n- previous decisions\n- historical campaigns\n\nSo:\n\n> **Cognee gives the brand a brain.**\n>\n> **Graphiti gives that brain memory of how reality changes over time.**\n\nAnd Cognee already has some integration with Graphiti, so we may not need to operate it as a completely separate system.\n\n---\n\n### Then our Context Compiler sits on top\n\nImagine the complete box contains **100,000 pieces of information**.\n\nThe Strategist shouldn't receive all of it.\n\nIf Strategist is answering:\n\n> \"Should we reposition toward enterprise buyers?\"\n\nour Context Compiler asks the box for:\n\n```text\nCurrent positioning\nEnterprise ICP\nCustomer problems\nCustomer language\nRelevant competitors\nPast positioning decisions\nPerformance evidence\nRecent market changes\n```\n\nand gives only that relevant package to the Strategist.\n\nSo:\n\n> **Cognee/Graphiti organize memory.**\n>\n> **Our Context Compiler decides what matters right now.**\n\n---\n\n### Then LangGraph controls HOW the agent thinks\n\nStrategist receives the information.\n\nLangGraph can define its process:\n\n```text\nUnderstand problem\n      ↓\nFind strategic tension\n      ↓\nGenerate hypotheses\n      ↓\nCheck evidence\n      ↓\nCompare alternatives\n      ↓\nCriticize own conclusions\n      ↓\nNeed more evidence?\n   ↙             ↘\n YES              NO\n ↓                 ↓\nResearch more    Decide\n      ↓\nRecommendation\n```\n\nSo:\n\n> **LangGraph = cognitive process.**\n\nDifferent little guys can literally have different thinking processes.\n\n---\n\n### DeepSeek Harness runs the little guys\n\nHarness handles more of the operational side:\n\n> Who is the Researcher?\n\n> What tools can it use?\n\n> What session is it working in?\n\n> Is it currently working?\n\n> Can it access HubSpot?\n\n> Can it call an MCP tool?\n\n> Does this action require approval?\n\n> What happened during its previous run?\n\nSo:\n\n> **Harness = agent runtime / workplace.**\n\n---\n\n# Put everything together\n\n```text\n           COMPANY'S WORLD\n                 │\n                 ▼\n        ┌─────────────────┐\n        │     COGNEE      │\n        │                 │\n        │ organizes       │\n        │ knowledge       │\n        │ relationships   │\n        │ evidence        │\n        └────────┬────────┘\n                 │\n             GRAPHITI\n          understands time\n                 │\n                 ▼\n        ┌─────────────────┐\n        │   OUR CONTEXT   │\n        │    COMPILER     │\n        │                 │\n        │ \"What matters   │\n        │  right now?\"    │\n        └────────┬────────┘\n                 │\n                 ▼\n        ┌─────────────────┐\n        │    LANGGRAPH    │\n        │                 │\n        │ \"How should I   │\n        │  think about    │\n        │  this?\"         │\n        └────────┬────────┘\n                 │\n                 ▼\n        ┌─────────────────┐\n        │     HARNESS     │\n        │                 │\n        │ runs the agent  │\n        │ tools/sessions  │\n        │ permissions     │\n        └────────┬────────┘\n                 │\n                 ▼\n             LITTLE GUY\n                 │\n                 ▼\n               FEED\n```\n\nThe encouraging part is that **most generic infrastructure already exists**.\n\nOur difficult work becomes much more focused:\n\n**1. Define what a brand/company consists of.**\nOur marketing ontology.\n\n**2. Determine what information matters for each problem.**\nContext Compiler.\n\n**3. Encode how excellent marketers actually reason.**\nLangGraph cognitive architectures.\n\n**4. Determine how new evidence changes what the system believes.**\nTruth/learning algorithms.\n\n**5. Turn all of that into the feed + little-guy experience.**\n\nThose five pieces are much closer to the actual intellectual/product value we want to create. memcite",

      "content": "what about giving instructions on how the system should extract and store information?\nshould we use cognee or can define this custom and hook it up to cognee",
      "blocks": [
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "what about giving instructions on how the system should extract and store information?\nshould we use cognee or can define this custom and hook it up to cognee"
        }
      ],
      "artifact_refs": []
    },
    {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "Yes. **I would define the extraction and storage intelligence ourselves and use Cognee as the infrastructure underneath it.**\n\nThat distinction is important.\n\n### Cognee should handle the machinery\n\nCognee can do things like:\n\n> receive document → parse → chunk → run extraction → create graph objects → create embeddings → store provenance → index everything → retrieve later\n\nWe don't want to rebuild that.\n\n### We should define what gets extracted\n\nFor example, when processing a customer interview, **our extraction specification** could say:\n\n```text\nExtract:\n\nCustomer segment\nRole/persona\nProblem\nUnderlying motivation\nDesired outcome\nObjection\nTrigger event\nAlternative currently used\nExact customer language\nProduct perception\nEvidence strength\n```\n\nAnd then specify relationships:\n\n```text\nPersona\n   └─ EXPERIENCES → Problem\n\nProblem\n   └─ CAUSED_BY → Motivation\n\nPersona\n   └─ OBJECTS_TO → Objection\n\nProduct\n   └─ RESOLVES → Problem\n\nQuote\n   └─ EVIDENCE_FOR → Problem\n```\n\nCognee supports custom typed `DataPoint` models and custom pipelines/tasks, so this domain-specific extraction can be defined by us while Cognee handles much of the graph/storage plumbing underneath. urlCognee custom data models documentationhttps://docs.cognee.ai/guides/custom-data-models\n\n### And extraction should depend on the source\n\nThis is something I **wouldn't leave to generic Cognee extraction**.\n\nA sales call should have a different extraction algorithm from a competitor website.\n\nFor example:\n\n```text\nSales call\n→ customer intelligence extractor\n\nFounder interview\n→ brand beliefs + strategy extractor\n\nWebsite\n→ claims + positioning + messaging extractor\n\nCompetitor website\n→ competitor positioning extractor\n\nCRM\n→ customer/segment/commercial signals\n\nAnalytics\n→ behavioral evidence\n\nCampaign results\n→ performance evidence\n```\n\nEach can be its own custom Cognee pipeline or a preprocessing service that writes structured objects into Cognee.\n\n---\n\n## Storage rules should also be ours\n\nWe don't merely want:\n\n> LLM extracted X → X enters Brand Core.\n\nInstead:\n\n```text\nSOURCE\n   ↓\nEXTRACTION\n   ↓\nOBSERVATION\n   ↓\nINTERPRETATION\n   ↓\nCANDIDATE FACT\n   ↓\nvalidation / evidence / human decision\n   ↓\nCANONICAL BRAND KNOWLEDGE\n```\n\nSo if three sales calls mention:\n\n> “Setup takes too long.”\n\nwe shouldn't immediately store:\n\n**Customer problem = setup time.**\n\nWe store three observations with provenance.\n\nOur intelligence layer might then infer:\n\n> `Hypothesis: implementation speed is a significant ICP pain`\n\nwith confidence 0.71.\n\nAfter more evidence or human approval:\n\n> `Confirmed insight: implementation speed is a major buying consideration`\n\nNow it can become canonical knowledge.\n\n**Cognee stores these objects and relationships. Our algorithms decide their epistemic meaning.**\n\n---\n\n## This gives us a clean architecture\n\n```text\nRaw information\n      ↓\nCognee loaders/parsing\n      ↓\nOUR EXTRACTION ALGORITHMS\n      ↓\nOUR BRAND ONTOLOGY\n      ↓\nOUR TRUTH / VALIDATION RULES\n      ↓\nCognee storage\n ├─ graph\n ├─ vectors\n ├─ provenance\n └─ documents\n      ↓\nOUR CONTEXT COMPILER\n      ↓\nAgents\n```\n\nCognee explicitly supports building custom pipelines from tasks rather than requiring its default `cognify` pipeline, so we don't have to accept Cognee's generic extraction behavior. urlCognee custom pipelines documentationhttps://docs.cognee.ai/core-concepts/main-operations/custom-pipelines\n\n### This is actually preferable to Cognee doing everything\n\nBecause **how we turn messy company information into reliable marketing knowledge is potentially one of our most valuable pieces of IP.**\n\nFor instance, over time we might develop a very sophisticated:\n\n**Customer Interview Extractor**\n\nthat knows the difference between:\n\n> stated preference\n> underlying motivation\n> objection\n> symptom\n> actual problem\n> purchase trigger\n> social motivation\n> functional motivation\n> emotional motivation\n\nThat's marketing/consumer-psychology intelligence.\n\nCognee shouldn't determine that for us.\n\nCognee should make it easy for us to **store and connect the result**.\n\nSo I'd think of Cognee less as *the brain* than I described earlier and more accurately as:\n\n> **Cognee = the memory infrastructure of the brain.**\n\nOur **ontology + extraction + truth algorithms + Context Compiler + cognitive graphs** are the actual intelligence.\n\nThat separation gives us much more control while still avoiding the enormous amount of boring infrastructure involved in building a knowledge system from scratch. memcite",

          "text": "Cognee explicitly supports building custom pipelines from tasks rather than requiring its default `cognify` pipeline, so we don't have to accept Cognee's generic extraction behavior. urlCognee custom pipelines documentationhttps://docs.cognee.ai/core-concepts/main-operations/custom-pipelines"

At the simple level you can configure chunk size, overlap, strategy such as paragraph/sentence/code/exact, and chunking engine. citeturn324136search7turn324136search0 At the deeper level, Cognee lets you provide a **custom chunker class**: you inherit from its `Chunker` base and implement the logic that yields `DocumentChunk`s. Cognee lets us assemble our own sequence of Python tasks, and the output of each task becomes the input of the next. Those tasks can be arbitrary sync/async Python callables. citeturn324136search6turn324136search9\n\nSo instead of Cognee's default pipeline, ours could be:\n\n```text\nraw sales call\n      ↓\nOUR  ↓\nOUR truth classifier\n      ↓\nOUR Brand DataPoints\n      ↓\nCognee storage/indexing\n```\n\nCognee's custom pipeline API is specifically intended to let you provide your own │\n                    ▼\n────────────────────────────────────\n                 COGNEE\n────────────────────────────────────\n pipeline/task framework\n graph persistence\n vector indexing\n relational metadata\n database abstractions\n retrieval infrastructure\n permissions/datasets\n────────────────────────────────────\n```\n\nThat is exactly the architecture I would want.\n\nWe control things such as:\n\n> **What counts as an entity?**\n\n> **What should be a node versus an attribute?**\n\n> **Which relationships exist?**\n\n> **How should a sales call be segmented?**\n\n> **What constitutes evidence?**\n\n> **When should two mentions resolve to the same customer problem?**\n\n> **When is something merely an observation versus an accepted fact?**\n\nCognee handles much of the machinery required to store and retrieve whatever structure our algorithms produce. Custom tasks and pipelines are expressly designed to give control over that entire processing workflow. citeturn324136search9\n\n### There's even a useful middle ground\n\nWe don't need to customize everything immediately.\n\nFor example, initially:\n\n```text\nWebsite\n→ Cognee standard paragraph chunker\n\nSales calls\n→ OUR custom conversation chunker\n\nCRM records\n→ no chunking; structured DataPoints\n\nCustomer research\n→ OUR psychology extraction pipeline\n\nStrategy docs\n→ Cognee standard chunks\n   + OUR Brand ontology extraction\n```\n\nThat lets us customize **only where marketing intelligence actually matters**.\n\nAnd we can gradually replace generic steps as we learn.\n\nThat's much better than spending six months building a knowledge-engine framework.\n\n### One qualification\n\n“Exactly define” doesn't mean Cognee disappears entirely. Once we hand it our structured DataPoints, Cognee still owns parts of indexing, persistence, vector storage and graph-database abstraction unless we deliberately replace or access those engines directly.     {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "Not necessarily.\n\nCognee needs **some intelligence layer** for things like extracting entities/relationships and generating embeddings, but that intelligence does **not have to come from a cloud provider API**.\n\nYou have three basic options.\n\n1. **Cloud model APIs** — simplest. For example OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Mistral, Bedrock, OpenRouter, etc. Cognee supports configurable LLM providers and routes many of them through LiteLLM. citeturn906034search0turn906034search8\n\n2. **Your own/local models** — no external API required. Cognee supports Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM and local embedding options like Fastembed. It even documents a fully local, zero-API-key setup. citeturn906034search2turn906034search1\n\n3. **Reuse the host agent's model through MCP sampling** — this is especially interesting for our architecture. If Cognee runs as an MCP server and the host supports MCP `sampling`, Cognee can delegate LLM completions back to the host instead of using its own separate LLM API key. Embeddings still need their own provider/local model. citeturn826867search0turn826867search1\n\nSo conceptually we could have:\n\n```text\nDeepSeek Harness\n      │\n      ├── main agent model\n      │\n      └── MCP\n           ↓\n         Cognee\n           │\n           ├── asks host model for extraction/reasoning\n           └── uses local embedding model\n```\n\nThat would mean potentially **one main model-provider configuration** rather than a separate OpenAI key inside Cognee.\n\nHowever, I would not make Cognee's internal LLM the source of our important intelligence anyway.\n\nFor our system I'd prefer:\n\n```text\nOUR extraction algorithm\n      ↓\nmodel call through our ModelRouter\n      ↓\nstructured Brand entities/facts\n      ↓\nCognee\n      ↓\nstore/index/retrieve\n```\n\nSo instead of Cognee deciding:\n\n> “Use GPT-X to determine the customer's motivation.”\n\nour code says:\n\n> “Run `CustomerInsightExtractor v3` with this schema, these instructions, this model, and these validation rules.”\n\nThen the resulting structured objects go into Cognee.\n\nIn other words:\n\n> **Cognee doesn't need to own the intelligence provider.**\n\nWe can treat Cognee mostly as **knowledge infrastructure** and route the important model calls ourselves.\n\nThat is probably the cleanest design for us because then the same model router can serve:\n\n```text\nLangGraph reasoning\nExtraction algorithms\nContext compilation\nTruth evaluation\nBrand Guardian\nCognee enrichment\n```\n\nrather than having every framework separately configured with its own model provider.\n\nSo the ideal end state could be:\n\n```text\n             OUR MODEL ROUTER\n       OpenAI / DeepSeek / Anthropic\n                  │\n        ┌─────────┼─────────┐\n        ↓         ↓         ↓\n   LangGraph  Extraction  Validators\n        │         │\n        └────┬────┘\n             ↓\n           Cognee\n     storage / graph / search\n```\n\nThat gives us much tighter control over quality, cost and which model is used for which type of intelligence. memcite",
