▼\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│            INGESTION LAYER              │\n│                                         │\n│ generic loaders + our source adapters   │\n└──────────────────┬──────────────────────┘\n                   │\n                   ▼\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                THE BOX                  │\n│                                         │\n│               COGNEE                    │\n│                                         │\n│ documents                               │\n│ chunks                                  │\n│ embeddings                              │\n│ graph                                   │\n│ entities                                │\n│ relationships                           │\n│ provenance                              │\n│ search/indexing                         │\n│ datasets/permissions                    │\n│                                         │\n│       + Graphiti where useful           │\n│         for changing facts/time         │\n└──────────────────┬──────────────────────┘\n                   │\n                   │\n             OUR BOX API\n                   │\n                   ▼\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│          OUR INTELLIGENCE LAYER         │\n│                                         │\n│ Brand Ontology                          │\n│ Extraction Algorithms                   │\n│ Truth / Confidence Logic                │\n│ Contradiction Resolution                │\n│ Context Compiler                        │\n└──────────────────┬──────────────────────┘\n                   │\n                   ▼\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│              LANGGRAPH                  │\n│                                         │\n│ specialist cognitive architectures     │\n│                                         │\n│ Researcher reasoning                    │\n│ Strategist reasoning                    │\n│ Storyteller reasoning                   │\n│ Growth reasoning                        │\n│ Brand Guardian reasoning                │\n└──────────────────┬──────────────────────┘\n                   │\n                   ▼\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│          DEEPSEEK HARNESS               │\n│                                         │\n│ persistent agents                       │\n│ sessions                                │\n│ tools                                   │\n│ permissions                             │\n│ MCP                                     │\n│ approvals                               │\n│ execution                               │\n│ events                                  │\n└──────────────────┬──────────────────────┘\n                   │\n       ┌───────────┴───────────┐\n       ▼                       ▼\n\n External world             OUR PRODUCT\n APIs                       Feed\n CRM                        Little guys\n Ads                        Conversations\n Email                      Decisions\n CMS                        Approvals\n Browser                    History\n\n       │                       │\n       └───────────┬───────────┘\n                   │\n                   ▼\n\n             RESULTS / FEEDBACK\n                   │\n                   ▼\n\n                 BOX\n```\n\nThat's the big picture.\n\n---\n\n# 1. Cognee is the memory infrastructure\n\nCognee shouldn't be our intelligence.\n\nIt is the machinery that makes the company's world manageable.\n\nImagine a client uploads:\n\n```text\n47 sales calls\n3 strategy decks\nwebsite\nCRM export\ncustomer research\ncompetitor sites\ncampaign results\nbrand guidelines\n```\n\nCognee helps us turn that mess into something queryable.\n\nInstead of having:\n\n```text\n/document-018.pdf\n/transcript-027.txt\n/webpage-881.html\n```\n\nwe eventually have concepts like:\n\n```text\nAudience:\nEnterprise Operations Leader\n\nProblem:\nImplementation takes too long\n\nMotivation:\nReduce organizational friction\n\nProduct:\nAcme Platform\n\nClaim:\nLive in under 14 days\n\nEvidence:\nCustomer interview #42\n```\n\nwith relationships:\n\n```text\nAudience\n   │\n experiences\n   ▼\nProblem\n\nProduct\n   │\n solves\n   ▼\nProblem\n\nClaim\n   │\n supported_by\n   ▼\nEvidence\n```\n\nCognee handles much of the difficult storage/search infrastructure underneath this.\n\nBut **we tell Cognee what those concepts are**.\n\n---\n\n# 2. We build the Brand Ontology\n\nThis is one of our core pieces.\n\nIt's our answer to:\n\n> **What actually constitutes the world of a brand/company?**\n\nFor example:\n\n```text\nCompany\nProduct\nAudience\nPersona\nProblem\nNeed\nMotivation\nObjection\nTrigger\nBenefit\nFeature\nProof\nClaim\nCompetitor\nPositioning\nNarrative\nMessage\nOffer\nCampaign\nCreative\nExperiment\nMetric\nDecision\n```\n\nand relationships such as:\n\n```text\nAudience → experiences → Problem\n\nProblem → driven_by → Motivation\n\nProduct → solves → Problem\n\nClaim → supported_by → Proof\n\nPositioning → targets → Audience\n\nPositioning → differentiates_from → Competitor\n\nNarrative → expresses → Positioning\n\nCampaign → communicates → Message\n```\n\nCognee provides graph machinery.\n\n**We provide the marketing model of reality.**\n\nThat's proprietary.\n\n---\n\n# 3. We build the extraction intelligence\n\nCognee can parse/chunk/store.\n\nBut we should determine **what the system looks for**.\n\nA sales call shouldn't be processed like a competitor website.\n\nFor a sales call, our algorithm might look for:\n\n```text\nProblems\nMotivations\nDesired outcomes\nObjections\nBuying triggers\nAlternatives\nPerceived value\nCustomer language\nEmotional drivers\nEvidence strength\n```\n\nFor a competitor website:\n\n```text\nPositioning\nClaims\nAudience\nBenefits\nNarrative\nOffers\nProof\nDifferentiators\nRecent changes\n```\n\nFor analytics:\n\n```text\nObserved behavior\nPerformance changes\nAnomalies\nConversion patterns\nExperiment outcomes\n```\n\nSo we create intelligence modules such as:\n\n```text\nCustomerInterviewExtractor\n\nCompetitorExtractor\n\nPositioningExtractor\n\nCampaignEvidenceExtractor\n\nBrandBeliefExtractor\n```\n\nThose modules can call whatever LLM/model we choose through **our Model Router**.\n\nThen they store structured results through Cognee.\n\n---\n\n# 4. We also decide what is actually true\n\nThis is another major proprietary component.\n\nSuppose one founder interview says:\n\n> Enterprise is our primary customer.\n\nCRM data says:\n\n> 72% of revenue is enterprise.\n\nThe website says:\n\n> Built for companies of every size.\n\nAnd another founder says:\n\n> We're starting to move downmarket.\n\nThe system shouldn't collapse that into:\n\n```text\nICP = enterprise\n```\n\nInstead:\n\n```text\nObservation A\nsource: founder\ndate: March\nconfidence: medium\n\nObservation B\nsource: CRM\ndate: current\nconfidence: high\n\nObservation C\nsource: website\nstatus: public messaging\n\nObservation D\nsource: founder\ndate: August\nstatus: strategic intention\n```\n\nOur truth layer determines things like:\n\n```text\nOBSERVATION\n\nHYPOTHESIS\n\nPROPOSED FACT\n\nCONFIRMED FACT\n\nREJECTED\n\nSUPERSEDED\n```\n\nwith provenance, confidence and time.\n\nCognee can store all of that.\n\n**We define what those states mean and how information moves between them.**\n\nThis could eventually become a major moat.\n\n---\n\n# 5. Graphiti handles “things change”\n\nGraphiti is optional.\n\nIts special purpose is:\n\n> **Remember what was true when.**\n\nFor example:\n\n```text\n2025\nICP = startups\n\n2026 Q1\nICP = mid-market\n\n2026 Q3\nICP = enterprise\n```\n\nInstead of overwriting history, the box can understand evolution.\n\nThis matters for:\n\n```text\npositioning\ncompetitors\nstrategy\ncustomer preferences\ncampaigns\nmarket conditions\nproduct capabilities\n```\n\nCognee already has some temporal functionality and Graphiti integration, so I wouldn't necessarily introduce Graphiti on day one.\n\nThink:\n\n> **Cognee = memory system.**\n>\n> **Graphiti = enhanced temporal memory.**\n\n---\n\n# 6. Our Box API hides all of this\n\nAgents should never care whether we're using Cognee, Graphiti, Neo4j, Postgres or something else.\n\nWe give the rest of our system a tiny interface:\n\n```text\nBox.get(entity)\n\nBox.search(query)\n\nBox.related(entity)\n\nBox.evidence(fact)\n\nBox.history(entity)\n\nBox.observe(...)\n\nBox.propose(...)\n\nBox.confirm(...)\n\nBox.reject(...)\n\nBox.recordDecision(...)\n```\n\nThis is important.\n\nOur code sees:\n\n```text\nBox\n```\n\nnot:\n\n```text\nCognee\n```\n\nSo Cognee stays replaceable infrastructure.\n\n---\n\n# 7. Our Context Compiler is the bridge between memory and intelligence\n\nThe box may eventually contain millions of pieces of information.\n\nAn agent should not receive all of them.\n\nImagine the Strategist receives:\n\n> Should we reposition around implementation speed?\n\nThe Context Compiler determines that it probably needs:\n\n```text\ncurrent positioning\n\nrelevant ICP\n\ncustomer complaints about implementation\n\npurchase motivations\n\nsales objections\n\ncompetitor positioning\n\nexisting implementation claims\n\nproof behind those claims\n\nprevious strategic decisions\n\nrelevant campaign results\n```\n\nIt might compile 100 useful pieces of information from 100,000 available pieces.\n\nThen:\n\n```text\nTHE BOX\n   ↓\nContext Compiler\n   ↓\ncompact ContextPackage\n   ↓\nStrategist\n```\n\nThis is one of our most important algorithms.\n\nCognee tells us:\n\n> what information exists.\n\nOur compiler determines:\n\n> **what information matters right now.**\n\n---\n\n# 8. LangGraph defines how each expert thinks\n\nOnce the Strategist gets the right context, another question begins:\n\n> **What should it do with that information?**\n\nThat's where LangGraph becomes valuable.\n\nWe can encode:\n\n```text\nSTRATEGIST\n\nunderstand objective\n       ↓\nidentify strategic tension\n       ↓\ngenerate competing hypotheses\n       ↓\ncollect supporting evidence\n       ↓\ncollect contradicting evidence\n       ↓\nevaluate differentiation\n       ↓\nevaluate customer relevance\n       ↓\ncritic attack\n       ↓\nconfidence sufficient?\n      / \\\n    no   yes\n    ↓     ↓\nresearch decide\nmore\n```\n\nResearcher gets a completely different graph.\n\nBrand Guardian gets another.\n\nStoryteller another.\n\nSo these agents don't merely have different personalities.\n\nThey have different **cognitive architectures**.\n\nThis is another large part of our IP.\n\n---\n\n# 9. Our Model Router supplies the intelligence\n\nCognee, LangGraph, extraction algorithms and agents may all need LLMs.\n\nI wouldn't let every framework independently decide which model to use.\n\nWe create:\n\n```text\n                 MODEL ROUTER\n\n          ┌──────────┼──────────┐\n          ▼          ▼          ▼\n       OpenAI     Anthropic   DeepSeek\n          ▼          ▼          ▼\n        local / other models etc.\n```\n\nThen our code can specify:\n\n```text\ncheap extraction\n→ Model A\n\ndifficult strategy\n→ Model B\n\nclassification\n→ small fast model\n\ncreative exploration\n→ Model C\n```\n\nThis gives us control over:\n\n```text\nquality\ncost\nlatency\nfallbacks\nprivacy\n```\n\nAgain, frameworks stay replaceable.\n\n---\n\n# 10. Harness makes those brains into persistent little guys\n\nLangGraph says:\n\n> how the Strategist thinks.\n\nHarness says:\n\n> **there is a Strategist.**\n\nHarness handles things like:\n\n```text\nStrategist exists\nStrategist has a session\nStrategist has these tools\nStrategist has these permissions\nStrategist is currently working\nStrategist needs approval\nStrategist called HubSpot\nStrategist's run failed\nStrategist resumed\n```\n\nSo the relationship is:\n\n```text\nHARNESS\n\"Who am I and what can I do?\"\n\n        ↓\n\nLANGGRAPH\n\"How do I think?\"\n\n        ↓\n\nBOX\n\"What do I know?\"\n```\n\nThat's the simplest mental model.\n\n---\n\n# 11. Harness also gives the agents hands\n\nThrough APIs/MCP/tools:\n\n```text\nResearcher\n→ web search\n\nGrowth\n→ analytics\n\nStrategist\n→ Brand Core\n\nCampaign agent\n→ HubSpot\n\nCreative\n→ image/video systems\n\nContent agent\n→ CMS\n```\n\nHarness can manage the execution and permission layer.\n\nWe shouldn't rebuild generic tool-calling infrastructure.\n\nWhat we **do** build are domain-specific tools like:\n\n```text\nbrand.find_customer_evidence()\n\nbrand.compare_positioning()\n\ncampaign.create_experiment()\n\nbrand.propose_decision()\n```\n\nUnderneath those might simply call existing APIs.\n\n---\n\n# 12. Then we build the actual product\n\nThis is the part customers see.\n\nNot LangGraph.\n\nNot Cognee.\n\nNot Harness.\n\nThe experience is:\n\n```text\nResearcher found something.\n\nStrategist has an opinion.\n\nStoryteller created something.\n\nBrand Guardian objects.\n\nGrowth found a result.\n```\n\nAnd those become feed posts.\n\nFor example:\n\n> 🔵 Researcher\n> 14 of the last 23 customer calls mention implementation effort. This theme has increased over the past three months.\n\nThen:\n\n> 🟡 Strategist\n> This may represent a positioning opportunity. Competitors emphasize capability, while customers increasingly care about implementation friction.\n\nThen perhaps:\n\n> 🟣 Storyteller\n> I developed three narrative territories around “time to value.”\n\nThe infrastructure disappears.\n\n---\n\n# 13. The little guys visualize the actual system\n\nThe avatars aren't just decoration.\n\nWe can map real LangGraph/Harness states:\n\n```text\nResearcher\n\nSEARCHING\n→ scanning animation\n\nCOMPARING\n→ objects move side by side\n\nCONNECTING\n→ particles connect\n\nSYNTHESIZING\n→ objects converge\n\nUNCERTAIN\n→ unstable motion\n\nPRESENTING\n→ settles with result\n```\n\nSo the motion becomes a visual language for what the intelligence is actually doing.\n\n---\n\n# 14. The learning loop brings everything back\n\nEventually:\n\n```text\nagent produces recommendation\n        ↓\nhuman approves/rejects/comments\n        ↓\naction happens\n        ↓\nperformance observed\n        ↓\nnew evidence enters box\n        ↓\nbeliefs/hypotheses updated\n        ↓\nfuture agents get better context\n```\n\nBut crucially:\n\n```text\n👍 like\n≠ truth\n```\n\nand:\n\n```text\ncampaign worked\n≠ automatically causal truth\n```\n\nWe build the semantics for how feedback affects confidence, hypotheses, decisions and canonical knowledge.\n\nThat learning logic is another proprietary part.\n\n---\n\n# So what exactly are we building ourselves?\n\nThis is the important distinction.\n\n| Layer | Existing infrastructure | We build |\n|---|---|---|\n| File parsing | Cognee/loaders | almost nothing |\n| Chunk storage | Cognee | custom rules where useful |\n| Vector storage | Cognee/provider | no |\n| Graph infrastructure | Cognee | no |\n| Temporal graph | Graphiti/Cognee | our semantics |\n| Embeddings | existing models | routing/config |\n| Model APIs | existing providers | Model Router |\n| Agent runtime | Harness | thin adapter |\n| Tool runtime | Harness/MCP | domain tools |\n| Workflow engine | LangGraph | **graphs themselves** |\n| Persistence | Cognee/Harness/LangGraph | boundaries/IDs |\n| **Brand ontology** | — | **YES** |\n| **Extraction intelligence** | generic primitives | **YES** |\n| **Truth model** | storage primitives | **YES** |\n| **Contradiction logic** | — | **YES** |\n| **Context Compiler** | retrieval primitives | **YES** |\n| **Marketing reasoning** | LangGraph primitives | **YES** |\n| **Learning algorithms** | — | **YES** |\n| **Evaluations** | libraries may help | **YES** |\n| **Feed semantics** | — | **YES** |\n| **Product UI** | React/etc. | **YES** |\n| **Avatar system** | animation libs | **YES** |\n| **Client configuration** | — | **YES** |\n\nAnd that's exactly where I want the project to land.\n\n---\n\n# A complete example\n\nSuppose tomorrow a new customer interview arrives.\n\n### Step 1 — ingestion\n\n```text\nZoom transcript\n     ↓\nCognee loader\n```\n\n### Step 2 — our extraction\n\nOur Customer Intelligence Extractor finds:\n\n```text\nProblem:\n\"Setup requires too much internal coordination\"\n\nMotivation:\n\"Get value without involving five departments\"\n\nObjection:\n\"Implementation risk\"\n\nQuote:\n\"We just don't have time for another six-month rollout.\"\n```\n\n### Step 3 — store it\n\nCognee stores the source, entities, relationships, embeddings and provenance.\n\nOur truth system labels them initially as:\n\n```text\nobservations\n```\n\nnot facts.\n\n### Step 4 — pattern emerges\n\nThe system notices 17 similar observations.\n\nOur intelligence layer proposes:\n\n```text\nHypothesis:\n\nImplementation friction is becoming\na major purchase criterion for enterprise buyers.\n\nconfidence: 0.78\n```\n\n### Step 5 — feed\n\nResearcher posts:\n\n> I'm seeing a growing implementation-friction pattern across enterprise interviews.\n\n### Step 6 — Strategist is triggered\n\nContext Compiler gathers:\n\n```text\n17 interview observations\ncurrent positioning\ncompetitor positioning\nsales objections\nproduct implementation metrics\nexisting proof\nhistorical positioning decisions\n```\n\n### Step 7 — LangGraph thinks\n\nStrategist:\n\n```text\nhypothesize\n→ challenge\n→ compare competitors\n→ inspect customer evidence\n→ check proof\n→ evaluate alternatives\n→ recommend\n```\n\n### Step 8 — Harness manages it\n\nHarness handles:\n\n```text\nagent session\ntools\nmodel calls\npermissions\nruntime\nevents\n```\n\n### Step 9 — recommendation\n\nFeed:\n\n> 🟡 Strategist\n> We have enough evidence to test implementation speed as a secondary positioning pillar. I would not make it the primary positioning yet.\n\nHuman:\n\n**Approve experiment**\n\n### Step 10 — action\n\nGrowth agent creates an experiment.\n\n### Step 11 — learning\n\nResults return to the box.\n\nNow the company has learned something.\n\nThat's essentially the entire product.\n\n---\n\n# And therefore the project is much smaller than it initially sounds\n\nAt first, “AI Marketing Operating System with a company world model and persistent specialist agents” sounds like we need to invent:\n\n```text\ndatabase architecture\nknowledge graph\nvector DB\ndocument parsing\nagent framework\ntool framework\nworkflow engine\nmemory system\nMCP\nLLM abstraction\netc.\n```\n\nWe don't.\n\nWe can reuse most of that.\n\nWhat we're really building is:\n\n> **A formal model of marketing reality.**\n>\n> **Algorithms that turn messy evidence into that model.**\n>\n> **Algorithms that select the right context.**\n>\n> **Expert cognitive architectures that reason over it.**\n>\n> **A learning system that improves the model over time.**\n>\n> **A beautiful human interface for interacting with that intelligence.**\n\nThat is still ambitious.\n\nBut it's a much better kind of ambitious.\n\nWe're spending engineering effort on **how an exceptional marketer understands a company and makes decisions**, rather than on implementing another vector database wrapper or agent loop.\n\nAnd I think that's the correct architectural north star for the complete project. memcite",

        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Cognee provides graph machinery."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**We provide the marketing model of reality.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's proprietary."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "3. We build the extraction intelligence"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Cognee can parse/chunk/store."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But we should determine **what the system looks for**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "A sales call shouldn't be processed like a competitor website."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For a sales call, our algorithm might look for:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Problems\nMotivations\nDesired outcomes\nObjections\nBuying triggers\nAlternatives\nPerceived value\nCustomer language\nEmotional drivers\nEvidence strength"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For a competitor website:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Positioning\nClaims\nAudience\nBenefits\nNarrative\nOffers\nProof\nDifferentiators\nRecent changes"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For analytics:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Observed behavior\nPerformance changes\nAnomalies\nConversion patterns\nExperiment outcomes"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So we create intelligence modules such as:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "CustomerInterviewExtractor\n\nCompetitorExtractor\n\nPositioningExtractor\n\nCampaignEvidenceExtractor\n\nBrandBeliefExtractor"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Those modules can call whatever LLM/model we choose through **our Model Router**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Then they store structured results through Cognee."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "4. We also decide what is actually true"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is another major proprietary component."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Suppose one founder interview says:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "Enterprise is our primary customer."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "CRM data says:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "72% of revenue is enterprise."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The website says:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "Built for companies of every size."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "And another founder says:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "We're starting to move downmarket."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The system shouldn't collapse that into:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "ICP = enterprise"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Instead:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Observation A\nsource: founder\ndate: March\nconfidence: medium\n\nObservation B\nsource: CRM\ndate: current\nconfidence: high\n\nObservation C\nsource: website\nstatus: public messaging\n\nObservation D\nsource: founder\ndate: August\nstatus: strategic intention"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Our truth layer determines things like:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "OBSERVATION\n\nHYPOTHESIS\n\nPROPOSED FACT\n\nCONFIRMED FACT\n\nREJECTED\n\nSUPERSEDED"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "with provenance, confidence and time."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Cognee can store all of that."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**We define what those states mean and how information moves between them.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This could eventually become a major moat."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "5. Graphiti handles “things change”"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Graphiti is optional."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Its special purpose is:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**Remember what was true when.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For example:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "2025\nICP = startups\n\n2026 Q1\nICP = mid-market\n\n2026 Q3\nICP = enterprise"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Instead of overwriting history, the box can understand evolution."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This matters for:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "positioning\ncompetitors\nstrategy\ncustomer preferences\ncampaigns\nmarket conditions\nproduct capabilities"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Cognee already has some temporal functionality and Graphiti integration, so I wouldn't necessarily introduce Graphiti on day one."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Think:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**Cognee = memory system.**\n\n**Graphiti = enhanced temporal memory.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "6. Our Box API hides all of this"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Agents should never care whether we're using Cognee, Graphiti, Neo4j, Postgres or something else."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "We give the rest of our system a tiny interface:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Box.get(entity)\n\nBox.search(query)\n\nBox.related(entity)\n\nBox.evidence(fact)\n\nBox.history(entity)\n\nBox.observe(...)\n\nBox.propose(...)\n\nBox.confirm(...)\n\nBox.reject(...)\n\nBox.recordDecision(...)"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is important."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Our code sees:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Box"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "not:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Cognee"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So Cognee stays replaceable infrastructure."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "7. Our Context Compiler is the bridge between memory and intelligence"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The box may eventually contain millions of pieces of information."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "An agent should not receive all of them."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Imagine the Strategist receives:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "Should we reposition around implementation speed?"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The Context Compiler determines that it probably needs:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "current positioning\n\nrelevant ICP\n\ncustomer complaints about implementation\n\npurchase motivations\n\nsales objections\n\ncompetitor positioning\n\nexisting implementation claims\n\nproof behind those claims\n\nprevious strategic decisions\n\nrelevant campaign results"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "It might compile 100 useful pieces of information from 100,000 available pieces."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Then:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "THE BOX\n   ↓\nContext Compiler\n   ↓\ncompact ContextPackage\n   ↓\nStrategist"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is one of our most important algorithms."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Cognee tells us:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "what information exists."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Our compiler determines:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**what information matters right now.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "8. LangGraph defines how each expert thinks"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Once the Strategist gets the right context, another question begins:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**What should it do with that information?**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's where LangGraph becomes valuable."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "We can encode:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "STRATEGIST\n\nunderstand objective\n       ↓\nidentify strategic tension\n       ↓\ngenerate competing hypotheses\n       ↓\ncollect supporting evidence\n       ↓\ncollect contradicting evidence\n       ↓\nevaluate differentiation\n       ↓\nevaluate customer relevance\n       ↓\ncritic attack\n       ↓\nconfidence sufficient?\n      / \\\n    no   yes\n    ↓     ↓\nresearch decide\nmore"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Researcher gets a completely different graph."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Brand Guardian gets another."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Storyteller another."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So these agents don't merely have different personalities."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "They have different **cognitive architectures**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is another large part of our IP."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "9. Our Model Router supplies the intelligence"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Cognee, LangGraph, extraction algorithms and agents may all need LLMs."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I wouldn't let every framework independently decide which model to use."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "We create:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "                 MODEL ROUTER\n\n          ┌──────────┼──────────┐\n          ▼          ▼          ▼\n       OpenAI     Anthropic   DeepSeek\n          ▼          ▼          ▼\n        local / other models etc."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Then our code can specify:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "cheap extraction\n→ Model A\n\ndifficult strategy\n→ Model B\n\nclassification\n→ small fast model\n\ncreative exploration\n→ Model C"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This gives us control over:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "quality\ncost\nlatency\nfallbacks\nprivacy"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Again, frameworks stay replaceable."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "10. Harness makes those brains into persistent little guys"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "LangGraph says:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "how the Strategist thinks."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Harness says:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**there is a Strategist.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Harness handles things like:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Strategist exists\nStrategist has a session\nStrategist has these tools\nStrategist has these permissions\nStrategist is currently working\nStrategist needs approval\nStrategist called HubSpot\nStrategist's run failed\nStrategist resumed"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So the relationship is:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "HARNESS\n\"Who am I and what can I do?\"\n\n        ↓\n\nLANGGRAPH\n\"How do I think?\"\n\n        ↓\n\nBOX\n\"What do I know?\""
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's the simplest mental model."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "11. Harness also gives the agents hands"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Through APIs/MCP/tools:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Researcher\n→ web search\n\nGrowth\n→ analytics\n\nStrategist\n→ Brand Core\n\nCampaign agent\n→ HubSpot\n\nCreative\n→ image/video systems\n\nContent agent\n→ CMS"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Harness can manage the execution and permission layer."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "We shouldn't rebuild generic tool-calling infrastructure."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "What we **do** build are domain-specific tools like:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "brand.find_customer_evidence()\n\nbrand.compare_positioning()\n\ncampaign.create_experiment()\n\nbrand.propose_decision()"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Underneath those might simply call existing APIs."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "12. Then we build the actual product"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is the part customers see."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Not LangGraph."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Not Cognee."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Not Harness."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The experience is:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Researcher found something.\n\nStrategist has an opinion.\n\nStoryteller created something.\n\nBrand Guardian objects.\n\nGrowth found a result."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "And those become feed posts."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For example:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "🔵 Researcher\n14 of the last 23 customer calls mention implementation effort. This theme has increased over the past three months."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Then:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "🟡 Strategist\nThis may represent a positioning opportunity. Competitors emphasize capability, while customers increasingly care about implementation friction."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Then perhaps:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "🟣 Storyteller\nI developed three narrative territories around “time to value.”"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The infrastructure disappears."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "13. The little guys visualize the actual system"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The avatars aren't just decoration."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "We can map real LangGraph/Harness states:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Researcher\n\nSEARCHING\n→ scanning animation\n\nCOMPARING\n→ objects move side by side\n\nCONNECTING\n→ particles connect\n\nSYNTHESIZING\n→ objects converge\n\nUNCERTAIN\n→ unstable motion\n\nPRESENTING\n→ settles with result"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So the motion becomes a visual language for what the intelligence is actually doing."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "14. The learning loop brings everything back"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Eventually:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "agent produces recommendation\n        ↓\nhuman approves/rejects/comments\n        ↓\naction happens\n        ↓\nperformance observed\n        ↓\nnew evidence enters box\n        ↓\nbeliefs/hypotheses updated\n        ↓\nfuture agents get better context"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But crucially:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "👍 like\n≠ truth"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "and:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "campaign worked\n≠ automatically causal truth"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "We build the semantics for how feedback affects confidence, hypotheses, decisions and canonical knowledge."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That learning logic is another proprietary part."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "So what exactly are we building ourselves?"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is the important distinction."
        },
        {
          "type": "table",
          "header": [
            "Layer",
            "Existing infrastructure",
            "We build"
          ],
          "rows": [
            [
              "File parsing",
              "Cognee/loaders",
              "almost nothing"
            ],
            [
              "Chunk storage",
              "Cognee",
              "custom rules where useful"
            ],
            [
              "Vector storage",
              "Cognee/provider",
              "no"
            ],
            [
              "Graph infrastructure",
              "Cognee",
              "no"
            ],
            [
              "Temporal graph",
              "Graphiti/Cognee",
              "our semantics"
            ],
            [
              "Embeddings",
              "existing models",
              "routing/config"
            ],
            [
              "Model APIs",
              "existing providers",
              "Model Router"
            ],
            [
              "Agent runtime",
              "Harness",
              "thin adapter"
            ],
            [
              "Tool runtime",
              "Harness/MCP",
              "domain tools"
            ],
            [
              "Workflow engine",
              "LangGraph",
              "**graphs themselves**"
            ],
            [
              "Persistence",
              "Cognee/Harness/LangGraph",
              "boundaries/IDs"
            ],
            [
              "**Brand ontology**",
              "—",
              "**YES**"
            ],
            [
              "**Extraction intelligence**",
              "generic primitives",
              "**YES**"
            ],
            [
              "**Truth model**",
              "storage primitives",
              "**YES**"
            ],
            [
              "**Contradiction logic**",
              "—",
              "**YES**"
            ],
            [
              "**Context Compiler**",
              "retrieval primitives",
              "**YES**"
            ],
            [
              "**Marketing reasoning**",
              "LangGraph primitives",
              "**YES**"
            ],
            [
              "**Learning algorithms**",
              "—",
              "**YES**"
            ],
            [
              "**Evaluations**",
              "libraries may help",
              "**YES**"
            ],
            [
              "**Feed semantics**",
              "—",
              "**YES**"
            ],
            [
              "**Product UI**",
              "React/etc.",
              "**YES**"
            ],
            [
              "**Avatar system**",
              "animation libs",
              "**YES**"
            ],
            [
              "**Client configuration**",
              "—",
              "**YES**"
            ]
          ]
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "And that's exactly where I want the project to land."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "A complete example"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Suppose tomorrow a new customer interview arrives."
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 3,
          "text": "Step 1 — ingestion"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Zoom transcript\n     ↓\nCognee loader"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 3,
          "text": "Step 2 — our extraction"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Our Customer Intelligence Extractor finds:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Problem:\n\"Setup requires too much internal coordination\"\n\nMotivation:\n\"Get value without involving five departments\"\n\nObjection:\n\"Implementation risk\"\n\nQuote:\n\"We just don't have time for another six-month rollout.\""
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 3,
          "text": "Step 3 — store it"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Cognee stores the source, entities, relationships, embeddings and provenance."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Our truth system labels them initially as:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "observations"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "not facts."
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 3,
          "text": "Step 4 — pattern emerges"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The system notices 17 similar observations."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Our intelligence layer proposes:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Hypothesis:\n\nImplementation friction is becoming\na major purchase criterion for enterprise buyers.\n\nconfidence: 0.78"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 3,
          "text": "Step 5 — feed"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Researcher posts:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "I'm seeing a growing implementation-friction pattern across enterprise interviews."
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 3,
          "text": "Step 6 — Strategist is triggered"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Context Compiler gathers:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",

mention\nimplementation friction\n\n        │ evidenced_by\n        ▼\n\nObservations\n\n        │ source\n        ▼\n\nActual customer quotes\n```\n\nThis is **much better than repeatedly summarizing I researched the remaining gaps against the architecture we’ve been building, and there are **a few more pieces I would reuse rather than build**.\n\nThe biggest finding is that we are missing one important layer in our current picture: **the box should probably have two kinds of memory, not one**.\n\nCognee is excellent for *semantic company knowledge*—brand facts, customer insights, evidence, relationships, positioning, narratives, documents. But campaign spend, conversion rates, CRM tables, daily traffic, funnel events, cohort data, etc. are fundamentally **analytical data**, and we should not force all of that into a knowledge graph.\n\nWith that correction, I think we can get quite close to a system where most of our engineering is indeed concentrated on intelligence.\n\n## The stack I would now aim toward\n\n```text\n                         CLIENT WORLD\n───────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n HubSpot   Slack   GA   Ads   Notion   CRM   etc.\n    │\n    ▼\n  NANGO\n OAuth / syncing / API access / credentials\n    │\n    ├───────────────────────────────┐\n    ▼                               ▼\nKNOWLEDGE DATA                  NUMERIC DATA\ndocs / calls / research         spend / events / CRM\nbrand / competitors             conversions / metrics\n    │                               │\n    ▼                               ▼\n  COGNEE                         DUCKDB\n    │                         / client warehouse\n    │                               │\n    └───────────────┬───────────────┘\n                    ▼\n                  BOX API\n                    │\n        ┌───────────┴───────────┐\n        │                       │\n        ▼                       ▼\n   Brand knowledge          Analytics\n   evidence                 metrics\n   relationships            calculations\n   history                  experiments\n        │                       │\n        └───────────┬───────────┘\n                    ▼\n            CONTEXT COMPILER\n                  [OURS]\n                    │\n                    ▼\n                LANGGRAPH\n          expert reasoning algorithms\n                  [OURS]\n                    │\n                    ▼\n            DEEPSEEK HARNESS\n           persistent little guys\n                    │\n                    ▼\n             tools / actions\n                    │\n                  NANGO\n                    │\n                    ▼\n          HubSpot / Ads / CMS etc.\n\n       CROSS-CUTTING INFRASTRUCTURE\n\n LiteLLM ─── model gateway\n Langfuse ── traces / evals / datasets\n Ragas ───── retrieval evaluation\n DSPy ────── algorithm optimization\n Trigger ─── background product jobs\n```\n\nThere are four additions I think are particularly important.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Nango could remove most of our integration work\n\nThis one is a **very strong fit**.\n\nEventually every client will say:\n\n> Connect our HubSpot.\n\n> Connect Google Analytics.\n\n> Connect Meta.\n\n> Connect Notion.\n\n> Connect Slack.\n\n> Connect our CRM.\n\nThe annoying part isn't usually calling an API. It's OAuth, token refresh, credential storage, rate limits, pagination, syncing, retries, webhooks, tenant isolation and keeping everything working when providers change.\n\nNango is explicitly built to handle that integration layer. Its current docs say it supports 700+ APIs and handles authentication, credential management, execution, retries, rate limits, observability, environments and tenant isolation. It can expose integration functions through APIs, SDKs or MCP, and supports keeping external data synchronized. citeturn975422search6turn975422search1\n\nSo instead of:\n\n```text\nOUR CODE\n\nHubSpot OAuth\nHubSpot refresh tokens\nHubSpot pagination\nHubSpot sync logic\n\nSlack OAuth\nSlack refresh\nSlack sync\n\nGoogle OAuth\nGoogle refresh\nGoogle sync\n\nMeta auth\nMeta token handling\n...\n```\n\nwe get:\n\n```text\n             NANGO\n\nHubSpot ──────┐\nSlack ────────┤\nGoogle ───────┼──→ our normalized adapters\nMeta ─────────┤\nNotion ───────┤\netc. ─────────┘\n```\n\nThen **we only write the interesting mapping**:\n\n```text\nHubSpotContact\n      ↓\nour interpretation\n      ↓\nCustomer / Audience / Revenue signal\n```\n\nNango also handles both directions, which is valuable because later Harness agents can use the same integration infrastructure to **act** rather than merely ingest data. citeturn565791search8turn565791search0\n\nSo I would probably add Nango.\n\n---\n\n## 2. LiteLLM should probably become our Model Router\n\nWe've kept talking about building a `ModelRouter`.\n\nI don't think we need to build most of it.\n\nLiteLLM already provides a central OpenAI-compatible gateway across 100+ model providers, with provider normalization, retries, fallbacks, routing, cost tracking, budgets, authentication and rate limiting. citeturn121825search6\n\nSo:\n\n```text\n                 OUR SYSTEM\n                     │\n                     ▼\n                  LiteLLM\n                     │\n       ┌─────────────┼──────────────┐\n       ▼             ▼              ▼\n     OpenAI       Anthropic      DeepSeek\n       │             │              │\n     Gemini       Mistral         local\n```\n\nOur code only says:\n\n```text\nmodel_role = \"cheap_extraction\"\n```\n\nor:\n\n```text\nmodel_role = \"deep_strategy\"\n```\n\nand our small configuration maps that to actual models.\n\nFor example:\n\n```text\ncustomer_extraction\n→ cheap structured-output model\n\nstrategic synthesis\n→ strongest reasoning model\n\ncreative exploration\n→ creative model\n\nclassification\n→ tiny fast model\n```\n\nLiteLLM handles much of the provider plumbing underneath. citeturn121825search6\n\nThis is another piece I would **not build ourselves**.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Langfuse could become our AI laboratory\n\nThis one is potentially extremely important.\n\nIf we are going to spend most of our time developing intelligence algorithms, we need to answer:\n\n> Did Strategist v17 actually become better than Strategist v16?\n\n> Did the new Context Compiler improve results?\n\n> Is CustomerExtractor v8 missing fewer motivations?\n\n> Which model gives us the best quality/cost ratio?\n\n> Why did this particular agent make a bad recommendation?\n\nBuilding that evaluation infrastructure ourselves would be a mistake.\n\nLangfuse is an open-source/self-hostable AI engineering platform combining tracing, prompt management, datasets, experiments, human feedback and automated evaluations. Its LangGraph integration can automatically trace graph execution, nested agents and scores, while its OpenTelemetry foundation lets us instrument custom systems too. citeturn121825search1turn297390search1turn297390search8\n\nImagine:\n\n```text\nStrategist v12\n────────────────\n\nStrategic relevance     8.4\nEvidence grounding      9.1\nDifferentiation         6.8\nBrand coherence         9.0\nCost                    €0.19\nLatency                 12.4 sec\n\nStrategist v13\n────────────────\n\nStrategic relevance     9.0 ↑\nEvidence grounding      9.2 ↑\nDifferentiation         8.1 ↑\nBrand coherence         8.9\nCost                    €0.17 ↓\nLatency                 10.2 sec ↓\n```\n\nThat's the development environment we want.\n\nLangfuse supports deterministic code evaluators, model judges, datasets, experiments, manual annotation and production feedback. citeturn121825search10turn121825search12\n\nSo I'd treat:\n\n> **Langfuse = laboratory for our intelligence.**\n\nVery strong addition.\n\n---\n\n## 4. DuckDB fills a missing part of the box\n\nThis is the architectural correction I mentioned.\n\nSuppose Growth asks:\n\n> Which audience had the highest CAC-adjusted LTV during the last six months?\n\nThat's not really a Cognee knowledge-graph problem.\n\nIt's SQL.\n\nSimilarly:\n\n```text\nAd spend\nConversions\nRevenue\nCTR\nCAC\nLTV\nTraffic\nCohorts\nFunnel stages\nExperiment results\nCRM records\n```\n\nshould remain structured/numeric.\n\nI'd therefore give the Box a small **analytics plane**.\n\nDuckDB is attractive because it can directly query things like Parquet files, object storage and Postgres rather than forcing us to build a large warehouse immediately. Its Postgres extension can query attached PostgreSQL databases directly, and it can query Parquet stored in S3-compatible storage. citeturn734296search2turn734296search11\n\nSo:\n\n```text\n             THE BOX\n\n     ┌─────────┴─────────┐\n     ▼                   ▼\n\n KNOWLEDGE            ANALYTICS\n  Cognee               DuckDB\n\n \"Customers care      CAC = €432\n  about speed\"        CVR = 4.7%\n\n Positioning          revenue\n Evidence             funnel\n Narratives           cohorts\n Quotes               experiments\n Competitors          metrics\n```\n\nAnd the Context Compiler can combine them.\n\nFor example:\n\n```text\nStrategist asks:\n\n\"Is implementation speed\na meaningful positioning opportunity?\"\n\n             ↓\n\nKnowledge side:\n18 customer interviews mention it\n\n             +\n\nAnalytics side:\ncampaigns emphasizing speed\nconverted 31% better\n\n             +\n\nBrand side:\nwe actually have proof for\n14-day implementation\n\n             ↓\n\nContext Compiler\n```\n\nThat's dramatically better than trying to stuff everything into one graph.\n\nAt very high scale we could later replace/augment DuckDB with something like ClickHouse, which is specifically designed for high-volume analytical workloads. citeturn734296search7\n\nBut I would **not start with ClickHouse**.\n\n---\n\n# Then there are two tools that could improve our intelligence itself\n\nThese are more interesting than infrastructure.\n\n## DSPy could help us optimize the algorithms\n\nThis might eventually be one of the most valuable additions.\n\nDSPy lets you define LLM operations as typed input/output programs and then **optimize them against an evaluation metric and training examples**, rather than manually tweaking prompts forever. citeturn382325search0\n\nImagine our customer extractor:\n\n```text\nINPUT\n\nsales-call segment\n\n      ↓\n\nCustomerInsightExtractor\n\n      ↓\n\nOUTPUT\n\nproblem\nmotivation\nobjection\ntrigger\ndesired_outcome\nevidence\nconfidence\n```\n\nInitially we write it.\n\nThen we collect 500 examples where we've manually judged what the correct extraction should have been.\n\nDSPy can optimize the LLM program against our score.\n\nConceptually:\n\n```text\nour extractor\n     ↓\n500 examples\n     ↓\nour quality metric\n     ↓\nDSPy optimizer\n     ↓\nbetter extractor\n```\n\nDSPy's current optimization model explicitly works this way: define a program, examples and a scoring metric, then compile/optimize the program. citeturn382325search0\n\nThis could apply to:\n\n```text\nCustomerInsightExtractor\nCompetitorExtractor\nContextQueryGenerator\nHypothesisGenerator\nEvidenceEvaluator\nStrategicCritic\nNarrativeEvaluator\n```\n\nSo LangGraph and DSPy have different roles:\n\n```text\nLANGGRAPH\n\ndefines:\nHOW THE THINKING PROCESS FLOWS\n\nDSPy\n\noptimizes:\nHOW WELL INDIVIDUAL THINKING OPERATIONS WORK\n```\n\nThat's potentially powerful.\n\nI would introduce DSPy **after we have evaluation datasets**, not before.\n\n---\n\n# Ragas could specifically help us improve the Context Compiler\n\nLangfuse gives us the general evaluation environment.\n\nRagas gives us useful retrieval-specific metrics.\n\nFor example, **context precision** measures whether relevant information is ranked ahead of irrelevant information, while **context recall** measures whether our retrieval failed to include important evidence. Ragas also includes metrics for things like noise sensitivity, faithfulness and agent/tool behavior. citeturn174243search0turn174243search2turn174243search3\n\nThat maps almost perfectly to our Context Compiler.\n\nWe could test:\n\n```text\nQuestion:\n\n\"Should Acme emphasize speed\nin enterprise positioning?\"\n```\n\nHuman expert says the ideal context contains:\n\n```text\nA\nB\nC\nD\nE\n```\n\nCompiler v1 returns:\n\n```text\nA\nB\nD\nX\nY\n```\n\nCompiler v2 returns:\n\n```text\nA\nB\nC\nD\nE\n```\n\nNow we can objectively improve retrieval rather than saying:\n\n> “v2 feels smarter.”\n\nRagas already documents integration with Langfuse, so scores can be attached to the traces we're already collecting. citeturn174243search1\n\nThat combination is very attractive:\n\n```text\nContext Compiler\n      ↓\nRagas evaluates retrieval\n      ↓\nLangfuse stores experiments\n      ↓\nDSPy/our algorithms improve it\n```\n\nThis creates an actual **intelligence-development loop**.\n\n---\n\n# Background processing is another thing we shouldn't build\n\nEventually there will be lots of:\n\n```text\nsync CRM every hour\n\nreprocess 3,000 interviews\n\nupdate competitor research\n\ngenerate nightly summaries\n\nrebuild abstraction indexes\n\nrun evaluation suite\n\nprocess uploaded documents\n```\n\nThose jobs need queues, retries, durability, concurrency limits, scheduling and progress reporting.\n\nTrigger.dev already provides durable TypeScript background tasks, retries, queues, schedules and real-time frontend status updates, and can be cloud-hosted or self-hosted. citeturn121825search2turn121825search15turn121825search14\n\nBut I would not add it immediately.\n\nHarness already handles agent work.\n\nNango handles integration sync work.\n\nIf we start accumulating lots of **non-agent application jobs**, then add Trigger.\n\nSo:\n\n```text\nHarness\n= agents working\n\nNango\n= external integrations syncing\n\nTrigger\n= miscellaneous durable backend jobs\n```\n\nNo overlap if we keep those boundaries.\n\n---\n\n# Two things I'd postpone\n\n**OpenFGA** is interesting if our permissions become complex—e.g. one agency employee can see Brand A but not Brand B, freelancers can access campaigns but not customer evidence, clients can share selected objects, and agents have their own resource permissions. OpenFGA provides relationship-based authorization around users, objects and relations. citeturn565791search13turn565791search12\n\nBut for an early managed product, standard tenant roles plus Cognee dataset isolation and Harness tool scopes should probably suffice.\n\nSimilarly, **Infisical** is a strong secrets-management option for API keys, database credentials and machine identities, with centralized versioned secrets and fine-grained access control. citeturn307454search1turn307454search7\n\nBut Nango already handles customer OAuth credentials, so I wouldn't add Infisical until our own infrastructure secrets become complicated.\n\n---\n\n# And I would use PostHog for our product, not the box\n\nWe'll want to know:\n\n> Do clients actually read Researcher posts?\n\n> What percentage of recommendations get approved?\n\n> Which agents get chatted with?\n\n> Do users drill from insight → evidence?\n\n> Does the avatar activity help or distract?\n\nPostHog currently combines product analytics, session replay, feature flags, experiments, surveys and related product-development tooling. citeturn112775search3\n\nThat's useful for improving **our UI/product**.\n\nI wouldn't make PostHog part of the core Brand Box.\n\n---\n\n# So the architecture becomes surprisingly complete\n\n```text\n                          DATA SOURCES\n                               │\n                     ┌─────────┴─────────┐\n                     │                   │\n                   NANGO              Files/Web\n                     │                   │\n                     └─────────┬─────────┘\n                               ▼\n\n                           THE BOX\n                 ┌─────────────┴─────────────┐\n                 │                           │\n              COGNEE                      DUCKDB\n        semantic knowledge              analytics\n        graph/evidence/time              metrics\n                 │                           │\n                 └─────────────┬─────────────┘\n                               │\n                          OUR BOX API\n                               │\n                               ▼\n                     OUR CONTEXT COMPILER\n                               │\n                               ▼\n                          LANGGRAPH\n                    cognitive architectures\n                               │\n                               ▼\n                    DEEPSEEK HARNESS\n                    persistent agent actors\n                               │\n                               ▼\n                            NANGO\n                      actions in real tools\n                               │\n                               ▼\n                         EXTERNAL WORLD\n\n──────────────── CROSS-CUTTING ────────────────\n\nLiteLLM\nmodel gateway\n\nLangfuse\ntraces / datasets / experiments / evals\n\nRagas\nretrieval & Context Compiler evaluation\n\nDSPy\noptimization of intelligence modules\n\nTrigger.dev\nbackground jobs when needed\n\nPostHog\nour product analytics\n```\n\n## And then what do we actually build?\n\nThis is now the interesting part.\n\nWe build approximately:\n\n```text\nOUR IP\n────────────────────────────────\n\nBrand Ontology\n\nSource Interpretation Rules\n\nExtraction Algorithms\n\nEvidence Model\n\nTruth / Confidence Model\n\nContradiction Resolution\n\nProgressive Abstraction Model\n\nContext Compiler\n\nCustomer Intelligence Algorithms\n\nResearch Algorithms\n\nStrategic Reasoning Algorithms\n\nNarrative Algorithms\n\nGrowth Algorithms\n\nBrand Guardian Algorithms\n\nLearning / Feedback Semantics\n\nDomain-specific agent tools\n\nFeed semantics\n\nLittle-guy UX\n```\n\nEverything else should be treated as infrastructure wherever practical.\n\nThere is still real engineering around tenant configuration, schema migrations, security, adapters, tests and product deployment, so I wouldn't say **literally** “all we'll write is intelligence.” But it gets much closer.\n\n---\n\n# The piece I now find most interesting\n\nWith this stack, we could create a **closed improvement loop for the intelligence itself**:\n\n```text\n                REAL CLIENT WORK\n                      │\n                      ▼\n               Langfuse traces\n                      │\n           humans score / correct\n                      │\n                      ▼\n               evaluation dataset\n                      │\n          ┌───────────┴────────────┐\n          ▼                        ▼\n       Ragas                     our metrics\n retrieval quality          marketing quality\n          │                        │\n          └───────────┬────────────┘\n                      ▼\n                 DSPy / us\n              optimize algorithms\n                      │\n                      ▼\n            new reasoning version\n                      │\n                      ▼\n                A/B evaluation\n                      │\n                      ▼\n               better system\n```\n\nThat changes the development problem from:\n\n> **“How do I build an enormous AI platform?”**\n\ninto:\n\n> **“How do I encode, measure and continuously improve exceptional marketing intelligence?”**\n\nThat is a much more attractive problem for us to own.\n\nAnd if I were simplifying aggressively, my **core reusable stack** would now be:\n\n**Cognee + DuckDB + Nango + LiteLLM + LangGraph + Harness + Langfuse.**\n\nI'd regard **Graphiti, Ragas, DSPy, Trigger.dev, OpenFGA, Infisical and PostHog as selective additions** when their specific need appears rather than installing the entire zoo on day one.\n\nThat distinction matters. Reusing infrastructure should make the architecture simpler—not turn the product into a fragile pile of fifteen frameworks. memcite",

          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Yes. I researched the remaining gaps against the architecture we’ve been building, and there are **a few more pieces I would reuse rather than build**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The biggest finding is that we are missing one important layer in our current picture: **the box should probably have two kinds of memory, not one**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Cognee is excellent for *semantic company knowledge*—brand facts, customer insights, evidence, relationships, positioning, narratives, documents. But campaign spend, conversion rates, CRM tables, daily traffic, funnel events, cohort data, etc. are fundamentally **analytical data**, and we should not force all of that into a knowledge graph."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "With that correction, I think we can get quite close to a system where most of our engineering is indeed concentrated on intelligence."
