        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "Did the new Context Compiler improve results?"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "Is CustomerExtractor v8 missing fewer motivations?"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "Which model gives us the best quality/cost ratio?"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "Why did this particular agent make a bad recommendation?"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Building that evaluation infrastructure ourselves would be a mistake."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Langfuse is an open-source/self-hostable AI engineering platform combining tracing, prompt management, datasets, experiments, human feedback and automated evaluations. Its LangGraph integration can automatically trace graph execution, nested agents and scores, while its OpenTelemetry foundation lets us instrument custom systems too. citeturn121825search1turn297390search1turn297390search8"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Imagine:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Strategist v12\n────────────────\n\nStrategic relevance     8.4\nEvidence grounding      9.1\nDifferentiation         6.8\nBrand coherence         9.0\nCost                    €0.19\nLatency                 12.4 sec\n\nStrategist v13\n────────────────\n\nStrategic relevance     9.0 ↑\nEvidence grounding      9.2 ↑\nDifferentiation         8.1 ↑\nBrand coherence         8.9\nCost                    €0.17 ↓\nLatency                 10.2 sec ↓"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's the development environment we want."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Langfuse supports deterministic code evaluators, model judges, datasets, experiments, manual annotation and production feedback. citeturn121825search10turn121825search12"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So I'd treat:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**Langfuse = laboratory for our intelligence.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Very strong addition."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 2,
          "text": "4. DuckDB fills a missing part of the box"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is the architectural correction I mentioned."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Suppose Growth asks:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "Which audience had the highest CAC-adjusted LTV during the last six months?"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's not really a Cognee knowledge-graph problem."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "It's SQL."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Similarly:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Ad spend\nConversions\nRevenue\nCTR\nCAC\nLTV\nTraffic\nCohorts\nFunnel stages\nExperiment results\nCRM records"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "should remain structured/numeric."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I'd therefore give the Box a small **analytics plane**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "DuckDB is attractive because it can directly query things like Parquet files, object storage and Postgres rather than forcing us to build a large warehouse immediately. Its Postgres extension can query attached PostgreSQL databases directly, and it can query Parquet stored in S3-compatible storage. citeturn734296search2turn734296search11"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "             THE BOX\n\n     ┌─────────┴─────────┐\n     ▼                   ▼\n\n KNOWLEDGE            ANALYTICS\n  Cognee               DuckDB\n\n \"Customers care      CAC = €432\n  about speed\"        CVR = 4.7%\n\n Positioning          revenue\n Evidence             funnel\n Narratives           cohorts\n Quotes               experiments\n Competitors          metrics"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "And the Context Compiler can combine them."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For example:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Strategist asks:\n\n\"Is implementation speed\na meaningful positioning opportunity?\"\n\n             ↓\n\nKnowledge side:\n18 customer interviews mention it\n\n             +\n\nAnalytics side:\ncampaigns emphasizing speed\nconverted 31% better\n\n             +\n\nBrand side:\nwe actually have proof for\n14-day implementation\n\n             ↓\n\nContext Compiler"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's dramatically better than trying to stuff everything into one graph."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "At very high scale we could later replace/augment DuckDB with something like ClickHouse, which is specifically designed for high-volume analytical workloads. citeturn734296search7"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But I would **not start with ClickHouse**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Then there are two tools that could improve our intelligence itself"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "These are more interesting than infrastructure."
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 2,
          "text": "DSPy could help us optimize the algorithms"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This might eventually be one of the most valuable additions."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "DSPy lets you define LLM operations as typed input/output programs and then **optimize them against an evaluation metric and training examples**, rather than manually tweaking prompts forever. citeturn382325search0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Imagine our customer extractor:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "INPUT\n\nsales-call segment\n\n      ↓\n\nCustomerInsightExtractor\n\n      ↓\n\nOUTPUT\n\nproblem\nmotivation\nobjection\ntrigger\ndesired_outcome\nevidence\nconfidence"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Initially we write it."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Then we collect 500 examples where we've manually judged what the correct extraction should have been."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "DSPy can optimize the LLM program against our score."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Conceptually:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "our extractor\n     ↓\n500 examples\n     ↓\nour quality metric\n     ↓\nDSPy optimizer\n     ↓\nbetter extractor"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "DSPy's current optimization model explicitly works this way: define a program, examples and a scoring metric, then compile/optimize the program. citeturn382325search0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This could apply to:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "CustomerInsightExtractor\nCompetitorExtractor\nContextQueryGenerator\nHypothesisGenerator\nEvidenceEvaluator\nStrategicCritic\nNarrativeEvaluator"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So LangGraph and DSPy have different roles:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "LANGGRAPH\n\ndefines:\nHOW THE THINKING PROCESS FLOWS\n\nDSPy\n\noptimizes:\nHOW WELL INDIVIDUAL THINKING OPERATIONS WORK"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's potentially powerful."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I would introduce DSPy **after we have evaluation datasets**, not before."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Ragas could specifically help us improve the Context Compiler"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Langfuse gives us the general evaluation environment."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Ragas gives us useful retrieval-specific metrics."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For example, **context precision** measures whether relevant information is ranked ahead of irrelevant information, while **context recall** measures whether our retrieval failed to include important evidence. Ragas also includes metrics for things like noise sensitivity, faithfulness and agent/tool behavior. citeturn174243search0turn174243search2turn174243search3"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That maps almost perfectly to our Context Compiler."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "We could test:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Question:\n\n\"Should Acme emphasize speed\nin enterprise positioning?\""
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Human expert says the ideal context contains:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "A\nB\nC\nD\nE"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Compiler v1 returns:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "A\nB\nD\nX\nY"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Compiler v2 returns:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "A\nB\nC\nD\nE"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Now we can objectively improve retrieval rather than saying:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "“v2 feels smarter.”"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Ragas already documents integration with Langfuse, so scores can be attached to the traces we're already collecting. citeturn174243search1"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That combination is very attractive:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Context Compiler\n      ↓\nRagas evaluates retrieval\n      ↓\nLangfuse stores experiments\n      ↓\nDSPy/our algorithms improve it"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This creates an actual **intelligence-development loop**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Background processing is another thing we shouldn't build"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Eventually there will be lots of:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "sync CRM every hour\n\nreprocess 3,000 interviews\n\nupdate competitor research\n\ngenerate nightly summaries\n\nrebuild abstraction indexes\n\nrun evaluation suite\n\nprocess uploaded documents"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Those jobs need queues, retries, durability, concurrency limits, scheduling and progress reporting."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Trigger.dev already provides durable TypeScript background tasks, retries, queues, schedules and real-time frontend status updates, and can be cloud-hosted or self-hosted. citeturn121825search2turn121825search15turn121825search14"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But I would not add it immediately."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Harness already handles agent work."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Nango handles integration sync work."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "If we start accumulating lots of **non-agent application jobs**, then add Trigger."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Harness\n= agents working\n\nNango\n= external integrations syncing\n\nTrigger\n= miscellaneous durable backend jobs"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "No overlap if we keep those boundaries."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Two things I'd postpone"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**OpenFGA** is interesting if our permissions become complex—e.g. one agency employee can see Brand A but not Brand B, freelancers can access campaigns but not customer evidence, clients can share selected objects, and agents have their own resource permissions. OpenFGA provides relationship-based authorization around users, objects and relations. citeturn565791search13turn565791search12"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But for an early managed product, standard tenant roles plus Cognee dataset isolation and Harness tool scopes should probably suffice."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Similarly, **Infisical** is a strong secrets-management option for API keys, database credentials and machine identities, with centralized versioned secrets and fine-grained access control. citeturn307454search1turn307454search7"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But Nango already handles customer OAuth credentials, so I wouldn't add Infisical until our own infrastructure secrets become complicated."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "And I would use PostHog for our product, not the box"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "We'll want to know:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "Do clients actually read Researcher posts?"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "What percentage of recommendations get approved?"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "Which agents get chatted with?"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "Do users drill from insight → evidence?"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "Does the avatar activity help or distract?"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "PostHog currently combines product analytics, session replay, feature flags, experiments, surveys and related product-development tooling. citeturn112775search3"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's useful for improving **our UI/product**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I wouldn't make PostHog part of the core Brand Box."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "So the architecture becomes surprisingly complete"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "                          DATA SOURCES\n                               │\n                     ┌─────────┴─────────┐\n                     │                   │\n                   NANGO              Files/Web\n                     │                   │\n                     └─────────┬─────────┘\n                               ▼\n\n                           THE BOX\n                 ┌─────────────┴─────────────┐\n                 │                           │\n              COGNEE                      DUCKDB\n        semantic knowledge              analytics\n        graph/evidence/time              metrics\n                 │                           │\n                 └─────────────┬─────────────┘\n                               │\n                          OUR BOX API\n                               │\n                               ▼\n                     OUR CONTEXT COMPILER\n                               │\n                               ▼\n                          LANGGRAPH\n                    cognitive architectures\n                               │\n                               ▼\n                    DEEPSEEK HARNESS\n                    persistent agent actors\n                               │\n                               ▼\n                            NANGO\n                      actions in real tools\n                               │\n                               ▼\n                         EXTERNAL WORLD\n\n──────────────── CROSS-CUTTING ────────────────\n\nLiteLLM\nmodel gateway\n\nLangfuse\ntraces / datasets / experiments / evals\n\nRagas\nretrieval & Context Compiler evaluation\n\nDSPy\noptimization of intelligence modules\n\nTrigger.dev\nbackground jobs when needed\n\nPostHog\nour product analytics"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 2,
          "text": "And then what do we actually build?"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is now the interesting part."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "We build approximately:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "OUR IP\n────────────────────────────────\n\nBrand Ontology\n\nSource Interpretation Rules\n\nExtraction Algorithms\n\nEvidence Model\n\nTruth / Confidence Model\n\nContradiction Resolution\n\nProgressive Abstraction Model\n\nContext Compiler\n\nCustomer Intelligence Algorithms\n\nResearch Algorithms\n\nStrategic Reasoning Algorithms\n\nNarrative Algorithms\n\nGrowth Algorithms\n\nBrand Guardian Algorithms\n\nLearning / Feedback Semantics\n\nDomain-specific agent tools\n\nFeed semantics\n\nLittle-guy UX"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Everything else should be treated as infrastructure wherever practical."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "There is still real engineering around tenant configuration, schema migrations, security, adapters, tests and product deployment, so I wouldn't say **literally** “all we'll write is intelligence.” But it gets much closer."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "The piece I now find most interesting"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "With this stack, we could create a **closed improvement loop for the intelligence itself**:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "                REAL CLIENT WORK\n                      │\n                      ▼\n               Langfuse traces\n                      │\n           humans score / correct\n                      │\n                      ▼\n               evaluation dataset\n                      │\n          ┌───────────┴────────────┐\n          ▼                        ▼\n       Ragas                     our metrics\n retrieval quality          marketing quality\n          │                        │\n          └───────────┬────────────┘\n                      ▼\n                 DSPy / us\n              optimize algorithms\n                      │\n                      ▼\n            new reasoning version\n                      │\n                      ▼\n                A/B evaluation\n                      │\n                      ▼\n               better system"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That changes the development problem from:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**“How do I build an enormous AI platform?”**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "into:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**“How do I encode, measure and continuously improve exceptional marketing intelligence?”**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That is a much more attractive problem for us to own."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "And if I were simplifying aggressively, my **core reusable stack** would now be:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**Cognee + DuckDB + Nango + LiteLLM + LangGraph + Harness + Langfuse.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I'd regard **Graphiti, Ragas, DSPy, Trigger.dev, OpenFGA, Infisical and PostHog as selective additions** when their specific need appears rather than installing the entire zoo on day one."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That distinction matters. Reusing infrastructure should make the architecture simpler—not turn the product into a fragile pile of fifteen frameworks. memcite"
        }
      ],
      "artifact_refs": []
    },

Improve this module.”\n\nBut before then, automatic optimization could easily optimize against a weak or artificial metric.\n\nSo I would actually remove DSPy from the initial architecture entirely.\n\nThe leaner stack becomes:\n\n```text\nCOGNEE\nknowledge infrastructure\n\nDUCKDB\nanalytics\n\nNANGO\nexternal integrations\n\nLITELLM\nmodel routing\n\nLANGGRAPH\nour reasoning algorithms\n\nDEEPSEEK HARNESS\nagent runtime\n\nLANGFUSE\ntracing + evaluation + future dataset\n\nOUR PRODUCT\nontology\nextraction logic\ntruth system\ncontext compiler\nreasoning logic\nfeed + avatars\n```\n\n**Langfuse is still worth keeping**, even without training data, because from day one it can record the cases that may eventually *become* your evaluation/training dataset.\n\nSo rather than trying to optimize the intelligence automatically now:\n\n> **design it manually → observe it → correct it → collect examples → formalize evaluation → optimize later.**\n\nThat is a much more sensible progression for where the product is today. memcite",

          "type": "code",

          "text": "COGNEE\nknowledge infrastructure\n\nDUCKDB\nanalytics\n\nNANGO\nexternal integrations\n\nLITELLM\nmodel routing\n\nLANGGRAPH\nour reasoning algorithms\n\nDEEPSEEK HARNESS\nagent runtime\n\nLANGFUSE\ntracing + evaluation + future dataset\n\nOUR PRODUCT\nontology\nextraction logic\ntruth system\ncontext compiler\nreasoning logic\nfeed + avatars"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**Langfuse is still worth keeping**, even without training data, because from day one it can record the cases that may eventually *become* your evaluation/training dataset."
        },

          "type": "paragraph",

      "role": "user",
      "content": "do we also need infrastructure for intra agent communication and work and management ?",

        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "do we also need infrastructure for intra agent communication and work and management ?"

      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "Yes — but I **would not add another large framework for this right now**.\n\nAfter looking more closely, most of the generic infrastructure is already covered by **Harness + LangGraph**. What we're still missing is a relatively small **domain-specific coordination layer** that we should build ourselves.\n\nThe key idea is:\n\n> Agents should not mainly communicate by “chatting with each other.”\n> They should communicate through **structured work, results, events and shared knowledge**.\n\n### What Harness already gives us\n\nDeepSeek Harness now has quite substantial subagent infrastructure. An agent can delegate work to child agents; those children can be durable/continuable, receive follow-up work, be interrupted, report back to their parent, and be discovered/listed. It even has optional model-facing controls such as `send_message`, `interrupt_agent`, and `list_agents`. fileciteturn27file0\n\nSo Harness can already handle things like:\n\n```text\nStrategist\n    ↓ delegates\nResearcher\n\nResearcher works\n    ↓\nreports result\n\nStrategist receives report\n    ↓\ncontinues\n```\n\nIt also owns the actual agent sessions, inboxes, cancellation, lifecycle and persistent child sessions. fileciteturn27file0\n\nWe absolutely should reuse that rather than building an agent messaging runtime.\n\n### LangGraph covers coordination inside a reasoning process\n\nLangGraph gives us shared state, subgraphs, branching and explicit handoffs. Its multi-agent architecture lets one agent/subgraph pass controlled state to another, and it explicitly emphasizes that **we decide exactly what context crosses between agents** rather than blindly sending all conversation history. citeturn587325search0turn587325search1\n\nSo if Strategist's reasoning algorithm says:\n\n```text\ngenerate hypothesis\n       ↓\nneed customer evidence?\n       ↓ yes\ncall Researcher\n       ↓\nResearcherGraph\n       ↓\nreturn EvidencePackage\n       ↓\ncontinue strategy process\n```\n\nLangGraph already handles that structure. citeturn587325search3turn587325search4\n\n---\n\n# What is actually missing\n\nWe need a **Work Coordination Layer** specific to our product.\n\nNot a huge system. Think of it as the company's internal AI task board.\n\nInstead of:\n\n> “Hey Researcher, can you look into competitors and tell me what you think?”\n\nStrategist creates something structured:\n\n```text\nTask\n\ntype:\nCOMPETITOR_RESEARCH\n\nobjective:\nDetermine whether competitors emphasize\nimplementation speed.\n\nrequested_by:\nStrategist\n\nassigned_to:\nResearcher\n\ncontext:\n[references into Brand Box]\n\nrequired_output:\nCompetitorEvidencePackage\n\npriority:\nhigh\n\nstatus:\nassigned\n```\n\nResearcher eventually returns:\n\n```text\nWorkResult\n\ntask_id:\n123\n\nfindings:\n[...]\n\nevidence:\n[...]\n\nconfidence:\n0.87\n\nunresolved_questions:\n[...]\n\nbox_references:\n[...]\n```\n\nThat's the piece I think **we should build**.\n\nAnd it should be small.\n\n---\n\n# I would create three primitives\n\n### `Task`\n\nSomething an agent wants done.\n\n```text\nTask\n├── id\n├── type\n├── objective\n├── requested_by\n├── assigned_to\n├── context_refs\n├── dependencies\n├── expected_output_schema\n├── priority\n└── status\n```\n\n### `Artifact / Result`\n\nSomething an agent produced.\n\n```text\nResult\n├── task_id\n├── producer\n├── structured_output\n├── evidence_refs\n├── confidence\n├── assumptions\n└── created_at\n```\n\n### `Event`\n\nSomething that happened.\n\n```text\nTaskCreated\nTaskAssigned\nTaskStarted\nResearchStarted\nEvidenceFound\nHypothesisCreated\nReviewRequested\nTaskCompleted\nDecisionApproved\nDecisionRejected\n```\n\nThat's enough to power a surprisingly large amount of the system.\n\n---\n\n# Then communication becomes elegant\n\nImagine Researcher discovers something that matters to Strategist.\n\nWe **don't** need:\n\n```text\nResearcher → random message → Strategist\n```\n\nInstead:\n\n```text\nResearcher\n     ↓\ncreates Insight\n\n\"Competitors have shifted toward\nimplementation simplicity.\"\n\n     ↓\nstored in Box\n\n     +\nemits InsightCreated\n\n     ↓\nDirector / Strategist sees event\n```\n\nNow the information isn't trapped inside an agent conversation.\n\nIt's part of the company's knowledge.\n\nThat's much stronger.\n\n---\n\n# This is especially important for our Box\n\nThe Box should function as the **shared world agents coordinate through**.\n\nFor example:\n\n```text\n             BRAND BOX\n\n       Customer Insight\n             │\n             │ referenced by\n             ▼\nResearcher ────── Strategist\n                    │\n                    │ creates\n                    ▼\n              Positioning Hypothesis\n                    │\n                    ▼\n               Storyteller\n                    │\n                    ▼\n                 Narrative\n```\n\nAgents aren't sending huge amounts of knowledge to each other.\n\nThey're saying:\n\n> “Look at Insight `#1842`.”\n\nThe actual information remains in the Box.\n\nThat keeps context compact and gives us provenance.\n\n---\n\n# The Director becomes a manager, not a super-brain\n\nI'd give one agent/system role responsibility for coordination:\n\n```text\n                  DIRECTOR\n\n                     │\n\n       ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐\n       ▼             ▼             ▼\n Researcher      Strategist     Growth\n       │             │             │\n       └─────────────┼─────────────┘\n                     ▼\n                  The Box\n```\n\nThe Director's job isn't to redo everyone's reasoning.\n\nIt handles things like:\n\n> Who should work on this?\n\n> Can these tasks run in parallel?\n\n> Does Strategist need Researcher's result first?\n\n> Does Brand Guardian need to review this?\n\n> Does this need human approval?\n\n> Is work duplicated?\n\n> Has something stalled?\n\nThen specialist agents do the actual intellectual work.\n\n---\n\n# An example\n\nUser says:\n\n> “I think we need a new positioning direction.”\n\nDirector turns that into:\n\n```text\nPROJECT\nNew positioning exploration\n```\n\nand creates:\n\n```text\nTask A\nResearch customer perception\n→ Researcher\n\nTask B\nAnalyze competitor positions\n→ Researcher\n\nTask C\nAnalyze historical campaign performance\n→ Growth\n```\n\nA and B could run in parallel.\n\nGrowth queries analytics.\n\nResults become structured artifacts:\n\n```text\nCustomerEvidencePackage\n\nCompetitiveLandscape\n\nPerformanceEvidence\n```\n\nThen:\n\n```text\nA ──┐\nB ──┼──→ Strategy Task\nC ──┘\n```\n\nStrategist's LangGraph runs its reasoning process.\n\nIt outputs:\n\n```text\nPositioningRecommendation\n```\n\nThen:\n\n```text\nPositioningRecommendation\n        ↓\nBrand Guardian\n        ↓\nreview\n        ↓\nHuman approval\n```\n\nAnd every step creates feed events.\n\n---\n\n# This also solves our avatar states naturally\n\nThe work system knows:\n\n```text\nResearcher\ntask = competitor research\nstatus = working\nphase = searching\n```\n\nTherefore UI:\n\n```text\n🔵 Researcher\nSCANNING\n```\n\nLater LangGraph enters evidence comparison:\n\n```text\nphase = comparing\n```\n\nAvatar changes.\n\nThen:\n\n```text\nTaskCompleted\n```\n\nResearcher settles and publishes a feed post.\n\nSo the work-management system becomes part of the bridge between **backend reality and little-guy animation**.\n\n---\n\n# Do we need Kafka, Temporal, CrewAI, AutoGen, another multi-agent framework, etc.?\n\n**No, not initially.**\n\nThat would probably make the system worse.\n\nWe already have:\n\n```text\nHarness\n→ agent lifecycle + delegation + messaging\n\nLangGraph\n→ cognitive/workflow coordination\n\nPostgres\n→ durable product/work state\n\nCognee\n→ shared company knowledge\n\nTrigger.dev later\n→ generic long-running backend jobs\n```\n\nLangGraph itself is already meant for durable stateful workflows and multi-agent orchestration. citeturn587325search1turn587325search6\n\nAdding yet another “multi-agent management framework” would mostly duplicate responsibilities.\n\n---\n\n# The architecture I'd use\n\n```text\n                    USER\n                      │\n                      ▼\n                  DIRECTOR\n                      │\n             creates structured\n                    TASKS\n                      │\n        ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐\n        ▼             ▼             ▼\n   Researcher     Strategist      Growth\n   HARNESS        HARNESS         HARNESS\n        │             │             │\n   LangGraph      LangGraph      LangGraph\n   cognition      cognition      cognition\n        │             │             │\n        └─────────────┼─────────────┘\n                      │\n                  WORK LEDGER\n                [our Postgres]\n                      │\n              tasks / results\n              dependencies\n              statuses/events\n                      │\n        ┌─────────────┴─────────────┐\n        ▼                           ▼\n      BOX                         FEED\n    Cognee                     Product UI\n      │                           │\n shared knowledge             little guys\n```\n\nThe **Work Ledger** is the small missing piece.\n\n---\n\n## And I think we should own it\n\nBecause the semantics are product-specific.\n\nA generic framework knows:\n\n> agent A sent message B.\n\nWe care about:\n\n> Researcher produced evidence that supports Hypothesis X, Strategist used it in Decision Y, Brand Guardian challenged Claim Z, founder approved the resulting experiment.\n\nThose are **marketing work semantics**.\n\nI'd probably make our central domain objects something like:\n\n```text\nTask\nArtifact\nObservation\nInsight\nHypothesis\nRecommendation\nDecision\nExperiment\nResult\nEvent\n```\n\nThen agents create and transform these objects.\n\nThat's much more powerful than creating a Slack clone for AI agents.\n\nSo the answer is:\n\n> **Yes, we need intra-agent work coordination.**\n>\n> **No, we probably don't need another infrastructure product for it.**\n>\n> Harness + LangGraph give us most of the generic machinery; we should build a **thin structured Work Ledger + event protocol** that expresses how our particular AI marketing team works.\n\nAnd I think that layer, together with the Box, is what turns a collection of agents into an actual **AI organization**. memcite",

      "content": "arent there other systems already build for agent2agent communication and work that we could use to enhance our product? or does that add nore work than it solves instead if just creating our own light system",

        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "arent there other systems already build for agent2agent communication and work that we could use to enhance our product? or does that add nore work than it solves instead if just creating our own light system"
