      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "Yes. After looking at the current ecosystem, there **are** systems we can reuse—but I would only add one of them to our architecture now.\n\nThe important distinction is between:\n\n> **using a standard protocol**, which can simplify us,\n\nand\n\n> **adding another multi-agent framework**, which would mostly duplicate things we already have.\n\nThe one I think we should seriously adopt is **A2A (Agent2Agent Protocol)**.\n\n### A2A is almost exactly the standard vocabulary we were about to invent\n\nA2A is now a Linux Foundation open standard for communication between independent agents. Its core concepts are already:\n\n- `AgentCard` — what an agent is capable of\n- `Task` — a stateful piece of work\n- `Message` — communication\n- `Artifact` — something produced by work\n- `contextId` — grouping related work\n- task states such as working, input-required, completed, failed, rejected, canceled\n\nIt supports structured data, files, streaming and long-running tasks. citeturn841607search0turn841607search3\n\nThat's remarkably close to what we were designing:\n\n```text\nOUR IDEA               A2A\n\nAgent definition   →   AgentCard\n\nWork Task          →   Task\n\nAgent communication →  Message\n\nWork Result        →   Artifact\n\nProject/context    →   contextId\n\nTaskCompleted      →   Task status/update\n```\n\nSo rather than inventing all of the generic language ourselves, I would **design our Work Layer so it maps cleanly onto A2A**.\n\nBut there's an important twist.\n\n## I would NOT make the internal little guys communicate over A2A\n\nThe A2A project itself explicitly says A2A is **not intended to define communication between an agent and its own subagents**. It is primarily a protocol between independent/opaque agent systems. For internal subagents, it recommends using the native framework mechanism. citeturn841607search1\n\nThat means our internal architecture should remain:\n\n```text\n            OUR AI ORGANIZATION\n\n                 Director\n                    │\n          structured Task\n                    │\n          ┌─────────┼─────────┐\n          ▼         ▼         ▼\n      Researcher Strategist Growth\n          │         │         │\n          └──── Harness ──────┘\n                messaging\n                lifecycle\n                reports\n                subagents\n```\n\nHarness already supports continuable child agents, follow-up messages, reporting to parents, interruption, discovery/listing and durable child sessions. fileciteturn27file0\n\nSo using A2A **inside** that would be redundant.\n\nInstead:\n\n```text\nINTERNAL\n─────────────────────────\n\nHarness native communication\n\nEXTERNAL BOUNDARY\n─────────────────────────\n\nA2A\n```\n\nThat is much cleaner.\n\n---\n\n## Where A2A becomes very valuable for our product\n\nImagine three years from now.\n\nThe client's company already has:\n\n```text\nSalesforce Agent\nSAP Agent\ninternal Finance Agent\ncustomer-service agent\nour Marketing OS\n```\n\nRather than building custom integrations between every AI system:\n\n```text\n                    A2A\n\nFinance Agent ───────────────┐\n                             │\nSalesforce Agent ────────────┼── Our Marketing OS\n                             │\nSAP Agent ───────────────────┤\n                             │\nExternal research agent ─────┘\n```\n\nEach remains its own opaque system.\n\nThey can discover capabilities, issue tasks and return artifacts through a common protocol. That's exactly the use case A2A targets. citeturn472000search1turn841607search2\n\nAnd this ecosystem has become fairly credible: A2A was originally created by Google, then donated to the Linux Foundation, with governance involving companies including AWS, Cisco, Google, IBM, Microsoft, Salesforce, SAP and ServiceNow. citeturn841607search1\n\nSo future-proofing our work model around it makes sense.\n\n---\n\n# LangGraph also makes this easy later\n\nAnother positive finding: **LangGraph Agent Server already exposes A2A endpoints**.\n\nA deployed LangGraph assistant can expose an A2A Agent Card and support A2A methods such as sending messages, streaming results and fetching task status. citeturn433337search0turn433337search1\n\nSo potentially:\n\n```text\nExternal Agent\n      │\n     A2A\n      │\n      ▼\nOur LangGraph specialist\n      │\n      ▼\nHarness / Box / reasoning\n```\n\nwith relatively little adapter code.\n\nThat's exactly the sort of reuse we want.\n\n---\n\n# What about AGNTCY?\n\nThis is the more ambitious version.\n\nAGNTCY is an open-source stack focused on an **Internet of Agents**. It has infrastructure for:\n\nagent discovery, capability directories, decentralized identity, secure communication and multi-agent observability. citeturn528610search10\n\nOne interesting component is **SLIM**, a secure low-latency messaging layer for agents.\n\nThink:\n\n```text\nA2A\n= WHAT agents say\n\nSLIM\n= HOW those messages travel securely\n```\n\nSLIM provides things like secure messaging, group channels, RPC, reliable delivery, encryption and distributed routing. citeturn433337search2\n\nThat's impressive infrastructure.\n\nBut for us **right now it is overkill**.\n\nSLIM becomes interesting if one day we have:\n\n```text\n10,000 agents\n\nrunning across\nmultiple cloud providers\n\nacross multiple companies\n\ncommunicating directly\n\nwith strong identity/security requirements\n```\n\nThen I'd revisit it.\n\nFor six specialist marketing agents inside one client's environment?\n\nNo.\n\n---\n\n# What about AutoGen?\n\nAutoGen Core is explicitly an event-driven framework for scalable, distributed multi-agent systems, including distributed runtimes. citeturn472000search2\n\nSo yes, we could build:\n\n```text\nResearcher\n   ↓ message bus\nStrategist\n   ↓\nGrowth\n```\n\nwith AutoGen.\n\nBut then we'd have:\n\n```text\nHarness\n+\nLangGraph\n+\nAutoGen\n```\n\nand all three want to participate in:\n\nstate, orchestration, agents, events, messaging and lifecycle.\n\nThat would make the architecture worse.\n\nAutoGen would make sense as a **replacement** for part of our stack, not an addition.\n\n---\n\n# Same issue with CrewAI\n\nCrewAI has:\n\nagents, crews, tasks, processes, delegation, sequential/hierarchical workflows, memory, state and flows. citeturn782013search0turn782013search1\n\nIn other words, it already implements:\n\n```text\nManager\n │\n ├── Researcher\n ├── Writer\n └── Analyst\n\nTasks\nDependencies\nDelegation\nProcesses\n```\n\nVery relevant conceptually.\n\nBut it's basically trying to own the same layer as:\n\n```text\nHarness + LangGraph + our Work Layer\n```\n\nAdding CrewAI would therefore be **duplication**, not infrastructure reuse.\n\nAgain: legitimate alternative architecture, poor additional dependency.\n\n---\n\n# Microsoft now has an interesting alternative too\n\nMicrosoft Agent Framework has become quite substantial. It includes agents, a harness, graph-based workflows, checkpointing, human-in-the-loop and built-in multi-agent patterns including sequential, concurrent, handoff, group chat and manager-style coordination. citeturn123401search8turn123401search11\n\nFor example, Microsoft's handoff orchestration explicitly supports agents handing full task ownership to specialists, while its “agent as tool” pattern keeps a primary agent responsible and delegates only subtasks. citeturn123401search2\n\nThat's actually very close to decisions we're making.\n\nBut again, this tells me:\n\n> Microsoft Agent Framework is a possible **alternative to Harness + LangGraph**.\n\nIt doesn't tell me we should add Microsoft Agent Framework *on top of them*.\n\nThat would be four frameworks managing agents.\n\n---\n\n# So I would make one change to our architecture\n\nInstead of building a completely proprietary agent-work protocol, use:\n\n> **A2A concepts as the generic foundation, plus our marketing-specific extensions.**\n\nFor instance:\n\n```text\nGENERIC WORK\n────────────────────\n\nTask\nMessage\nArtifact\nStatus\nAgent\nContext\n\n        +\n\nOUR DOMAIN LANGUAGE\n────────────────────\n\nEvidence\nObservation\nInsight\nHypothesis\nRecommendation\nDecision\nExperiment\nBrandChange\nCampaign\n```\n\nThen a task could be:\n\n```text\nTask\n\nid:\ntask_481\n\nagent:\nresearcher\n\nskill:\ncompetitor-analysis\n\nstatus:\nworking\n\ncontext:\npositioning-project-42\n\ninput:\nBoxRefs [...]\n\nartifacts:\n[]\n```\n\nand later:\n\n```text\nArtifact\n\ntype:\nCompetitiveEvidencePackage\n\nproducer:\nresearcher\n\nevidence_refs:\n[...]\n\nfindings:\n[...]\n\nconfidence:\n0.88\n```\n\nThat's very close to A2A already. citeturn841607search0\n\nWe then add our richer domain semantics.\n\n---\n\n# Our own coordination layer becomes tiny\n\nInstead of building an “agent operating system”, we build essentially:\n\n```text\n              OUR WORK LAYER\n\nTask\nArtifact\nEvent\nDependency\nDecision\nBoxReference\n        │\n        ▼\n     Postgres\n```\n\nAnd adapters:\n\n```text\nWorkTask\n   │\n   ├──→ Harness subagent request\n   │\n   ├──→ LangGraph run\n   │\n   ├──→ Feed event\n   │\n   └──→ A2A Task\n```\n\nThat's exactly the kind of **small elegant adapter layer** you've been aiming for.\n\n---\n\n# The architecture would then have three communication mechanisms\n\nAnd I think this separation is particularly clean:\n\n```text\n               OUR SYSTEM\n\nAGENT ↔ TOOL\n────────────────────\nMCP\n\nResearcher → web\nGrowth → HubSpot\nStrategist → Box\n\nINTERNAL AGENT ↔ AGENT\n────────────────────\nHarness\n\nDirector → Researcher\nResearcher → Director\nStrategist → Brand Guardian\n\nEXTERNAL AGENT ↔ AGENT\n────────────────────\nA2A\n\nOur Marketing OS → Salesforce Agent\nOur Marketing OS → client's Finance Agent\nExternal Agent → our Strategist\n```\n\nThis actually matches the standards' intended boundaries: A2A is explicitly agent-to-agent interoperability, while MCP is agent-to-tool/context interoperability. citeturn841607search1\n\n---\n\n# And one shared Work Model sits above all of them\n\n```text\n                   WORK MODEL\n                       │\n         Task / Artifact / Event\n                       │\n       ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐\n       ▼               ▼               ▼\n\n    Harness          LangGraph          A2A\n   internal           reasoning        external\n communication         work          communication\n```\n\nThat is where I think we've landed on something quite elegant.\n\n## So: use another system or build light ourselves?\n\nMy answer is now:\n\n**Do both, but at different levels.**\n\nDon't invent communication transport, subagent sessions, distributed protocols or agent discovery.\n\nReuse:\n\n**Harness** → internal agent runtime\n**LangGraph** → reasoning orchestration\n**A2A** → standard external agent protocol\n**MCP** → tool protocol\n\nBut build a very small proprietary:\n\n> **Marketing Work Model**\n\nbecause that's where our useful semantics live.\n\nAnd I would deliberately model its generic parts after A2A so that we don't paint ourselves into a corner.\n\nI would **not add CrewAI, AutoGen, Microsoft Agent Framework or AGNTCY/SLIM now**. They mostly duplicate our current layers. I'd keep them in mind as replacements or scaling infrastructure if requirements change.\n\nSo the resulting system is actually getting simpler:\n\n```text\nKNOWLEDGE       Cognee\nANALYTICS       DuckDB\nINTEGRATIONS    Nango\nMODELS          LiteLLM\n\nTHINKING        LangGraph\nAGENT RUNTIME   Harness\nTOOLS           MCP\nEXTERNAL AGENTS A2A\n\nWORK SEMANTICS  OURS\nINTELLIGENCE    OURS\nPRODUCT         OURS\n```\n\nThat feels like a much healthier boundary: **standards and open infrastructure underneath; our marketing intelligence and product semantics on top.** memcite",
      "blocks": [
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Yes. After looking at the current ecosystem, there **are** systems we can reuse—but I would only add one of them to our architecture now."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The important distinction is between:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**using a standard protocol**, which can simplify us,"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "and"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**adding another multi-agent framework**, which would mostly duplicate things we already have."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The one I think we should seriously adopt is **A2A (Agent2Agent Protocol)**."
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 3,
          "text": "A2A is almost exactly the standard vocabulary we were about to invent"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "A2A is now a Linux Foundation open standard for communication between independent agents. Its core concepts are already:"
        },
        {
          "type": "list",
          "ordered": false,
          "items": [
            "`AgentCard` — what an agent is capable of",
            "`Task` — a stateful piece of work",
            "`Message` — communication",
            "`Artifact` — something produced by work",
            "`contextId` — grouping related work",
            "task states such as working, input-required, completed, failed, rejected, canceled"
          ]
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "It supports structured data, files, streaming and long-running tasks. citeturn841607search0turn841607search3"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's remarkably close to what we were designing:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "OUR IDEA               A2A\n\nAgent definition   →   AgentCard\n\nWork Task          →   Task\n\nAgent communication →  Message\n\nWork Result        →   Artifact\n\nProject/context    →   contextId\n\nTaskCompleted      →   Task status/update"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So rather than inventing all of the generic language ourselves, I would **design our Work Layer so it maps cleanly onto A2A**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But there's an important twist."
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 2,
          "text": "I would NOT make the internal little guys communicate over A2A"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The A2A project itself explicitly says A2A is **not intended to define communication between an agent and its own subagents**. It is primarily a protocol between independent/opaque agent systems. For internal subagents, it recommends using the native framework mechanism. citeturn841607search1"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That means our internal architecture should remain:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "            OUR AI ORGANIZATION\n\n                 Director\n                    │\n          structured Task\n                    │\n          ┌─────────┼─────────┐\n          ▼         ▼         ▼\n      Researcher Strategist Growth\n          │         │         │\n          └──── Harness ──────┘\n                messaging\n                lifecycle\n                reports\n                subagents"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Harness already supports continuable child agents, follow-up messages, reporting to parents, interruption, discovery/listing and durable child sessions. fileciteturn27file0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So using A2A **inside** that would be redundant."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Instead:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "INTERNAL\n─────────────────────────\n\nHarness native communication\n\nEXTERNAL BOUNDARY\n─────────────────────────\n\nA2A"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That is much cleaner."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 2,
          "text": "Where A2A becomes very valuable for our product"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Imagine three years from now."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The client's company already has:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Salesforce Agent\nSAP Agent\ninternal Finance Agent\ncustomer-service agent\nour Marketing OS"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Rather than building custom integrations between every AI system:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "                    A2A\n\nFinance Agent ───────────────┐\n                             │\nSalesforce Agent ────────────┼── Our Marketing OS\n                             │\nSAP Agent ───────────────────┤\n                             │\nExternal research agent ─────┘"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Each remains its own opaque system."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "They can discover capabilities, issue tasks and return artifacts through a common protocol. That's exactly the use case A2A targets. citeturn472000search1turn841607search2"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "And this ecosystem has become fairly credible: A2A was originally created by Google, then donated to the Linux Foundation, with governance involving companies including AWS, Cisco, Google, IBM, Microsoft, Salesforce, SAP and ServiceNow. citeturn841607search1"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So future-proofing our work model around it makes sense."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "LangGraph also makes this easy later"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Another positive finding: **LangGraph Agent Server already exposes A2A endpoints**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "A deployed LangGraph assistant can expose an A2A Agent Card and support A2A methods such as sending messages, streaming results and fetching task status. citeturn433337search0turn433337search1"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So potentially:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "External Agent\n      │\n     A2A\n      │\n      ▼\nOur LangGraph specialist\n      │\n      ▼\nHarness / Box / reasoning"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "with relatively little adapter code."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's exactly the sort of reuse we want."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "What about AGNTCY?"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is the more ambitious version."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "AGNTCY is an open-source stack focused on an **Internet of Agents**. It has infrastructure for:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "agent discovery, capability directories, decentralized identity, secure communication and multi-agent observability. citeturn528610search10"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "One interesting component is **SLIM**, a secure low-latency messaging layer for agents."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Think:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "A2A\n= WHAT agents say\n\nSLIM\n= HOW those messages travel securely"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "SLIM provides things like secure messaging, group channels, RPC, reliable delivery, encryption and distributed routing. citeturn433337search2"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's impressive infrastructure."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But for us **right now it is overkill**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "SLIM becomes interesting if one day we have:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "10,000 agents\n\nrunning across\nmultiple cloud providers\n\nacross multiple companies\n\ncommunicating directly\n\nwith strong identity/security requirements"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Then I'd revisit it."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For six specialist marketing agents inside one client's environment?"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "No."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "What about AutoGen?"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "AutoGen Core is explicitly an event-driven framework for scalable, distributed multi-agent systems, including distributed runtimes. citeturn472000search2"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So yes, we could build:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Researcher\n   ↓ message bus\nStrategist\n   ↓\nGrowth"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "with AutoGen."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But then we'd have:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Harness\n+\nLangGraph\n+\nAutoGen"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "and all three want to participate in:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "state, orchestration, agents, events, messaging and lifecycle."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That would make the architecture worse."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "AutoGen would make sense as a **replacement** for part of our stack, not an addition."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Same issue with CrewAI"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "CrewAI has:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "agents, crews, tasks, processes, delegation, sequential/hierarchical workflows, memory, state and flows. citeturn782013search0turn782013search1"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "In other words, it already implements:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Manager\n │\n ├── Researcher\n ├── Writer\n └── Analyst\n\nTasks\nDependencies\nDelegation\nProcesses"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Very relevant conceptually."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But it's basically trying to own the same layer as:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Harness + LangGraph + our Work Layer"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Adding CrewAI would therefore be **duplication**, not infrastructure reuse."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Again: legitimate alternative architecture, poor additional dependency."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Microsoft now has an interesting alternative too"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Microsoft Agent Framework has become quite substantial. It includes agents, a harness, graph-based workflows, checkpointing, human-in-the-loop and built-in multi-agent patterns including sequential, concurrent, handoff, group chat and manager-style coordination. citeturn123401search8turn123401search11"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For example, Microsoft's handoff orchestration explicitly supports agents handing full task ownership to specialists, while its “agent as tool” pattern keeps a primary agent responsible and delegates only subtasks. citeturn123401search2"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's actually very close to decisions we're making."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But again, this tells me:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "Microsoft Agent Framework is a possible **alternative to Harness + LangGraph**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "It doesn't tell me we should add Microsoft Agent Framework *on top of them*."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That would be four frameworks managing agents."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "So I would make one change to our architecture"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Instead of building a completely proprietary agent-work protocol, use:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**A2A concepts as the generic foundation, plus our marketing-specific extensions.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For instance:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "GENERIC WORK\n────────────────────\n\nTask\nMessage\nArtifact\nStatus\nAgent\nContext\n\n        +\n\nOUR DOMAIN LANGUAGE\n────────────────────\n\nEvidence\nObservation\nInsight\nHypothesis\nRecommendation\nDecision\nExperiment\nBrandChange\nCampaign"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Then a task could be:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Task\n\nid:\ntask_481\n\nagent:\nresearcher\n\nskill:\ncompetitor-analysis\n\nstatus:\nworking\n\ncontext:\npositioning-project-42\n\ninput:\nBoxRefs [...]\n\nartifacts:\n[]"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "and later:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Artifact\n\ntype:\nCompetitiveEvidencePackage\n\nproducer:\nresearcher\n\nevidence_refs:\n[...]\n\nfindings:\n[...]\n\nconfidence:\n0.88"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's very close to A2A already. citeturn841607search0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "We then add our richer domain semantics."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Our own coordination layer becomes tiny"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Instead of building an “agent operating system”, we build essentially:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "              OUR WORK LAYER\n\nTask\nArtifact\nEvent\nDependency\nDecision\nBoxReference\n        │\n        ▼\n     Postgres"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "And adapters:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "WorkTask\n   │\n   ├──→ Harness subagent request\n   │\n   ├──→ LangGraph run\n   │\n   ├──→ Feed event\n   │\n   └──→ A2A Task"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's exactly the kind of **small elegant adapter layer** you've been aiming for."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "The architecture would then have three communication mechanisms"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "And I think this separation is particularly clean:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "               OUR SYSTEM\n\nAGENT ↔ TOOL\n────────────────────\nMCP\n\nResearcher → web\nGrowth → HubSpot\nStrategist → Box\n\nINTERNAL AGENT ↔ AGENT\n────────────────────\nHarness\n\nDirector → Researcher\nResearcher → Director\nStrategist → Brand Guardian\n\nEXTERNAL AGENT ↔ AGENT\n────────────────────\nA2A\n\nOur Marketing OS → Salesforce Agent\nOur Marketing OS → client's Finance Agent\nExternal Agent → our Strategist"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This actually matches the standards' intended boundaries: A2A is explicitly agent-to-agent interoperability, while MCP is agent-to-tool/context interoperability. citeturn841607search1"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "And one shared Work Model sits above all of them"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "                   WORK MODEL\n                       │\n         Task / Artifact / Event\n                       │\n       ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐\n       ▼               ▼               ▼\n\n    Harness          LangGraph          A2A\n   internal           reasoning        external\n communication         work          communication"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That is where I think we've landed on something quite elegant."
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 2,
          "text": "So: use another system or build light ourselves?"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "My answer is now:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**Do both, but at different levels.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Don't invent communication transport, subagent sessions, distributed protocols or agent discovery."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Reuse:"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**Harness** → internal agent runtime\n**LangGraph** → reasoning orchestration\n**A2A** → standard external agent protocol\n**MCP** → tool protocol"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But build a very small proprietary:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**Marketing Work Model**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "because that's where our useful semantics live."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "And I would deliberately model its generic parts after A2A so that we don't paint ourselves into a corner."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I would **not add CrewAI, AutoGen, Microsoft Agent Framework or AGNTCY/SLIM now**. They mostly duplicate our current layers. I'd keep them in mind as replacements or scaling infrastructure if requirements change."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So the resulting system is actually getting simpler:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "KNOWLEDGE       Cognee\nANALYTICS       DuckDB\nINTEGRATIONS    Nango\nMODELS          LiteLLM\n\nTHINKING        LangGraph\nAGENT RUNTIME   Harness\nTOOLS           MCP\nEXTERNAL AGENTS A2A\n\nWORK SEMANTICS  OURS\nINTELLIGENCE    OURS\nPRODUCT         OURS"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That feels like a much healthier boundary: **standards and open infrastructure underneath; our marketing intelligence and product semantics on top.** memcite"
        }
      ],
      "artifact_refs": []
    },
    {
      "role": "user",
      "content": "we also talked about frontend.\ncan you trace what exactly we talked about and what exactly we need to build. are there any existing frameworks or system we should use snd leverage",
      "blocks": [
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "we also talked about frontend.\ncan you trace what exactly we talked about and what exactly we need to build. are there any existing frameworks or system we should use snd leverage"
        }
      ],
      "artifact_refs": []
    },
    {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "Yes. Looking back across the frontend direction we developed, I think the frontend is now quite well defined. And after checking the current ecosystem, **there is a lot we should reuse—but the distinctive feed + agent-character experience should remain ours.**\n\nThe key distinction is:\n\n> **Use frameworks for UI plumbing, streaming, accessibility, chat, state and animation runtimes.**\n>\n> **Build the actual product language ourselves.**\n\n## What we had already converged on\n\nThe product started closer to a conventional Brand Core dashboard, but we moved away from that. The primary interface became a **private intelligence feed**, where the company’s specialist agents appear as persistent actors.\n\nThe home screen is essentially:\n\n```text\n┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                                                 │\n│  🔵 Researcher                                  │\n│                                                 │\n│  \"Implementation friction appeared in 14 of    │\n│   the latest 23 enterprise conversations.\"      │\n│                                                 │\n│  Evidence 14     Confidence 84%                 │\n│                                                 │\n│  Ask   Save   Discuss                           │\n│                                                 │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                                                 │\n│  🟡 Strategist                                  │\n│                                                 │\n│  \"This may be a positioning opportunity...\"    │\n│                                                 │\n│  Approve experiment    Adjust    Discuss        │\n│                                                 │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                                                 │\n│  🟣 Storyteller                                 │\n│                                                 │\n│  \"I developed three narrative territories...\"  │\n│                                                 │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\nBut the characters aren't emoji or generic robots. We settled on **abstract little creatures with distinct anatomy**, each agent having its own silhouette, color and movement vocabulary.\n\nAnd an important visual rule emerged:\n\n> **Avatar = expression**\n> **UI = container**\n> **Motion = meaning**\n\nThe UI itself stays quiet: neutral surfaces, restrained typography, minimal chrome and little decorative color. Almost all expressive color comes from the agents.\n\nThat means the frontend has two visual layers:\n\n```text\nCALM PRODUCT LAYER\n────────────────────────\nlayout\ncards\ntext\nevidence\ncontrols\nnavigation\ndata\n\nEXPRESSIVE AGENT LAYER\n────────────────────────\ncolor\nmovement\npersonality\nworking state\nenergy\nuncertainty\nattention\n```\n\nI think that's still exactly the right direction. memcite\n\n---\n\n# The actual product surfaces we discussed\n\nI would now formalize them like this:\n\n| Surface | Purpose |\n|---|---|\n| **Feed** | What matters right now |\n| **Core** | What the system currently believes about the company |\n| **Agents** | Who is working, what they're doing and what they've recently produced |\n| **Work** | Projects, tasks, experiments and dependencies |\n| **Library** | Research, creatives, campaigns, documents and generated artifacts |\n| **History** | Decisions, belief changes, strategy changes and prior states |\n| **Agent conversation** | Direct discussion with Researcher, Strategist, etc. |\n| **Evidence view** | Drill from recommendation → insight → observations → original evidence |\n\nThe Feed remains the home screen.\n\nEverything else is accessible by drilling down.\n\nSo:\n\n```text\nFEED POST\n\n\"Implementation speed appears\nto be an emerging customer priority.\"\n\n          ↓ click evidence\n\nINSIGHT\n\n18 supporting observations\nconfidence 0.81\n\n          ↓\n\nOBSERVATIONS\n\nSales call #27\nSales call #42\nCustomer survey #8\nCRM pattern\n\n          ↓\n\nSOURCE\n\nOriginal transcript\n```\n\nThat progressive disclosure mirrors the progressive knowledge architecture we discussed for the Box.\n\n---\n\n# The feed itself should have typed posts\n\nI wouldn't build it as arbitrary AI-generated HTML.\n\nOur backend should emit a typed object such as:\n\n```ts\nFeedItem =\n  | ObservationPost\n  | InsightPost\n  | HypothesisPost\n  | RecommendationPost\n  | ArtifactPost\n  | QuestionPost\n  | ResultPost\n  | LearningPost\n  | ExternalSignalPost\n```\n\nThen **we control exactly how each type renders**.\n\nFor example:\n\n```text\nObservationPost\n─────────────────\nlow-level discovery\n\nInsightPost\n─────────────────\nsynthesized meaning\n\nHypothesisPost\n─────────────────\nuncertain interpretation\n\nRecommendationPost\n─────────────────\nproposed decision/action\n\nResultPost\n─────────────────\nwhat happened\n\nLearningPost\n─────────────────\nwhat the system learned\n```\n\nThis is one of the frontend pieces we should definitely own.\n\n---\n\n# User interactions also have domain meaning\n\nWe had discussed:\n\n```text\nLike\nDislike\nComment\nAsk\nSave\nApprove\nAdjust\nShare/tag\n```\n\nThose aren't merely UI buttons.\n\nTheir semantics feed back into the system.\n\nFor example:\n\n```text\nLIKE\n→ weak preference signal\n\nCOMMENT\n→ contextual signal\n\nCORRECTION\n→ strong epistemic signal\n\nAPPROVE\n→ explicit decision\n\nADJUST\n→ modify recommendation\n\nREJECT\n→ explicit negative decision\n```\n\nSo the React button itself is trivial.\n\nThe meaning behind it is ours.\n\n---\n\n# The avatars should be actual state machines\n\nWe had settled on states roughly like:\n\n```text\nidle\n\nthinking\n\nsearching\n\nreading\n\ncomparing\n\nconnecting\n\nsynthesizing\n\ncreating\n\npresenting\n\nwaiting_for_approval\n\nsuccess\n\nuncertain\n\nerror\n```\n\nAnd those states should correspond to **real backend execution**, not random animation.\n\nExample:\n\n```text\nLangGraph:\nsource_search\n\n        ↓\n\nDomain event:\nresearch.searching\n\n        ↓\n\nFrontend:\nResearcher state = SEARCHING\n\n        ↓\n\nRive:\nblue creature scans around\n```\n\nThen:\n\n```text\nLangGraph:\ncompare_evidence\n\n        ↓\n\nResearcher state = COMPARING\n\n        ↓\n\navatar visually arranges\ntwo objects side-by-side\n```\n\nThis part is important because it makes the little guys a real **visualization of system state** rather than branding decoration.\n\n---\n\n# What I would reuse for the frontend\n\nThis is where the ecosystem is now quite good.\n\n## Next.js + React + TypeScript\n\nI would use **Next.js App Router** as the product shell.\n\nIt already gives us React Server Components, Suspense, Server Functions, layouts and the modern server/client boundary we need. citeturn981261search1\n\nSo:\n\n```text\nNext.js\n\n/app/feed\n/app/core\n/app/agents\n/app/work\n/app/library\n/app/history\n```\n\nNo reason to invent web-app infrastructure.\n\n---\n\n# shadcn/ui + Radix for the boring UI\n\nThis is almost ideal for our aesthetic.\n\nshadcn/ui deliberately gives you the **actual source code of components**, rather than locking you into a component-library package, so we can change every detail to match our design language. citeturn647156search0\n\nUnderneath, Radix gives us robust accessible primitives for things like dialogs, popovers, menus, tooltips, tabs and focus/keyboard management while remaining essentially unstyled. citeturn647156search1turn647156search2\n\nThat means we don't need to waste time implementing:\n\n```text\ndialog behavior\nkeyboard navigation\ndropdowns\npopovers\ntooltips\nselects\nfocus management\naccessibility\n```\n\nwhile still being free to make everything look completely unlike standard shadcn.\n\nI'd use it as **construction material**, not as our visual identity.\n\n---\n\n# assistant-ui for conversations\n\nThis is one of the strongest pieces I found for us.\n\nI would **not** use assistant-ui for our Feed.\n\nBut I would absolutely consider it for:\n\n```text\nAgent chat\nmessage composer\nattachments\nstreaming\nmessage actions\ntool result rendering\napproval widgets\nthread behavior\n```\n\nIts primitives are deliberately headless/un-styled React building blocks that already handle streaming state, message composition, keyboard behavior, scrolling and tool calls. citeturn971416search0turn971416search2\n\nSo clicking:\n\n```text\n🟡 Strategist\n\n[Discuss]\n```\n\ncould open:\n\n```text\n┌───────────────────────────────┐\n│ 🟡 Strategist                 │\n│                               │\n│ You                           │\n│ Why do you think this is      │\n│ strong enough to test?        │\n│                               │\n│ Strategist                    │\n│ Three reasons...              │\n│                               │\n│ [evidence card]               │\n│                               │\n│ ┌───────────────────────────┐ │\n│ │ Ask Strategist...         │ │\n│ └───────────────────────────┘ │\n└───────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\nwithout us implementing the entire streaming-chat interaction model.\n\nassistant-ui also has explicit support for rendering tool calls as custom interactive React components and human-interaction tools. citeturn971416search1turn971416search3\n\nThat fits things like:\n\n```text\nStrategist requests approval\n\n┌────────────────────────────┐\n│ Run positioning experiment │\n│                            │\n│ Estimated duration: 2 wks  │\n│                            │\n│ [Approve]      [Adjust]     │\n└────────────────────────────┘\n```\n\nvery nicely.\n\n---\n\n# The really interesting new addition: AG-UI\n\nThis is the frontend equivalent of MCP/A2A.\n\nWe already have:\n\n```text\nMCP\nAgent ↔ Tools\n\nA2A\nAgent ↔ External Agents\n```\n\nI would seriously consider adding:\n\n```text\nAG-UI\nAgent ↔ User Interface\n```\n\nAG-UI is an open event protocol specifically for agent-to-frontend communication. It covers run lifecycle, streamed text, tool calls, synchronized state, ongoing activity, human interaction and custom events. citeturn971416search8turn351746search4\n\nThis could save us from inventing our own WebSocket/event protocol.\n\nOur architecture becomes:\n\n```text\n                BACKEND\n\n        Harness + LangGraph\n               │\n               ▼\n       Domain Event Adapter\n               │\n               ▼\n             AG-UI\n               │\n       SSE / HTTP stream\n               │\n               ▼\n\n               FRONTEND\n```\n\nAG-UI's JavaScript client already exposes event subscriptions, state tracking, aborting runs and an observable event stream. citeturn456618search0turn456618search1turn456618search2\n\n---\n\n# And AG-UI maps unusually well to our avatar concept\n\nAG-UI now has **Activity events** specifically designed for ongoing activity/progress, along with state snapshot/delta events. citeturn351746search0\n\nSo we could translate:\n\n```text\nHarness event\ntool: web_search\n\n        ↓\n\nour domain translator\n\nResearcherSearching\n\n        ↓\n\nAG-UI ActivitySnapshot\n\n{\n  agent: \"researcher\",\n  state: \"searching\",\n  query: \"enterprise SaaS implementation positioning\"\n}\n\n        ↓\n\nFrontend\n\nResearcherAvatar → searching\n```\n\nThen:\n\n```text\nResearcherComparingEvidence\n        ↓\nAG-UI ActivityDelta\n        ↓\navatar transitions\n```\n\nThat's extremely close to what we were going to invent ourselves.\n\n---\n\n# AG-UI also lets us keep our custom domain vocabulary\n\nIt includes a `Custom` event specifically for application-defined semantics. citeturn351746search0turn351746search1\n\nSo we can still emit:\n\n```text\ninsight.created\n\nhypothesis.updated\n\nrecommendation.proposed\n\napproval.required\n\nevidence.added\n\ndecision.confirmed\n\ntask.assigned\n```\n\nwithout modifying the standard.\n\nThat's exactly the right architecture.\n\n---\n\n# I would not necessarily use CopilotKit\n\nCopilotKit is heavily invested in AG-UI and provides React components, shared state, generative UI and human-in-the-loop functionality. It already integrates with LangGraph and many other agent frameworks. citeturn404960search0turn404960search9\n\nIt's good infrastructure.\n\nBut for **our** product I suspect it does slightly too much.\n\nOur UI is not primarily:\n\n> “embed an AI copilot into an app.”\n\nThe entire application **is the AI organization**.\n\nI'd rather use:\n\n```text\n@ag-ui/core\n@ag-ui/client\n+\nour React UI\n```\n\nand selectively use assistant-ui for conversations.\n\nThat gives us more aesthetic/product control.\n\n---\n\n# Motion for the product UI\n\nFor normal interface movement—cards entering the feed, opening detail views, drawers, hovering, reordering, transitions—I'd use **Motion for React**.\n\nMotion handles React-based layout animations, gestures, enter/exit transitions, springs and state-driven animations. citeturn362885search2turn362885search0\n\nSo:\n\n```text\nfeed card enters\ndetail expands\npost changes state\napproval collapses\ndrawer opens\n```\n\nall use Motion.\n\nBut I would keep those animations restrained.\n\nRemember:\n\n> the UI itself should stay calm.\n\n---\n\n# Rive for the little guys\n\nThis is where I think **Rive is particularly suitable**.\n\nRive has actual visual state machines consisting of states, transitions, inputs and layers, and those state machines can be driven programmatically from the application runtime. citeturn362885search10turn362885search3\n\nThat means each agent avatar could literally contain:\n\n```text\nResearcher.riv\n\nStateMachine:\n\nIDLE\nSEARCHING\nREADING\nCOMPARING\nCONNECTING\nSYNTHESIZING\nPRESENTING\nWAITING\nSUCCESS\nUNCERTAIN\nERROR\n```\n\nOur React component just says:\n\n```text\n<AgentAvatar\n    agent=\"researcher\"\n    state=\"comparing\"\n/>\n```\n\nRive handles the visual transition.\n\nThat's much better than implementing complex character animation manually with CSS.\n\nSo I would divide motion:\n\n```text\nMotion\n→ interface movement\n\nRive\n→ character movement\n```\n\nVery clean.\n\n---\n\n# TanStack Query for durable frontend data\n\nOur Feed, Core, Work, Library and History are not primarily LLM streams.\n\nThey are ordinary **server state**.\n\nTanStack Query is designed around fetching, caching, synchronizing and updating asynchronous server state, including integration with Next.js server rendering. citeturn647156search4turn647156search12\n\nSo I would have:\n\n```text\nTanStack Query\n─────────────────\n\nfeed\ncore entities\ntasks\nprojects\nartifacts\nhistory\nagents\ncomments\ndecisions\n```\n\nwhile:\n\n```text\nAG-UI\n─────────────────\n\nactive agent run\nstreaming\ntool activity\nlive state\navatar activity\ninterrupts\nlive result generation\n```\n\nThat's an important separation.\n\n---\n\n# Durable feed versus live activity\n\nI would not make AG-UI itself the database.\n\nImagine Researcher is working:\n\n```text\nLIVE\n──────────────────────────\n\nResearcher is searching...\nResearcher is comparing...\nResearcher is synthesizing...\n```\n\nThose can be transient AG-UI activity events.\n\nWhen it has something worth saying:\n\n```text\nDURABLE\n──────────────────────────\n\nInsightCreated\n        ↓\nPostgres Work/Feed store\n        ↓\nFeedItem #829\n```\n\nThen the frontend updates its TanStack Query cache.\n\nSo:\n\n```text\n       AGENT RUN\n\n           │\n\n       AG-UI events\n           │\n           ▼\n    live avatar/activity\n\n           │\n      meaningful result\n           ▼\n\n       WORK LEDGER\n        Postgres\n           │\n           ▼\n        FEED ITEM\n           │\n           ▼\n   TanStack Query cache\n```\n\nThis prevents our feed from becoming a replay of raw agent logs.\n\n---\n\n# What exactly we still need to build\n\nMost of the normal frontend machinery disappears.\n\nBut the **important product layer remains ours**.\n\n| Component | Build or reuse? |\n|---|---|\n| React framework | Next.js |\n| Accessible primitives | Radix/shadcn |\n| Styling foundation | Tailwind/CSS |\n| Server-state caching | TanStack Query |\n| Agent↔UI transport | AG-UI |\n| Chat mechanics | assistant-ui |\n| Basic UI motion | Motion |\n| Character animation runtime | Rive |\n| **Product visual system** | **OURS** |\n| **Feed architecture** | **OURS** |\n| **Feed post components** | **OURS** |\n| **Feed ranking/presentation** | **OURS** |\n| **Agent avatar designs** | **OURS** |\n| **Avatar state vocabulary** | **OURS** |\n| **Harness/LangGraph → domain event mapping** | **OURS** |\n| **Core explorer** | **OURS** |\n| **Evidence drilldown** | **OURS** |\n| **Work view** | **OURS** |\n| **Interaction semantics** | **OURS** |\n| **Approval/rejection UX** | mostly ours on primitives |\n| **Agent identity/personality UI** | **OURS** |\n| **History visualization** | **OURS** |\n\nThat's a very favorable split.\n\n---\n\n# The custom component library I would build\n\nOur codebase would eventually have concepts like:\n\n```text\ncomponents/\n│\n├── agents/\n│   ├── AgentAvatar\n│   ├── AgentIdentity\n│   ├── AgentPresence\n│   ├── AgentActivity\n│   └── AgentConversation\n│\n├── feed/\n│   ├── Feed\n│   ├── FeedItem\n│   ├── ObservationPost\n│   ├── InsightPost\n│   ├── HypothesisPost\n│   ├── RecommendationPost\n│   ├── ArtifactPost\n│   ├── QuestionPost\n│   ├── ResultPost\n│   └── LearningPost\n│\n├── knowledge/\n│   ├── EntityView\n│   ├── EvidenceTrail\n│   ├── ConfidenceIndicator\n│   ├── ProvenanceView\n│   └── HistoryTimeline\n│\n├── work/\n│   ├── Task\n│   ├── WorkResult\n│   ├── Project\n│   └── Experiment\n│\n└── interactions/\n    ├── Approve\n    ├── Reject\n    ├── Adjust\n    ├── Discuss\n    ├── Save\n    └── Feedback\n```\n\n**That component vocabulary is part of our product IP.**\n\n---\n\n# There is one frontend adapter we definitely need\n\nSomething approximately like:\n\n```text\nHarness / LangGraph\n        ↓\nRuntime events\n        ↓\n──────────────────────────────\n   OUR UI EVENT TRANSLATOR\n──────────────────────────────\n        ↓\nAG-UI\n        ↓\nFrontend\n```\n\nFor example:\n\n```text\nraw Harness:\n\ntool/call web.search\n```\n\nbecomes:\n\n```text\ndomain:\n\nresearch.search_started\n```\n\nthen:\n\n```text\nAG-UI:\n\nActivitySnapshot\n```\n\nthen:\n\n```text\nReact:\n\nagentActivityStore[\"researcher\"]\n    = SEARCHING\n```\n\nthen:\n\n```text\nRive:\n\nResearcher.searching\n```\n\nThis is probably only a modest amount of code, but architecturally it's important because **we don't want the frontend coupled directly to Harness internals**.\n\n---\n\n# And the same translator produces feed events\n\n```text\nLangGraph:\nstrategic_recommendation node finished\n\n          ↓\n\nDomain translator\n\nRecommendationCreated\n\n          ↓\n\nPostgres\n\n          ↓\n\nFeedItem\n\n          ↓\n\nFrontend\n\n<RecommendationPost />\n```\n\nSo frontend never asks:\n\n> “What is LangGraph node 8?”\n\nIt understands:\n\n> “The Strategist created a recommendation.”\n\nThat's exactly the abstraction we want.\n\n---\n\n# I would not use generative UI everywhere\n\nBoth assistant-ui and current agent-UI ecosystems can let models dynamically choose/render UI components. assistant-ui supports constrained generative UI from a component allowlist as well as LangGraph-emitted UI. citeturn971416search11turn741323search5\n\nUseful occasionally.\n\nBut I would **not** let agents dynamically design the main feed.\n\nOur product should have extremely consistent interaction grammar.\n\nThe model can decide:\n\n```text\nRecommendation\nEvidence\nQuestion\nExperiment\n```\n\nbut **we decide how Recommendation looks**.\n\nThis keeps the interface elegant and predictable.\n\n---\n\n# What I would not add\n\nI don't think we need a large dashboard framework, Material UI-style visual system, generic admin template, another frontend-agent runtime, elaborate global-state framework, or real-time collaboration product at V1.\n\nThose would either fight our design language or duplicate AG-UI/TanStack/assistant-ui.\n\nSimilarly, AI SDK UI is good infrastructure for streaming chat and tool calls and can work with custom backends, but if we adopt **AG-UI + assistant-ui**, much of its frontend role would overlap. citeturn981261search9turn981261search12\n\nSo I wouldn't automatically add it.\n\n---\n\n# My recommended frontend stack now\n\n```text\n                     PRODUCT\n\n                       NEXT.JS\n                         │\n              React / TypeScript\n                         │\n       ┌─────────────────┴─────────────────┐\n       │                                   │\n       ▼                                   ▼\n\n   PRODUCT DATA                      AGENT STREAMS\n\n TanStack Query                         AG-UI\n       │                                   │\n       ▼                                   ▼\n\nFeed / Core / Work               active agents / tools\nLibrary / History                live state / approvals\n       │                                   │\n       └─────────────────┬─────────────────┘\n                         ▼\n\n                 OUR COMPONENT SYSTEM\n\n              shadcn + Radix underneath\n\n        ┌────────────────┴─────────────────┐\n        ▼                                  ▼\n\n   PRODUCT UI                         AGENT UI\n   Motion                            assistant-ui\n                                        │\n                                        ▼\n                                      Rive\n                                  little guys\n```\n\nAnd behind AG-UI:\n\n```text\nHarness\n   +\nLangGraph\n   ↓\nour DomainEventAdapter\n   ↓\nAG-UI\n```\n\nI think this is probably the cleanest frontend architecture we've considered so far.\n\n---\n\n# What I would build first\n\n1. **Product shell + Feed.** Build the neutral design system and three post types: Insight, Recommendation and Result. Use static/fake data initially.\n\n2. **AgentAvatar component.** Build one Researcher avatar in Rive with `idle`, `searching`, `synthesizing`, `presenting`, `success` and `error`. Prove the state-driven animation concept before designing seven characters.\n\n3. **Agent conversation drawer.** Use assistant-ui primitives for chat rather than writing thread/composer/streaming mechanics ourselves.\n\n4. **AG-UI bridge.** Translate a real Researcher LangGraph/Harness run into agent activity and UI events.\n\n5. **Recommendation approval.** Build the full `recommendation → discuss → adjust → approve` loop.\n\n6. **Evidence drilldown.** Connect a feed insight back through Box objects to observations and original evidence.\n\n7. **Secondary views.** Add minimal Core, Agents, Work, Library and History once the feed interaction model works.\n\nThat would let us test the genuinely unusual part of the product very early:\n\n> **Does interacting with a company through a living feed of specialist agent characters feel materially better than another AI dashboard/chatbot?**\n\nEverything else can grow outward from there.\n\nMy strongest update after researching this is that **AG-UI is probably the missing frontend infrastructure piece** in the architecture we've been assembling. It gives us a clean standard boundary between our agent runtime and the custom frontend, in the same way MCP gives us a clean tool boundary and A2A gives us a clean external-agent boundary. citeturn351746search4turn456618search6\n\nThat leaves us owning exactly the part that should be unique: **the feed, the information hierarchy, the agent identities, the interaction semantics, and the little-guy experience.** memcite",
      "blocks": [
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Yes. Looking back across the frontend direction we developed, I think the frontend is now quite well defined. And after checking the current ecosystem, **there is a lot we should reuse—but the distinctive feed + agent-character experience should remain ours.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The key distinction is:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**Use frameworks for UI plumbing, streaming, accessibility, chat, state and animation runtimes.**\n\n**Build the actual product language ourselves.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 2,
          "text": "What we had already converged on"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The product started closer to a conventional Brand Core dashboard, but we moved away from that. The primary interface became a **private intelligence feed**, where the company’s specialist agents appear as persistent actors."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The home screen is essentially:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐\n│                                                 │\n│  🔵 Researcher                                  │\n│                                                 │\n│  \"Implementation friction appeared in 14 of    │\n│   the latest 23 enterprise conversations.\"      │\n│                                                 │\n│  Evidence 14     Confidence 84%                 │\n│                                                 │\n│  Ask   Save   Discuss                           │\n│                                                 │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                                                 │\n│  🟡 Strategist                                  │\n│                                                 │\n│  \"This may be a positioning opportunity...\"    │\n│                                                 │\n│  Approve experiment    Adjust    Discuss        │\n│                                                 │\n├─────────────────────────────────────────────────┤\n│                                                 │\n│  🟣 Storyteller                                 │\n│                                                 │\n│  \"I developed three narrative territories...\"  │\n│                                                 │\n└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But the characters aren't emoji or generic robots. We settled on **abstract little creatures with distinct anatomy**, each agent having its own silhouette, color and movement vocabulary."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "And an important visual rule emerged:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**Avatar = expression**\n**UI = container**\n**Motion = meaning**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The UI itself stays quiet: neutral surfaces, restrained typography, minimal chrome and little decorative color. Almost all expressive color comes from the agents."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That means the frontend has two visual layers:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "CALM PRODUCT LAYER\n────────────────────────\nlayout\ncards\ntext\nevidence\ncontrols\nnavigation\ndata\n\nEXPRESSIVE AGENT LAYER\n────────────────────────\ncolor\nmovement\npersonality\nworking state\nenergy\nuncertainty\nattention"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I think that's still exactly the right direction. memcite"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",

            "Surface",
            "Purpose"

              "**Feed**",

        },
        {
