          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "The feed itself should have typed posts"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I wouldn't build it as arbitrary AI-generated HTML."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Our backend should emit a typed object such as:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "ts",
          "text": "FeedItem =\n  | ObservationPost\n  | InsightPost\n  | HypothesisPost\n  | RecommendationPost\n  | ArtifactPost\n  | QuestionPost\n  | ResultPost\n  | LearningPost\n  | ExternalSignalPost"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Then **we control exactly how each type renders**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For example:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "ObservationPost\n─────────────────\nlow-level discovery\n\nInsightPost\n─────────────────\nsynthesized meaning\n\nHypothesisPost\n─────────────────\nuncertain interpretation\n\nRecommendationPost\n─────────────────\nproposed decision/action\n\nResultPost\n─────────────────\nwhat happened\n\nLearningPost\n─────────────────\nwhat the system learned"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is one of the frontend pieces we should definitely own."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "User interactions also have domain meaning"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "We had discussed:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Like\nDislike\nComment\nAsk\nSave\nApprove\nAdjust\nShare/tag"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Those aren't merely UI buttons."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Their semantics feed back into the system."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For example:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "LIKE\n→ weak preference signal\n\nCOMMENT\n→ contextual signal\n\nCORRECTION\n→ strong epistemic signal\n\nAPPROVE\n→ explicit decision\n\nADJUST\n→ modify recommendation\n\nREJECT\n→ explicit negative decision"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So the React button itself is trivial."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The meaning behind it is ours."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "The avatars should be actual state machines"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "We had settled on states roughly like:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "idle\n\nthinking\n\nsearching\n\nreading\n\ncomparing\n\nconnecting\n\nsynthesizing\n\ncreating\n\npresenting\n\nwaiting_for_approval\n\nsuccess\n\nuncertain\n\nerror"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "And those states should correspond to **real backend execution**, not random animation."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Example:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "LangGraph:\nsource_search\n\n        ↓\n\nDomain event:\nresearch.searching\n\n        ↓\n\nFrontend:\nResearcher state = SEARCHING\n\n        ↓\n\nRive:\nblue creature scans around"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Then:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "LangGraph:\ncompare_evidence\n\n        ↓\n\nResearcher state = COMPARING\n\n        ↓\n\navatar visually arranges\ntwo objects side-by-side"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This part is important because it makes the little guys a real **visualization of system state** rather than branding decoration."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "What I would reuse for the frontend"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is where the ecosystem is now quite good."
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 2,
          "text": "Next.js + React + TypeScript"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I would use **Next.js App Router** as the product shell."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "It already gives us React Server Components, Suspense, Server Functions, layouts and the modern server/client boundary we need. citeturn981261search1"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Next.js\n\n/app/feed\n/app/core\n/app/agents\n/app/work\n/app/library\n/app/history"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "No reason to invent web-app infrastructure."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "shadcn/ui + Radix for the boring UI"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is almost ideal for our aesthetic."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "shadcn/ui deliberately gives you the **actual source code of components**, rather than locking you into a component-library package, so we can change every detail to match our design language. citeturn647156search0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Underneath, Radix gives us robust accessible primitives for things like dialogs, popovers, menus, tooltips, tabs and focus/keyboard management while remaining essentially unstyled. citeturn647156search1turn647156search2"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That means we don't need to waste time implementing:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "dialog behavior\nkeyboard navigation\ndropdowns\npopovers\ntooltips\nselects\nfocus management\naccessibility"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "while still being free to make everything look completely unlike standard shadcn."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I'd use it as **construction material**, not as our visual identity."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "assistant-ui for conversations"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is one of the strongest pieces I found for us."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I would **not** use assistant-ui for our Feed."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But I would absolutely consider it for:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Agent chat\nmessage composer\nattachments\nstreaming\nmessage actions\ntool result rendering\napproval widgets\nthread behavior"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Its primitives are deliberately headless/un-styled React building blocks that already handle streaming state, message composition, keyboard behavior, scrolling and tool calls. citeturn971416search0turn971416search2"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So clicking:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "🟡 Strategist\n\n[Discuss]"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "could open:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "┌───────────────────────────────┐\n│ 🟡 Strategist                 │\n│                               │\n│ You                           │\n│ Why do you think this is      │\n│ strong enough to test?        │\n│                               │\n│ Strategist                    │\n│ Three reasons...              │\n│                               │\n│ [evidence card]               │\n│                               │\n│ ┌───────────────────────────┐ │\n│ │ Ask Strategist...         │ │\n│ └───────────────────────────┘ │\n└───────────────────────────────┘"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "without us implementing the entire streaming-chat interaction model."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "assistant-ui also has explicit support for rendering tool calls as custom interactive React components and human-interaction tools. citeturn971416search1turn971416search3"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That fits things like:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Strategist requests approval\n\n┌────────────────────────────┐\n│ Run positioning experiment │\n│                            │\n│ Estimated duration: 2 wks  │\n│                            │\n│ [Approve]      [Adjust]     │\n└────────────────────────────┘"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "very nicely."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "The really interesting new addition: AG-UI"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is the frontend equivalent of MCP/A2A."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "We already have:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "MCP\nAgent ↔ Tools\n\nA2A\nAgent ↔ External Agents"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I would seriously consider adding:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "AG-UI\nAgent ↔ User Interface"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "AG-UI is an open event protocol specifically for agent-to-frontend communication. It covers run lifecycle, streamed text, tool calls, synchronized state, ongoing activity, human interaction and custom events. citeturn971416search8turn351746search4"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This could save us from inventing our own WebSocket/event protocol."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Our architecture becomes:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "                BACKEND\n\n        Harness + LangGraph\n               │\n               ▼\n       Domain Event Adapter\n               │\n               ▼\n             AG-UI\n               │\n       SSE / HTTP stream\n               │\n               ▼\n\n               FRONTEND"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "AG-UI's JavaScript client already exposes event subscriptions, state tracking, aborting runs and an observable event stream. citeturn456618search0turn456618search1turn456618search2"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "And AG-UI maps unusually well to our avatar concept"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "AG-UI now has **Activity events** specifically designed for ongoing activity/progress, along with state snapshot/delta events. citeturn351746search0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So we could translate:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Harness event\ntool: web_search\n\n        ↓\n\nour domain translator\n\nResearcherSearching\n\n        ↓\n\nAG-UI ActivitySnapshot\n\n{\n  agent: \"researcher\",\n  state: \"searching\",\n  query: \"enterprise SaaS implementation positioning\"\n}\n\n        ↓\n\nFrontend\n\nResearcherAvatar → searching"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Then:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "ResearcherComparingEvidence\n        ↓\nAG-UI ActivityDelta\n        ↓\navatar transitions"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's extremely close to what we were going to invent ourselves."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "AG-UI also lets us keep our custom domain vocabulary"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "It includes a `Custom` event specifically for application-defined semantics. citeturn351746search0turn351746search1"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So we can still emit:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "insight.created\n\nhypothesis.updated\n\nrecommendation.proposed\n\napproval.required\n\nevidence.added\n\ndecision.confirmed\n\ntask.assigned"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "without modifying the standard."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's exactly the right architecture."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "I would not necessarily use CopilotKit"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "CopilotKit is heavily invested in AG-UI and provides React components, shared state, generative UI and human-in-the-loop functionality. It already integrates with LangGraph and many other agent frameworks. citeturn404960search0turn404960search9"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "It's good infrastructure."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But for **our** product I suspect it does slightly too much."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Our UI is not primarily:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "“embed an AI copilot into an app.”"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The entire application **is the AI organization**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I'd rather use:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "@ag-ui/core\n@ag-ui/client\n+\nour React UI"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "and selectively use assistant-ui for conversations."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That gives us more aesthetic/product control."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Motion for the product UI"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For normal interface movement—cards entering the feed, opening detail views, drawers, hovering, reordering, transitions—I'd use **Motion for React**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Motion handles React-based layout animations, gestures, enter/exit transitions, springs and state-driven animations. citeturn362885search2turn362885search0"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "feed card enters\ndetail expands\npost changes state\napproval collapses\ndrawer opens"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "all use Motion."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But I would keep those animations restrained."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Remember:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "the UI itself should stay calm."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Rive for the little guys"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is where I think **Rive is particularly suitable**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Rive has actual visual state machines consisting of states, transitions, inputs and layers, and those state machines can be driven programmatically from the application runtime. citeturn362885search10turn362885search3"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That means each agent avatar could literally contain:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Researcher.riv\n\nStateMachine:\n\nIDLE\nSEARCHING\nREADING\nCOMPARING\nCONNECTING\nSYNTHESIZING\nPRESENTING\nWAITING\nSUCCESS\nUNCERTAIN\nERROR"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Our React component just says:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "<AgentAvatar\n    agent=\"researcher\"\n    state=\"comparing\"\n/>"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Rive handles the visual transition."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's much better than implementing complex character animation manually with CSS."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So I would divide motion:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Motion\n→ interface movement\n\nRive\n→ character movement"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Very clean."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "TanStack Query for durable frontend data"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Our Feed, Core, Work, Library and History are not primarily LLM streams."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "They are ordinary **server state**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "TanStack Query is designed around fetching, caching, synchronizing and updating asynchronous server state, including integration with Next.js server rendering. citeturn647156search4turn647156search12"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So I would have:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "TanStack Query\n─────────────────\n\nfeed\ncore entities\ntasks\nprojects\nartifacts\nhistory\nagents\ncomments\ndecisions"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "while:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "AG-UI\n─────────────────\n\nactive agent run\nstreaming\ntool activity\nlive state\navatar activity\ninterrupts\nlive result generation"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's an important separation."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "Durable feed versus live activity"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I would not make AG-UI itself the database."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Imagine Researcher is working:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "LIVE\n──────────────────────────\n\nResearcher is searching...\nResearcher is comparing...\nResearcher is synthesizing..."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Those can be transient AG-UI activity events."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "When it has something worth saying:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "DURABLE\n──────────────────────────\n\nInsightCreated\n        ↓\nPostgres Work/Feed store\n        ↓\nFeedItem #829"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Then the frontend updates its TanStack Query cache."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "       AGENT RUN\n\n           │\n\n       AG-UI events\n           │\n           ▼\n    live avatar/activity\n\n           │\n      meaningful result\n           ▼\n\n       WORK LEDGER\n        Postgres\n           │\n           ▼\n        FEED ITEM\n           │\n           ▼\n   TanStack Query cache"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This prevents our feed from becoming a replay of raw agent logs."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "What exactly we still need to build"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Most of the normal frontend machinery disappears."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But the **important product layer remains ours**."
        },
        {
          "type": "table",
          "header": [
            "Component",
            "Build or reuse?"
          ],
          "rows": [
            [
              "React framework",
              "Next.js"
            ],
            [
              "Accessible primitives",
              "Radix/shadcn"
            ],
            [
              "Styling foundation",
              "Tailwind/CSS"
            ],
            [
              "Server-state caching",
              "TanStack Query"
            ],
            [
              "Agent↔UI transport",
              "AG-UI"
            ],
            [
              "Chat mechanics",
              "assistant-ui"
            ],
            [
              "Basic UI motion",
              "Motion"
            ],
            [
              "Character animation runtime",
              "Rive"
            ],
            [
              "**Product visual system**",
              "**OURS**"
            ],
            [
              "**Feed architecture**",
              "**OURS**"
            ],
            [
              "**Feed post components**",
              "**OURS**"
            ],
            [
              "**Feed ranking/presentation**",
              "**OURS**"
            ],
            [
              "**Agent avatar designs**",
              "**OURS**"
            ],
            [
              "**Avatar state vocabulary**",
              "**OURS**"
            ],
            [
              "**Harness/LangGraph → domain event mapping**",
              "**OURS**"
            ],
            [
              "**Core explorer**",
              "**OURS**"
            ],
            [
              "**Evidence drilldown**",
              "**OURS**"
            ],
            [
              "**Work view**",
              "**OURS**"
            ],
            [
              "**Interaction semantics**",
              "**OURS**"
            ],
            [
              "**Approval/rejection UX**",
              "mostly ours on primitives"
            ],
            [
              "**Agent identity/personality UI**",
              "**OURS**"
            ],
            [
              "**History visualization**",
              "**OURS**"
            ]
          ]
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's a very favorable split."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "The custom component library I would build"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Our codebase would eventually have concepts like:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "components/\n│\n├── agents/\n│   ├── AgentAvatar\n│   ├── AgentIdentity\n│   ├── AgentPresence\n│   ├── AgentActivity\n│   └── AgentConversation\n│\n├── feed/\n│   ├── Feed\n│   ├── FeedItem\n│   ├── ObservationPost\n│   ├── InsightPost\n│   ├── HypothesisPost\n│   ├── RecommendationPost\n│   ├── ArtifactPost\n│   ├── QuestionPost\n│   ├── ResultPost\n│   └── LearningPost\n│\n├── knowledge/\n│   ├── EntityView\n│   ├── EvidenceTrail\n│   ├── ConfidenceIndicator\n│   ├── ProvenanceView\n│   └── HistoryTimeline\n│\n├── work/\n│   ├── Task\n│   ├── WorkResult\n│   ├── Project\n│   └── Experiment\n│\n└── interactions/\n    ├── Approve\n    ├── Reject\n    ├── Adjust\n    ├── Discuss\n    ├── Save\n    └── Feedback"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "**That component vocabulary is part of our product IP.**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "There is one frontend adapter we definitely need"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Something approximately like:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Harness / LangGraph\n        ↓\nRuntime events\n        ↓\n──────────────────────────────\n   OUR UI EVENT TRANSLATOR\n──────────────────────────────\n        ↓\nAG-UI\n        ↓\nFrontend"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "For example:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "raw Harness:\n\ntool/call web.search"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "becomes:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "domain:\n\nresearch.search_started"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "then:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "AG-UI:\n\nActivitySnapshot"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "then:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "React:\n\nagentActivityStore[\"researcher\"]\n    = SEARCHING"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "then:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Rive:\n\nResearcher.searching"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This is probably only a modest amount of code, but architecturally it's important because **we don't want the frontend coupled directly to Harness internals**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "And the same translator produces feed events"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "LangGraph:\nstrategic_recommendation node finished\n\n          ↓\n\nDomain translator\n\nRecommendationCreated\n\n          ↓\n\nPostgres\n\n          ↓\n\nFeedItem\n\n          ↓\n\nFrontend\n\n<RecommendationPost />"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So frontend never asks:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "“What is LangGraph node 8?”"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "It understands:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "“The Strategist created a recommendation.”"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That's exactly the abstraction we want."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "I would not use generative UI everywhere"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Both assistant-ui and current agent-UI ecosystems can let models dynamically choose/render UI components. assistant-ui supports constrained generative UI from a component allowlist as well as LangGraph-emitted UI. citeturn971416search11turn741323search5"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Useful occasionally."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "But I would **not** let agents dynamically design the main feed."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Our product should have extremely consistent interaction grammar."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "The model can decide:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Recommendation\nEvidence\nQuestion\nExperiment"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "but **we decide how Recommendation looks**."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "This keeps the interface elegant and predictable."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "What I would not add"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I don't think we need a large dashboard framework, Material UI-style visual system, generic admin template, another frontend-agent runtime, elaborate global-state framework, or real-time collaboration product at V1."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Those would either fight our design language or duplicate AG-UI/TanStack/assistant-ui."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Similarly, AI SDK UI is good infrastructure for streaming chat and tool calls and can work with custom backends, but if we adopt **AG-UI + assistant-ui**, much of its frontend role would overlap. citeturn981261search9turn981261search12"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "So I wouldn't automatically add it."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "My recommended frontend stack now"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "                     PRODUCT\n\n                       NEXT.JS\n                         │\n              React / TypeScript\n                         │\n       ┌─────────────────┴─────────────────┐\n       │                                   │\n       ▼                                   ▼\n\n   PRODUCT DATA                      AGENT STREAMS\n\n TanStack Query                         AG-UI\n       │                                   │\n       ▼                                   ▼\n\nFeed / Core / Work               active agents / tools\nLibrary / History                live state / approvals\n       │                                   │\n       └─────────────────┬─────────────────┘\n                         ▼\n\n                 OUR COMPONENT SYSTEM\n\n              shadcn + Radix underneath\n\n        ┌────────────────┴─────────────────┐\n        ▼                                  ▼\n\n   PRODUCT UI                         AGENT UI\n   Motion                            assistant-ui\n                                        │\n                                        ▼\n                                      Rive\n                                  little guys"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "And behind AG-UI:"
        },
        {
          "type": "code",
          "language": "text",
          "text": "Harness\n   +\nLangGraph\n   ↓\nour DomainEventAdapter\n   ↓\nAG-UI"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "I think this is probably the cleanest frontend architecture we've considered so far."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "---"
        },
        {
          "type": "heading",
          "level": 1,
          "text": "What I would build first"
        },
        {
          "type": "list",
          "ordered": true,
          "items": [
            "**Product shell + Feed.** Build the neutral design system and three post types: Insight, Recommendation and Result. Use static/fake data initially."
          ]
        },
        {
          "type": "list",
          "ordered": true,
          "items": [
            "**AgentAvatar component.** Build one Researcher avatar in Rive with `idle`, `searching`, `synthesizing`, `presenting`, `success` and `error`. Prove the state-driven animation concept before designing seven characters."
          ]
        },
        {
          "type": "list",
          "ordered": true,
          "items": [
            "**Agent conversation drawer.** Use assistant-ui primitives for chat rather than writing thread/composer/streaming mechanics ourselves."
          ]
        },
        {
          "type": "list",
          "ordered": true,
          "items": [
            "**AG-UI bridge.** Translate a real Researcher LangGraph/Harness run into agent activity and UI events."
          ]
        },
        {
          "type": "list",
          "ordered": true,
          "items": [
            "**Recommendation approval.** Build the full `recommendation → discuss → adjust → approve` loop."
          ]
        },
        {
          "type": "list",
          "ordered": true,
          "items": [
            "**Evidence drilldown.** Connect a feed insight back through Box objects to observations and original evidence."
          ]
        },
        {
          "type": "list",
          "ordered": true,
          "items": [
            "**Secondary views.** Add minimal Core, Agents, Work, Library and History once the feed interaction model works."
          ]
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That would let us test the genuinely unusual part of the product very early:"
        },
        {
          "type": "blockquote",
          "text": "**Does interacting with a company through a living feed of specialist agent characters feel materially better than another AI dashboard/chatbot?**"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "Everything else can grow outward from there."
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "My strongest update after researching this is that **AG-UI is probably the missing frontend infrastructure piece** in the architecture we've been assembling. It gives us a clean standard boundary between our agent runtime and the custom frontend, in the same way MCP gives us a clean tool boundary and A2A gives us a clean external-agent boundary. citeturn351746search4turn456618search6"
        },
        {
          "type": "paragraph",
          "text": "That leaves us owning exactly the part that should be unique: **the feed, the information hierarchy, the agent identities, the interaction semantics, and the little-guy experience.** memcite"
        }

    {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "Yes. If we strip away everything handled by infrastructure and list **only what we actually need to design/build**, I would organize the project into these areas:\n\n1. **Brand/Marketing Ontology** — the formal model of a company's immaterial world: Company, Product, Audience, Problem, Motivation, Claim, Evidence, Positioning, Narrative, Competitor, Campaign, Decision, etc.; their relationships and schemas.\n\n2. **Knowledge Processing System** — our rules for turning raw information into that ontology: source classification, source-specific chunking, extraction algorithms, entity resolution, relationship extraction, deduplication, evidence linking and provenance rules.\n\n3. **Truth & Epistemic System** — how the system distinguishes observations, interpretations, hypotheses, proposals, confirmed knowledge, rejected beliefs and superseded knowledge; confidence, contradiction handling, evidence weighting and human confirmation.\n\n4. **Progressive Abstraction System** — the hierarchy from raw source → evidence → observation → pattern → insight → strategic knowledge → company model, including how higher abstractions are created, updated and linked back to evidence.\n\n5. **Box API** — our stable interface over Cognee/analytics infrastructure: `search`, `related`, `evidence`, `history`, `observe`, `propose`, `confirm`, `reject`, `recordDecision`, etc.\n\n6. **Analytics Interface** — our semantic layer over numeric/business data: standardized metrics, campaign/CRM/analytics queries, experiment results and the interface agents use to combine quantitative evidence with Box knowledge.\n\n7. **Context Compiler** — arguably one of the most important pieces: given `agent + task + current state`, determine what knowledge is relevant, at what abstraction level, how much evidence is needed, when to drill deeper, and package it into a clean `ContextPackage`.\n\n8. **Agent Definitions** — define the specialist team: Researcher, Strategist, Storyteller, Growth, Brand Guardian, Director/orchestrator, etc.; responsibilities, boundaries, capabilities, permissions and personalities.\n\n9. **Reasoning Architectures** — the actual intelligence algorithms executed through LangGraph: how each specialist decomposes problems, generates hypotheses, seeks evidence, challenges itself, consults other agents, resolves uncertainty, makes decisions and knows when to stop.\n\n10. **Cross-Agent Work Model** — our lightweight organizational semantics: `Task`, `Artifact`, `Event`, `Dependency`, `Insight`, `Hypothesis`, `Recommendation`, `Decision`, `Experiment`, `Result`; plus assignment, dependencies, completion and escalation.\n\n11. **Director / Coordination Logic** — determine who should work on a problem, break larger objectives into tasks, parallelize work, manage dependencies, request specialist reviews, prevent duplicated work and escalate to the human.\n\n12. **Domain Tools** — higher-level marketing tools exposed to agents, such as `find_customer_evidence()`, `compare_positioning()`, `analyze_campaign()`, `propose_brand_change()`, `create_experiment()`, rather than exposing raw databases/APIs everywhere.\n\n13. **Model Policy** — not the model gateway itself, but our rules for which model should handle extraction, classification, research, deep reasoning, creative exploration, verification, etc., including fallbacks and cost/quality policies.\n\n14. **Learning & Feedback System** — define what likes, dislikes, comments, corrections, approvals, rejections and real-world outcomes mean; how they influence future retrieval, confidence, hypotheses and decisions without incorrectly turning feedback into “truth.”\n\n15. **Evaluation System** — our marketing-specific definition of good: extraction accuracy, evidence grounding, retrieval quality, strategic quality, originality, brand coherence, decision quality, hallucination rate, etc.; plus test cases and regression suites.\n\n16. **Domain Event Layer** — translate low-level Harness/LangGraph/tool events into product concepts such as `research.searching`, `insight.created`, `recommendation.proposed`, `approval.required`, `experiment.completed`. This becomes the stable bridge to the frontend.\n\n17. **Feed System** — feed model, ranking/prioritization and typed posts: Observation, Insight, Hypothesis, Recommendation, Question, Artifact, Result, Learning and External Signal; plus deciding what deserves to become a post rather than remaining background work.\n\n18. **Interaction Semantics** — what happens when someone likes, comments, discusses, corrects, adjusts, approves, rejects, saves or asks an agent about something.\n\n19. **Evidence/Knowledge Explorer** — the UX for progressively moving from a high-level statement down through insight → pattern → observations → evidence → original source, and exploring relationships in the Brand Box.\n\n20. **Work Experience** — projects, active tasks, agent assignments, experiments, dependencies, approvals, status and completed work. Not necessarily a conventional project-management dashboard; it should fit the feed-first product.\n\n21. **Agent Conversation Experience** — direct conversations with individual agents while preserving references to Box knowledge, feed posts, tasks, artifacts and decisions.\n\n22. **Agent Character System** — the distinct “species”/anatomy language, silhouette, personality, color, behavior and identity of every little guy.\n\n23. **Agent Motion Language** — map meaningful computational states such as searching, reading, comparing, connecting, synthesizing, creating, uncertain, waiting and succeeding into distinct Rive animations.\n\n24. **Visual/Product Design System** — the intentionally quiet surrounding UI: typography, spacing, surfaces, cards, information density, interaction patterns, responsive behavior and accessibility. Color/action largely comes from agents.\n\n25. **Core Product Frontend** — implement Feed, Core, Agents, Work, Library, History, Evidence views, conversations, settings/configuration and onboarding using the reusable frontend infrastructure we've selected.\n\n26. **Client Setup & Configuration System** — because this is initially a configured service rather than pure self-serve SaaS: create client, connect sources, define products/markets, configure ontology extensions, choose agents, set permissions, validate extracted knowledge and launch the system.\n\n27. **Runtime Adapters** — the deliberately thin interfaces isolating our IP from dependencies: `BoxAdapter → Cognee`, `AgentRuntime → Harness`, `ReasoningRuntime → LangGraph`, `ModelGateway → LiteLLM`, integrations → Nango, frontend stream → AG-UI.\n\n28. **Security/Permission Semantics** — our rules for what each agent/user/client can read, write, approve and execute, even if underlying authentication/storage enforcement comes from existing infrastructure.\n\n29. **Observability Integration** — instrument our custom reasoning, context compilation, extraction and agent work so Langfuse can actually tell us why something succeeded or failed.\n\n30. **Onboarding / Initial Brand Build** — the workflow that takes a new company from messy sources to a usable initial Box: ingest → extract → resolve → synthesize → identify contradictions/gaps → human validation → generate initial Brand World → activate agents.\n\nIf I compress all of that into the **actual intellectual core**, we're really building six things:\n\n> **1. A formal representation of a brand/company.**\n> **2. A system for turning evidence into reliable evolving knowledge.**\n> **3. A system for giving an intelligence exactly the right context.**\n> **4. Expert marketing reasoning algorithms.**\n> **5. A model of how a team of those intelligences works together and learns.**\n> **6. A distinctive human interface for interacting with that artificial organization.**\n\nEverything else should be adapters, configuration, testing and product engineering around those six.\n\nThat is the scope I would use as the project's master decomposition going forward. memcite",

      "content": "We discussed something more specific than ordinary progressive abstraction: **the Box should maintain multiple abstracted indexes of the same underlying company world, organized both by abstraction level and by semantic dimension.**\n\nThe idea was roughly:\n\n```text\n                    THE BOX\n                       │\n        ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐\n        │              │              │\n     CUSTOMER        BRAND          MARKET\n     dimension       dimension      dimension\n        │              │              │\n   motivations     positioning    competitors\n   problems        narrative      categories\n   objections      principles     trends\n   language        claims         alternatives\n```\n\nBut each dimension also exists at **multiple abstraction levels**:\n\n```text\nHIGH ABSTRACTION\n────────────────────────\nStrategic model\nMajor truths\nKey tensions\nCurrent positioning\nCore customer model\n\n        ↑\n\nInsights / patterns\n────────────────────────\n\"Implementation friction is\na major enterprise concern\"\n\n        ↑\n\nObservations / facts\n────────────────────────\n\"18/24 enterprise interviews\nmention implementation effort\"\n\n        ↑\n\nEvidence\n────────────────────────\nquotes / CRM records / metrics\n\n        ↑\n\nRaw sources\n────────────────────────\ncalls / docs / websites / data\n```\n\nSo it isn't one hierarchy. It's more like a **multidimensional semantic index over the Brand World**.\n\nFor example, one customer quote might simultaneously be indexed as:\n\n```text\nQuote #1827\n\nDIMENSIONS\ncustomer.problem\ncustomer.motivation\nproduct.onboarding\npositioning.speed\nenterprise\n\nABSTRACTION\nevidence\n\nTIME\n2026-Q2\n\nEPISTEMIC STATUS\nobservation\n\nSOURCE\ncustomer_interview\n\nCONFIDENCE\nhigh\n```\n\nThen higher-order objects derived from it might be indexed differently:\n\n```text\nInsight #92\n\nDIMENSIONS\ncustomer.problem\npositioning.opportunity\nenterprise\n\nABSTRACTION\ninsight\n\nEPISTEMIC STATUS\nhypothesis\n\nSUPPORTED BY\nEvidence #1827\nEvidence #1922\nEvidence #2011\n...\n```\n\n### Why we wanted this\n\nIt makes the Context Compiler much more intelligent than ordinary vector search.\n\nInstead of asking:\n\n> \"What text is semantically similar to this task?\"\n\nit can ask:\n\n> \"For this **strategy** problem, give me **customer + positioning + competitor** knowledge, initially at **high abstraction**, restricted to **current/confirmed** knowledge.\"\n\nSomething like:\n\n```text\nTask\n\"Should we reposition enterprise?\"\n\n        ↓\n\ndimensions:\ncustomer\npositioning\ncompetitors\nproduct proof\n\n        +\n\nabstraction:\nstrategic → insight\n\n        +\n\nepistemic:\nconfirmed + strong hypotheses\n\n        +\n\ntime:\ncurrent\n\n        ↓\n\nretrieve\n```\n\nIf the Strategist needs more evidence:\n\n```text\nstrategic knowledge\n        ↓\ninsights\n        ↓\npatterns\n        ↓\nobservations\n        ↓\nevidence\n        ↓\nraw source\n```\n\nSo it **progressively drills downward** rather than loading everything upfront.\n\nAnd there are other useful indexing dimensions beyond topic:\n\n```text\nSEMANTIC\ncustomer / product / brand / market / competitor...\n\nABSTRACTION\nsource → evidence → observation → pattern → insight → strategy\n\nEPISTEMIC\nobserved / inferred / hypothesized / confirmed / rejected\n\nTEMPORAL\nhistorical / current / emerging / superseded\n\nSOURCE\ninterview / CRM / analytics / founder / website...\n\nCONFIDENCE\nlow → high\n\nSCOPE\ncompany / product / market / segment / persona / campaign\n\nRELATIONSHIP\nsupports / contradicts / derives-from / supersedes / causes...\n```\n\nThe important idea was **not to physically duplicate the knowledge into dozens of databases**.\n\nThe underlying knowledge remains connected in Cognee/the Box. These dimensions become metadata, graph relationships, typed objects and specialized indexes/retrievers.\n\nConceptually:\n\n```text\n                  ONE KNOWLEDGE WORLD\n                         │\n            ┌────────────┼────────────┐\n            ↓            ↓            ↓\n        Customer      Strategy      Market\n          view          view          view\n            │            │            │\n            └────────────┼────────────┘\n                         │\n                  abstraction level\n                         │\n                  epistemic status\n                         │\n                       time\n                         │\n                     evidence\n```\n\nI think this should actually be elevated from a sub-feature of the \"Progressive Abstraction System\" in my previous list into its own core component:\n\n> **Dimensional Knowledge Index + Progressive Abstraction Architecture**\n\nBecause together with the Context Compiler, this is potentially one of the most important architectural ideas in the system: **represent the company's world once, but make it cheaply accessible through many semantic perspectives and at different resolutions.** memcite",

I reviewed the market around the **full architecture we have now**, not just “AI marketing tools.” The result is more encouraging and more cautionary than when we started.\n\nThe most important finding is this:\n\n> **The market is converging toward almost exactly the architecture we designed.**\n\nBCG’s June 2026 CMO survey describes the emerging winning marketing stack as a combination of a **data foundation, brand-intelligence layer, multi-agent orchestration, and unified marketer interface**. Only 8% of surveyed CMOs said they were already running campaigns with multiple autonomous agents, while 42% were still using GenAI mainly for discrete task assistance. BCG explicitly argues that the next competitive layer is the operating infrastructure connecting these pieces. citeturn846322view0turn846322view1\n\nThat is remarkably close to:\n\n```text\nOur Box\n    ↓\nContext Compiler\n    ↓\nspecialist reasoning\n    ↓\nmulti-agent system\n    ↓\ntools / execution\n    ↓\nunified feed\n```\n\nThat strongly validates the **problem and timing**.\n\nIt also means the architecture itself is **not a moat anymore**.\n\n---\n\n## My current market assessment\n\n| Dimension | Assessment |\n|---|---:|\n| Market timing | **9.5/10** |\n| Evidence of real demand | **9/10** |\n| Competitive intensity | **9/10** |\n| Broad “AI Marketing OS” differentiation | **3/10** |\n| Our deeper intelligence architecture differentiation | **7.5–8/10** |\n| Opportunity below large-enterprise suites | **8/10** |\n| Technical feasibility with our infrastructure stack | **8.5/10** |\n| GTM difficulty | **7.5/10** |\n| Potential long-term defensibility | **8/10 if we build the intelligence moat** |\n| Overall opportunity | **~8/10** |\n\nI would pursue it.\n\nBut I would **not market it simply as “an AI Marketing OS.”**\n\nThat phrase is becoming commoditized.\n\n---\n\n# The market has moved very fast\n\nWhen we initially discussed the concept, “brand brain + marketing agents” felt relatively unusual.\n\nIt isn't anymore.\n\nAdobe launched **Brand Intelligence** inside GenStudio in April 2026. Adobe describes it as a continuously learning brand engine that learns not only from guidelines but also from annotations, approvals, rejections and review feedback, then makes that intelligence available to agents across planning and content-production workflows. Adobe Workfront can also treat agents as assignable project resources. citeturn372999view0turn372999view1\n\nThat is quite close to parts of our Brand Box + feedback + agent-work model.\n\nTypeface is even closer conceptually. Its **Arc Graph** creates a dynamic brand system from DAMs, CMSs and knowledge bases; connects brand rules with audience data, performance insights and compliance; and feeds specialist Arc Agents working inside a shared marketing workspace. citeturn372999view2turn372999view3\n\nGradial describes itself as an **AI-native marketing organization platform**, connects people, agents, tools, context and governance, and explicitly says its long-term organizational memory is a **knowledge graph that agents reference and act on**. Its emphasis is execution across CMS/DAM/email/web/marketing operations. citeturn372999view4turn372999view5\n\nHightouch has gone beyond CDP infrastructure into an Agentic Marketing Platform with **Agents, a Context Hub, campaign intelligence, creative, experimentation and AI Decisioning**. Its AI Decisioning agents use reinforcement learning to optimize message, timing and channel based on actual outcomes. citeturn372999view6turn898752search2\n\nJasper now explicitly calls itself a **marketing agents platform**. Its Jasper IQ layer combines Brand IQ, Marketing IQ and company knowledge and applies that persistent context across agents and workflows. citeturn770997search1turn770997search3\n\nOptimizely Opal now offers customizable marketing agents, workflows, company context and experimentation. Optimizely says almost 1,700 customers had built more than 4,000 agents and executed them more than 172,000 times by May 2026. citeturn642582search1turn642582search2\n\nSo the signal is very strong:\n\n> **Agentic marketing is real. Brand context is becoming foundational. Persistent company context is becoming expected.**\n\n---\n\n# There is also a second competitive wave below enterprise\n\nThis is important.\n\nA lot of very young products now openly use **“Marketing Operating System”**, **“AI Marketing Team”**, or nearly identical language.\n\nNano claims six marketing agents, brand intelligence, strategy, campaigns, analytics and autonomous execution; its publicly listed plans run from free to $299/month. citeturn514194search0\n\nSintra sells a collection of marketing specialists and “Brain AI” at consumer/prosumer-style pricing. citeturn514194search1\n\nNimbus calls itself an autonomous Marketing OS and combines Brand DNA, Product DNA, strategy, content, advertising, analytics and closed-loop experimentation. citeturn514194search2\n\nCleo presents itself as an AI marketing director that researches the market, creates strategy, produces content, runs campaigns and analyzes performance, aimed at founders and small teams. citeturn514194search3\n\nEven Ahrefs has launched Agent A/Letaido around always-on marketing agents, reports, tooling and automations. citeturn566023search13\n\nSo if our website says:\n\n> “Meet your AI marketing team. Six agents that understand your brand and work 24/7.”\n\nwe are entering a **price-compressed red ocean**.\n\nThat's the first major conclusion from the research.\n\n---\n\n# Where the enterprise competitors are strongest\n\nThe closest products cluster around particular centers of gravity.\n\n| Player | Their center of gravity | Overlap with us | Main difference |\n|---|---|---:|---|\n| **Typeface** | Brand context + content + agents | Very high | Enterprise content/campaign orientation |\n| **Adobe** | Content supply chain + brand intelligence | Very high | Adobe ecosystem, enterprise creative execution |\n| **Gradial** | Agentic marketing operations | Very high | Execution-first |\n| **Hightouch** | Customer data + lifecycle decisioning | High | Customer activation/personalization-first |\n| **Jasper** | Brand-governed marketing content | High | Content still central |\n| **Optimizely** | DXP + experimentation + agents | High | Existing Optimizely experience stack |\n| **Salesforce** | CRM/CDP + customer journey agents | High | Salesforce ecosystem/customer activation |\n| **HubSpot** | CRM-native growth agents | Medium-high | HubSpot-centric and workflow/task focused |\n| **Frontify** | Brand source-of-truth | Medium | Brand management rather than intelligence organization |\n| **Dovetail/Sprig/Zappi** | Customer intelligence/research | Medium | Insights without full marketing organization |\n\nSalesforce, for example, now describes Agentforce Marketing as an “agency of agents” spanning planning, creation, optimization and customer experiences on top of its CDP. citeturn325486search1 HubSpot similarly lets customers build/customize agents with instructions, tools and knowledge vaults inside the CRM. citeturn566023search0turn566023search5\n\nAt the brand-management end, Frontify is explicitly positioning itself as a **machine-readable source of brand intelligence** accessible to external agents through MCP and APIs. citeturn770997search2turn770997search4\n\nAt the customer-intelligence end, Dovetail now connects sales calls, support, surveys, research and feedback into evidence-backed customer intelligence; Sprig has specialized Design, Field and Synthesize research agents; and Zappi combines persistent consumer research with AI-assisted brand, innovation and ad decisions. citeturn693482search15turn693482search9turn693482search4\n\n---\n\n# Where I still see meaningful whitespace\n\nHere's where our architecture becomes important.\n\nMost competitors publicly organize their systems around one of these:\n\n```text\ncontent\ncustomer activation\nbrand governance\nresearch\ncampaign execution\nCRM\nexperimentation\n```\n\nWe're proposing something subtly different:\n\n```text\n             COMPANY REALITY\n\nbrand ─ customer ─ market ─ product ─ performance\n                 │\n                 ▼\n         structured model\n                 │\n                 ▼\n        evidence / history\n                 │\n                 ▼\n          expert reasoning\n                 │\n                 ▼\n            decisions\n                 │\n                 ▼\n             actions\n                 │\n                 ▼\n             learning\n```\n\nThat distinction matters.\n\nOur core object isn't a **campaign**.\n\nIt isn't a **piece of content**.\n\nIt isn't a **customer profile**.\n\nIt isn't a **brand guideline**.\n\nIt's the company's evolving **marketing model of reality**.\n\nI did not find a direct marketing competitor publicly describing the whole system with the epistemic depth we've discussed: explicit `Observation → Pattern → Insight → Hypothesis → Confirmed Knowledge → Decision`, source provenance, contradiction handling, temporal validity, dimensional indexing and progressive abstraction across brand + customer + market + performance. That does **not** prove competitors lack these capabilities internally, but it does suggest this is not yet the standard public product model. citeturn372999view0turn372999view2turn372999view4turn372999view6\n\nThat is the area I would protect.\n\n---\n\n# The Box is still interesting — but only the deeper version\n\nSimply having:\n\n```text\nbrand voice\npersona\nguidelines\nproducts\ncompetitors\n```\n\nis no longer differentiated.\n\nAdobe, Typeface, Jasper, Frontify, Hightouch and dozens of smaller products are moving there. citeturn372999view0turn372999view2turn770997search1turn770997search2turn372999view6\n\nOur Box needs to become:\n\n```text\n                        THE BOX\n\n             WHAT THE COMPANY KNOWS\n                       +\n             WHY IT BELIEVES IT\n                       +\n             HOW CERTAIN IT IS\n                       +\n             WHEN IT WAS TRUE\n                       +\n             WHAT CONTRADICTS IT\n                       +\n             WHAT IT WAS DERIVED FROM\n                       +\n             WHICH DIMENSION IT BELONGS TO\n                       +\n             WHAT ABSTRACTION LEVEL IT IS\n```\n\nThat's materially different from a “Brand Knowledge Base.”\n\n---\n\n# I like the dimensional progressive abstraction architecture even more now\n\nThis may be one of the least commoditized parts of what we've designed.\n\nRather than searching a flat knowledge base:\n\n```text\nquery → embeddings → documents\n```\n\nwe can reason over:\n\n```text\nDOMAIN\nbrand / customer / market / competitor / product / performance\n\n×\n\nABSTRACTION\nsource → evidence → observation → pattern → insight → strategy\n\n×\n\nEPISTEMIC STATUS\nobserved → inferred → hypothesized → confirmed → rejected\n\n×\n\nTIME\nhistorical → current → emerging → superseded\n\n×\n\nSCOPE\ncompany → product → segment → persona → campaign\n```\n\nThe Context Compiler can then retrieve:\n\n> current + customer + positioning + strategic-level + confirmed/high-confidence\n\nbefore deciding whether to descend into raw evidence.\n\nI didn't find a direct marketing platform publicly presenting retrieval this way.\n\nThat's technically invisible to customers, but it could produce a visibly **better intelligence product**.\n\n---\n\n# The Context Compiler may be more valuable than the agents\n\nThis is another conclusion I feel stronger about.\n\nThe market is rapidly commoditizing agents.\n\nHubSpot lets people customize agents. Optimizely customers have already built thousands of them. Salesforce offers an agency of agents. Jasper has purpose-built marketing agents. Typeface has specialist agents. citeturn566023search5turn642582search2turn325486search1turn770997search3turn372999view3\n\nSo:\n\n> “We have a Strategist Agent”\n\nisn't valuable by itself.\n\nBut:\n\n> “The Strategist automatically receives the correct current strategic context, customer evidence, contradictions, historical decisions and market signals at the appropriate resolution”\n\nis much harder.\n\nBCG essentially reinforces this: it says agents only become truly company-specific when grounded in structured business understanding, and identifies the brand-intelligence/context layer as part of the operating blueprint. citeturn846322view0\n\nSo I would continue treating the **Context Compiler as first-class IP**.\n\n---\n\n# The reasoning architectures also matter more now\n\nOptimizely already lets specialist agents use adjustable reasoning and defined inputs; HubSpot exposes configurable instructions, tools and knowledge; most platforms will rapidly reach parity on basic agent construction. citeturn642582search5turn566023search5\n\nTherefore our LangGraph layer becomes important if it actually captures expert decision processes.\n\nFor example:\n\n```text\nGeneric Strategist\n\nprompt:\n\"You are an expert marketing strategist.\"\n```\n\nwill not be defensible.\n\nWhereas:\n\n```text\nOur Strategist\n\nidentify strategic tension\n→ generate competing hypotheses\n→ retrieve evidence\n→ actively seek disconfirming evidence\n→ assess customer relevance\n→ assess differentiation\n→ test claim support\n→ critic attack\n→ uncertainty calibration\n→ investigate if needed\n→ recommendation\n```\n\ncould be.\n\nBut only if we **evaluate it**.\n\nEventually the moat becomes the accumulated knowledge of:\n\n> which reasoning procedures actually produce good marketing decisions.\n\n---\n\n# Customer intelligence should become more central\n\nThe research also made me slightly change the weighting of our product.\n\nDovetail, Sprig and Zappi show strong momentum around turning customer evidence into persistent intelligence instead of one-off research reports. citeturn693482search15turn693482search9turn693482search4\n\nMeanwhile the big marketing-agent companies overwhelmingly emphasize **execution**.\n\nThat creates an attractive opportunity to make our system unusually strong at:\n\n```text\nlisten\n→ understand\n→ synthesize\n→ reason\n→ decide\n```\n\nbefore:\n\n```text\ngenerate\n→ publish\n→ optimize\n```\n\nThat's consistent with the product direction we've already been moving toward.\n\n---\n\n# Hightouch is the competitor I would study most carefully\n\nTypeface and Adobe are visually/conceptually obvious competitors.\n\nBut strategically I think **Hightouch is the one to watch**.\n\nWhy?\n\nBecause it already connects:\n\n```text\ncustomer data\n+\nbrand context\n+\nagents\n+\ncampaign creation\n+\nexperiments\n+\ndecisioning\n+\nreal-world outcomes\n```\n\nand its AI Decisioning product closes the loop using actual behavioral outcomes. citeturn372999view6turn898752search2\n\nThat's closer to our:\n\n> intelligence → decision → action → measurement → learning\n\nloop than most brand/content competitors.\n\nIts weakness relative to our concept is that the center of gravity is **customer-level lifecycle decisioning and warehouse data**, rather than broad brand/customer/market strategy.\n\nBut that's a meaningful adjacent direction.\n\n---\n\n# Gradial is the architectural competitor I'd watch\n\nGradial's public description is almost uncannily close to parts of our technical design:\n\n```text\npeople\nagents\ntools\nbusiness context\ngovernance\nknowledge graph\nsystems of record\nwork\n```\n\nIts long-term memory is explicitly a knowledge graph used by agents. citeturn372999view4turn372999view5\n\nThe key difference is that Gradial explicitly describes itself as **execution-first**: turning briefs/direction into deployed marketing work across enterprise tools. citeturn372999view5\n\nOur opportunity is almost the inverse:\n\n> **intelligence-first.**\n\n---\n\n# Typeface is the closest conceptual brand competitor\n\nTypeface Arc Graph already talks about a dynamic brand system that:\n\n```text\nlearns\nremembers\nconnects repositories\ncontains audience data\ncontains performance insights\nevolves\nsupports agents\ngoverns content\n```\n\nThat is extremely close to the surface description of our Box. citeturn372999view2\n\nWe should therefore never pitch:\n\n> “We build a living AI memory of your brand.”\n\nTypeface can already say that.\n\nOur distinction needs to be:\n\n> **The system doesn't merely know your brand. It models the evidence, customers, market, strategy, decisions and performance relationships from which the brand should evolve.**\n\nThat's deeper.\n\n---\n\n# The feed is good UX, but it is not a moat\n\nI specifically checked this because we've put a lot of thought into it.\n\nTextQL already has a shared Feed where agents publish data insights. Sophyx has an agent activity feed/status monitor, and Flockion advertises a social feed of agent/team outputs. citeturn194857search3turn194857search8turn194857search1\n\nSo:\n\n> “AI agents post into a feed”\n\nis not unique.\n\nWhat could still be very distinctive is the **specific experience**:\n\n```text\nfeed posts = meaningful company intelligence\n\nnot raw activity\n\n+\n\neach agent has identity\n\n+\n\nmotion reflects real cognitive state\n\n+\n\npost → reasoning → evidence → raw source\n\n+\n\ninteractions feed into the decision/truth system\n```\n\nThe little guys and the quiet feed can create a highly recognizable product.\n\nThat's a **brand/adoption advantage**, not a hard technical moat.\n\nAnd that's perfectly fine.\n\n---\n\n# There is a very interesting gap in the middle of the market\n\nThis is an inference from the product positioning I reviewed.\n\nAt one extreme:\n\n```text\nAdobe\nTypeface\nSalesforce\nGradial\nHightouch\nOptimizely\nFrontify\n```\n\nare largely selling enterprise infrastructure, enterprise workflows or existing-suite extensions. citeturn372999view0turn372999view3turn325486search1turn372999view4turn372999view7turn642582search1turn770997search2\n\nAt the other:\n\n```text\nNano\nSintra\nCleo\netc.\n```\n\nsell cheap, broad “AI marketing team” propositions to founders and small businesses. citeturn514194search0turn514194search1turn514194search3\n\nThat leaves a plausible gap for:\n\n> companies that are **too sophisticated for a $50 AI marketing bot**, but **too lean or too independent to implement an Adobe/Salesforce-scale AI marketing architecture**.\n\nThat looks much closer to the kind of founder-led, AI-native company we've been discussing.\n\nI think that's a real potential wedge. memcite\n\n---\n\n# But I would tighten the ICP\n\nI would not target:\n\n> “all SMEs.”\n\nNor:\n\n> “all brands.”\n\nNor:\n\n> “everyone who does marketing.”\n\nThe ideal first customer is likely something like:\n\n```text\nalready has meaningful revenue\n+\nalready spends meaningful money on marketing\n+\nbrand matters economically\n+\nmultiple customer-information sources exist\n+\nmarketing decisions are still founder/head-of-marketing influenced\n+\nteam is small enough that more intelligence creates leverage\n+\nalready comfortable using AI\n+\ndoesn't want a giant enterprise transformation\n```\n\nThat's a **much better customer** than a five-person company looking to replace a social media freelancer.\n\nThe latter will compare us against Sintra or Nano at tens of dollars per month. citeturn514194search0turn514194search1\n\nWe don't want that comparison.\n\n---\n\n# The managed model actually looks stronger after this research\n\nBCG says the major blocker now isn't awareness of AI. It's the structural work: data foundations, operating models, brand intelligence, orchestration, governance and skills. It also notes that companies are struggling because the systems, tools and talent aren't all there yet. citeturn846322view1turn846322view3\n\nThat's exactly why:\n\n> **“We install and continuously operate your Marketing Intelligence System.”**\n\ncan be stronger initially than:\n\n> “Sign up and configure your own AI marketing platform.”\n\nA managed setup gives us permission to do the difficult initial work:\n\n```text\nconnect sources\n→ construct Box\n→ resolve contradictions\n→ configure ontology\n→ establish ICP/product structure\n→ calibrate reasoning\n→ configure agents\n→ set approvals\n→ launch\n```\n\nThe client buys the **working system**, not the software configuration exercise.\n\nThat's potentially a good business wedge while the market is immature.\n\n---\n\n# But managed service alone isn't defensibility\n\nOver time we need the service work to produce reusable IP.\n\nEvery deployment should improve:\n\n```text\nontology templates\nextraction algorithms\ncontext strategies\nreasoning graphs\nevaluation suites\nindustry patterns\ndecision models\n```\n\nEventually:\n\n```text\nClient 1 requires 100% custom work\n\nClient 10 requires 40%\n\nClient 50 requires 10–20%\n```\n\nThat's how this becomes a productized managed platform rather than an AI agency with expensive software.\n\n---\n\n# The market is attracting serious capital\n\nCompetitive pressure is likely to intensify rather than fade. Gradial raised a $65 million Series C in June 2026, while Hightouch reportedly raised another $150 million in 2026 at a $2.75 billion valuation. citeturn770997news54turn770997news57\n\nMeanwhile major incumbents are shipping quickly: Adobe added Brand Intelligence and agents this year, Optimizely is expanding Opal, HubSpot is iterating Breeze Studio, and Ahrefs has just entered always-on agentic marketing. citeturn372999view0turn642582search8turn566023search0turn566023search13\n\nSo there is a window.\n\nBut I would assume **18 months from now the generic features are commodities**.\n\n---\n\n# What I think is commodity vs proprietary\n\nBy now I would treat all of this as commodity:\n\n```text\nLLM calls\nagents\nagent personas\ntool calling\nMCP\nA2A\nvector search\nbasic knowledge graph\nbrand voice\ngeneric RAG\nchat\napproval workflows\ncontent generation\ncampaign generation\nagent orchestration\nbasic memory\n```\n\nThe market is already there. citeturn325486search1turn770997search1turn372999view2turn372999view4turn642582search1\n\nOur potential proprietary layer is:\n\n```text\nMARKETING ONTOLOGY\n\n+\n\nEPISTEMIC / TRUTH MODEL\n\n+\n\nDIMENSIONAL PROGRESSIVE\nKNOWLEDGE ARCHITECTURE\n\n+\n\nCONTEXT COMPILER\n\n+\n\nSPECIALIZED MARKETING\nREASONING ALGORITHMS\n\n+\n\nDECISION / LEARNING MODEL\n\n+\n\nACCUMULATED EVALUATION DATA\n```\n\nThat is where I would put disproportionate engineering effort.\n\n---\n\n# I would also change the positioning language\n\nI would use **“Marketing OS” internally**, because it describes the architecture.\n\nI would not lead with it externally.\n\nThe market is already full of products literally calling themselves Marketing Operating Systems. citeturn514194search0turn514194search2turn514194search3\n\nI would move closer to something like:\n\n> **A living marketing intelligence system for AI-native companies.**\n\nor:\n\n> **Turn everything your company knows about customers, brand, market and performance into better marketing decisions.**\n\nor even:\n\n> **Your company's marketing intelligence layer.**\n\nThe agents become the experience.\n\nThey don't have to be the category.\n\n---\n\n# And I would make “decision” the center of the product\n\nThis is probably my strongest strategic recommendation.\n\nDo not make the primary loop:\n\n```text\nbrief\n→ content\n→ publish\n```\n\nAdobe, Jasper, Typeface, Gradial, Salesforce and dozens of smaller vendors are attacking that hard. citeturn372999view0turn770997search3turn372999view3turn372999view5turn325486search1\n\nMake it:\n\n```text\nSIGNAL\n   ↓\nUNDERSTANDING\n   ↓\nHYPOTHESIS\n   ↓\nEVIDENCE\n   ↓\nDECISION\n   ↓\nACTION\n   ↓\nOUTCOME\n   ↓\nLEARNING\n```\n\nThen content is merely one possible action.\n\nCampaign creation is one possible action.\n\nPositioning change is another.\n\nAudience shift is another.\n\nProduct messaging is another.\n\nLifecycle experiment is another.\n\nThat's a much higher-value system.\n\n---\n\n# My recommended go-to-market wedge\n\nIf I were reducing the whole vision to a first product, I would not launch seven autonomous agents.\n\nI would launch one complete intelligence loop:\n\n```text\nCUSTOMER + MARKET INTELLIGENCE\n\n           ↓\n\n       STRATEGIST\n\n           ↓\n\nevidence-backed recommendation\n\n           ↓\n\n       human decision\n\n           ↓\n\n        experiment\n\n           ↓\n\n          result\n\n           ↓\n\n         learning\n```\n\nResearcher + Strategist + Brand Guardian are enough initially.\n\nThat gets us directly to the thing the large platforms are less focused on:\n\n> **high-quality strategic decision support grounded in the company's own evolving reality.**\n\nThen Storyteller, Creative, Growth execution, content and autonomous campaign operations can expand outward.\n\n---\n\n# What could kill the idea?\n\nThere are three serious risks.\n\nThe first is **category collapse**. If frontier models become so good that a well-connected general-purpose agent can infer most of the necessary structure dynamically, some of our explicit ontology/context machinery becomes less valuable. My view is that provenance, governance, temporal truth and company-specific decision history will still matter, but we should continuously test whether complexity is earning its keep.\n\nThe second is **incumbent bundling**. Adobe, Salesforce, HubSpot, Typeface, Optimizely and Hightouch can bundle agents/context into products customers already pay for. citeturn372999view0turn325486search1turn566023search9turn372999view3turn642582search1turn372999view7 We need to be materially better at intelligence, not 15% nicer.\n\nThe third is **failure to prove economic value**. “Better strategic thinking” is harder to measure than “we produced 400 ads.” The product therefore needs a strong decision ledger connecting recommendations → actions → experiments → business outcomes.\n\nThat should be designed into the system from the beginning.\n\n---\n\n# What I would do now\n\n1. **Stop treating “AI marketing team” as the differentiation.** Keep the characters as UX, but position around trusted marketing intelligence and decisions.\n\n2. **Make the Box deeper, not broader.** Prioritize evidence/provenance, truth states, temporal history, dimensional abstraction and decision history over adding more raw integrations.\n\n3. **Build the Context Compiler and Researcher/Strategist reasoning before autonomous execution.** Those are more likely to differentiate than another content agent.\n\n4. **Choose one narrow initial ICP and one repeatable high-value decision loop.** I would strongly test founder-led B2B SaaS/technology companies against digitally native consumer brands before committing, because their data structures and buying reasons differ substantially.\n\n5. **Sell it as a managed intelligence system first.** The installation/service layer solves the very implementation gap the CMO research is identifying. citeturn846322view1\n\n6. **Instrument every recommendation from day one.** Evidence used, context compiled, reasoning version, human decision, action taken and eventual outcome should all become evaluation data.\n\n7. **Assume generic features will become free.** Every roadmap item should pass the test: “If Adobe/HubSpot/OpenAI ships this next quarter, does it still matter that we built ours?” If not, use infrastructure instead.\n\n---\n\n## Final judgment\n\nSix months ago I might have said:\n\n> “Interesting concept; uncertain whether the market really wants an AI marketing operating layer.”\n\nAfter researching the 2026 market, I don't think that question is uncertain anymore.\n\n**The market clearly wants the layer.** BCG is essentially describing it; Adobe, Salesforce, Typeface, Gradial, Hightouch, Jasper and Optimizely are building pieces or versions of it. citeturn846322view0turn372999view0turn325486search1turn372999view2turn372999view4turn372999view7turn770997search1turn642582search1\n\nThe question is now:\n\n> **Can we build a version whose intelligence is meaningfully better for a specific customer than the increasingly commoditized alternatives?**\n\nI think **yes**, but only if we commit to the deeper thesis:\n\n> **not an AI marketing workforce with a memory layer, but an evidence-grounded marketing intelligence and decision system that happens to express itself through a team of agents.**\n\nThat distinction is now the whole strategy.\n\nnavlistRecent moves in agentic marketingturn770997news54,turn770997news57,turn770997news51,turn604712news49\n\nI can also monitor this market weekly—especially Adobe, Typeface, Gradial, Hightouch, Jasper, HubSpot and new “Marketing OS” startups—and alert you when something materially changes our differentiation.",
